story: Tommy was terrible at sawing wood. Every time he tried to make something with saw, it never looked quite right. He wanted to improve his sawing skills. So he asked Papa to help. Papa showed Tommy how to carefully hold the saw and make the right shapes. Tommy practiced every day, and soon he was sawing much better. Tommy was so proud of himself for improving. He started to make lots of different things with his saw. He made wooden dolls and toys. He made little tables and chairs. All his friends and family said how much better his sawing had become. When Tommy saw what he had created with his saw, he knew that he had improved a lot. It made him feel really happy. He knew he had worked really hard and now everything he made with his saw looked great!

"What are you doing grandma?" asked Charles. "I'm adding yarn" said grandma. "Wow! What a lot of yarn!" said Charles. He watched as grandma wound the high yarn around her fingers and added more. "Why are you making yarn?" asked Charles. "I'm making a special scarf for your mom's birthday," said grandma. Charles smiled. "Can I help you add the yarn?" he asked. Grandma smiled and gave Charles some yarn to add. They spent the rest of the afternoon adding the yarn together. They laughed and sang as they worked. At the end of the day, the scarf was finished. It was a long, high scarf, full of many colors. Charles was so proud of the finished scarf. "That looks wonderful" said Charles. Grandma smiled. "It sure does," she said. "It was so nice to have your help in adding the yarn. You did a great job."

Yesterday, two adventurous friends pretended they were explorers and sailed to an imaginary far away island. As they sailed the sparkling sea and looked out to the horizon, they made up stories and dreamed of the things they would find. When they finally arrived, they imagined beautiful tropical plants and wild animals. Swimming in the blue ocean, they pretended they were magical creatures that could breathe under water like a fish. As the day ended, they climbed back into their boat and waved goodbye, happy to have had an adventurous day.

Tommy stopped and noticed something in the grass. It was a bright, golden thread. It was coming out of the ground! Tommy got down and grabbed the thread. He asked his mother, "What is this?" His Mom smiled and said, "It's a stitch. Someone must have dropped it here." Tommy looked around the field and saw more threads. He said, "Let's follow the threads! Maybe it'll lead us to whoever is missing them!" His Mom chuckled and said, "That's a great idea Tommy! Let's go!" Tommy smiled and together they followed the golden threads. Soon they saw a big, open door leading to an old abandoned house. Tommy tugged on his Mom's shirt and said, "Maybe the stitches are from this house!" His Mom smiled and said, "Let's go and check it out!" They opened the door and stepped into the house. There were lots of stitches everywhere! Tommy started to collect them all. His Mom smiled and said, "Let's take the stitches home and find their owner!

She then asked, "Mommy, can I use your microphone?" "That's a good idea," mom said. The girl grabbed the microphone and pretended to be a singer. She sang her favorite song at the top of her lungs. Mom said, "You are so interesting and creative. I'm so proud of you!" The girl smiled and thanked mom. She then put the microphone away, and the two hugged.

Yesterday, Maria's Mommy gave her a special box. Inside the box was a messy surprise. Maria pulled it out and ripped the paper. She was very happy to find a puppy! Maria hugged the puppy and the puppy licked her face. Maria giggled with joy. Maria cuddled the puppy all day. They played tag and chased each other around the yard. When it was time for bed, Maria put the puppy in its bed. They said goodnight and Maria went to hers. This morning, Maria ran to the puppy and they played again. But the puppy got so excited that he tore all the paper off the box! It was very messy, but Maria still loved her puppy. She said, ''It's okay. We just have to play cleaner games.'' The end.

Suddenly, Jenny found a loud buzzer. She picked it up and quickly put it in the place of the knot. Mommy shook her head, but said nothing. Jenny smiled as the buzzer made a loud noise. But then, it wouldn't stop! Mommy shouted, "What did you do?" Unfortunately, the buzzer just kept getting louder and louder. Eventually, Mommy had to take it away and put the knot back in its place. And Jenny learned her lesson

Young Jenny and her adorable bear were walking in the park. Suddenly the bear sneezed. Jenny smiled and hugged him tightly. Then she noticed something was wrong. The bear started to get smaller and smaller! Soon he was so small that he disappeared! Jenny was very sad and couldn't understand what had happened. Her bear had gone forever! Jenny cried and hugged the air and said goodbye to her lost bear. The end.

"Are you ready to go to the park?" Mommy asked. "No," said little John. He was playing with his yellow trucks on the rug. "We need to leave now," said Mommy. John shook his head. He didn't want to go. Mommy sighed. "John, if we delay any more, it will be morning." Little John looked out the window at the bright yellow sunshine. He smiled and said, "Okay, Mommy. Let's go!"

Finally, Wendy stopped running. She was sad and a bit out of breath so she sat down to rest. As she sat there, she closed her eyes and imagined what could have made the fairy so upset. She imagined that maybe the fairy had lost her way and needed help to find her home. With a renewed sense of hope, Wendy jumped up and started to search for the fairy. She called out to her but the fairy was nowhere to be seen. Suddenly, in the distance, Wendy saw a shimmering light. She knew it was the fairy flying away and that the fairy had now found her way home. Wendy smiled with relief.

"Ready, set, go!" shouted Molly as she climbed the ladder to the top of the slide. She excitedly slid down the slide, giggling along the way. When she reached the bottom, she looked across the park. The sun was setting, painting the sky pink and orange. Molly spotted a curious machine near the swing set. She approached it and saw it said "mixer". Molly peered into the bowl and saw many colorful objects. She reached inside and began to play with them. Suddenly, a voice behind her said, "Careful there, Molly. That mixer can be very clumsy." Molly spun around and saw her Nana standing there. Molly smiled, grabbed a handful of the colorful objects, and scrambled back up the ladder to the top of the slide. "Ready, set, go!" shouted Molly again as she slid back down the slide for the second time.

Zoe was a very sleepy girl. She put on her blouse, but it was a bit too big. Her mum smiled at her, because she knew how much Zoe liked big things. 'Let's go outside and play,' her mum said. Zoe nodded and followed her mum outside. Together they stood in the middle of the garden and bowed down. Zoe's mum started counting: 'One, two, three, bow!' and Zoe started to laugh. She felt happy and stretched her arms as far as she could. A few minutes later, Zoe was feeling very sleepy. She could hardly keep her eyes open. 'Let's go inside, Zoe. It's time for bed,' her mum said, and Zoe nodded. 'Goodnight,' her mum said as she hugged Zoe tight. Zoe smiled and said 'Night night!' before drifting off to sleep.

Tommy was walking in the park with his mommy. He was holding her hand and they were having a nice time. Suddenly, his mommy said, "We need to go home now." Tommy was not happy. He wanted to stay and play. He said, "No! I'm not tired." His mommy said, "But it is getting dark. We should go home before it gets too late." Tommy's mommy gave him a snack to make him happy. He likes snacks! But, it didn't work. He was still unhappy. He said, "I don't want to go home! Please don't make me!" His mommy said, "We have to go, Tommy. You are very tired and need to go home now." So, Tommy and his mommy had to go home. Tommy was still sad, but he was very tired, so he agreed to go home. He held his mommy's hand tightly and they went home. Tommy was happy to be home and remembered to eat his snack!

"Mama, can I ride my bike?" Benny asked. Mama nodded and said, "Yes, Benny. But be careful!" Benny chuckled and grabbed his bike. He took a deep breath and started riding. All around him, he noticed clear and fluffy wool coming down from the sky. He smiled and kept on going. Before long, Benny was far away from home and he was getting tired. He stopped by a tree and looked up. The wool had turned darker and darker. He realized it was getting late. He knew he had to go home. He hopped back on his bike and rode hard. But he was too late. The wool fell and suddenly, it was raining hard. He tried to go back, but Benny got lost and he couldn't find his way home. He cried out for help, but no one was around. Finally, Benny went to sleep under the tree. He was cold and scared. The wool stayed and stayed, and Benny stayed too, until the morning.

Zoe was playing in the park. She was so excited! She ran to the big swings and saw that one of them was gray. Zoe knew she wanted to swing on that one. She asked her mom, "Can I swing on that one?" Her mom smiled and said, "Of course, Zoe. Let's go!" Zoe and her mom walked to the gray swing. Zoe's mom helped Zoe onto the wide seat. Zoe was so happy! She tilted her head back and laughed. "Mommy, this is fun!" she said, as she swung back and forth. Her mom replied, "Yes, it sure is. Have a great time, Zoe!" Zoe smiled as she swung higher and higher. She laughed and closed her eyes. Zoe had the best time!

"Look, Mary!" said Daddy. Mary looked out of the car window and saw a pink road up ahead. "What's down the pink road, Daddy?" she asked. "Let's go and see," he said. So they set off down the pink road. As they drove, they saw lots of different things. Colorful houses, tall trees, a big lake. They even saw a farmer with a big, red tractor. Then, they came to the end of the road. There was a park, with a swing, a slide and lots of things to play with. There was even an ice cream truck. Mary was so excited, she started running around. She wanted to play with everything at once. Then, Daddy said, "Let's complete the road". Mary stopped, wondering what this meant. Daddy said, "Let's complete the road by taking a ride on the ice cream truck". So together, Daddy and Mary hopped on the ice cream truck, and off they went, completing their pink road adventure.

Tommy was restless. He did not want to sit still and eat his potato. He wanted to ride his bike outside with his friends. He pushed his plate away and said, "No potato, Mommy. I want to ride!" Mommy was not happy. She said, "Tommy, you have to eat your potato. It is good for you. You can ride your bike later, after you finish your dinner." Tommy shook his head. He did not like potato. He thought it was yucky and boring. He said, "No, Mommy. Potato is bad. I want to ride now!" Mommy sighed. She knew Tommy loved his bike, but he also needed to eat healthy food. She had an idea. She said, "Tommy, how about this? If you eat half of your potato, I will let you ride your bike for ten minutes. But then you have to come back and eat the other half. Deal?" Tommy thought about it. He really wanted to ride his bike, but he also did not want to eat his potato. He looked at his plate. He saw that his potato was not very big. He decided to try Mommy's idea. He said, "Okay, Mommy. Deal. I will eat half of my potato, and then I will ride." Mommy smiled. She was glad Tommy agreed. She cut his potato in half and gave him a fork. She said, "Good boy, Tommy. Eat your potato, and then you can ride. But remember, only for ten minutes." Tommy nodded. He took a bite of his potato. He did not like it, but he swallowed it. He took another bite, and another, until he ate half of his potato. He put down his fork and said, "Done, Mommy. I ate half of my potato. Can I ride now?" Mommy checked his plate. She saw that he ate half of his potato. She said, "Yes, Tommy. You can ride now. But don't forget to come back and eat the other half. I will be waiting for you." Tommy jumped off his chair and ran to his bike. He put on his helmet and said, "Thank you, Mommy. I will be back soon. Bye!" Mommy watched him ride away. She hoped he would have fun, but also remember his promise. She said, "Bye, Tommy. Be careful and have fun. I love you."

"Look, kids!" said Mum. Peter and his little brother, Ben, looked outside the window. They noticed a large tank in the garden. Mum opened the door and they stepped outside. The tank was very shiny and huge! Peter and Ben ran to it and looked inside. "Look," said Peter, pointing to the water. "There are lots of colorful fish swimming in the tank." Ben smiled as he watched the fish. "Oh, wow," he said. Mum laughed. "Do you want to feed them?" The boys nodded eagerly. Mum gave them some food and they sprinkled it over the tank. The fish swam towards them and gobbled up the food. It was so much fun! Peter and Ben giggled as they watched the fish. Mum smiled, glad to see her two boys having so much fun.

Today, Tommy and his mommy went to the store. They bought lots of colorful paper, markers, balloons and glue. Tommy was so excited! At home, Tommy and his mommy began to decorate the house. They put up streamers and balloons on the walls. Tommy made a big sign with the yellow markers. Finally, when they finished, Tommy noticed that his mommy looked sad. He asked her why and she said, "I was decorating for your birthday tomorrow." Tommy was so surprised and happy! He had completely forgotten that tomorrow was his birthday. Now Tommy was filled with anticipation and excitement and his mommy smiled too. Tommy and his mommy had created the perfect decorations for his special day.

Ben and his mom were playing at the park. Ben wanted to go swimming so they went looking for a swimming pool. Luckily, they found one nearby and they got into a van to go there. When they arrived, Ben was very excited! His mom showed him how to wear his swimming vests and told him to stay safe when he was in the water. Ben was so happy when he was able to jump in the pool and start swimming. He swam and splashed around like a fish. He accidentally got a bit too close to the edge of the pool but his mom was there to help him stay safe. When Ben was tired from swimming, he and his mom changed into dry clothes and went back home in the van. It had been the best day ever!

Will was a wise boy who liked to notice things. He noticed the sun and the moon, the birds and the bugs, the flowers and the trees. He noticed when his mom was happy or sad, when his dad was busy or bored, when his sister was nice or mean. He noticed everything. One day, he noticed a big box in the living room. It was wrapped with shiny paper and had a bow on top. He wondered what was inside. He asked his mom, "What is that?" His mom smiled and said, "That is a surprise for you, Will. But you have to wait until your birthday to open it." Will nodded and said, "Okay, mom. I will wait." But he was very curious. He wanted to know what was in the box. He thought maybe it was a toy, or a book, or a puzzle. He thought about it all day and all night. The next day, he noticed that his mom and dad were busy in the kitchen. They were making a cake and blowing up balloons. He noticed that his sister was wearing a dress and had a ribbon in her hair. He noticed that his friends were coming over with gifts and cards. He realized that it was his birthday. He was very happy. He ran to the living room and saw the big box. He said, "Can I open it now, mom?" His mom said, "Yes, you can, Will. It is your special day. Go ahead and open it." Will tore off the paper and the bow and opened the box. He gasped. Inside was a puppy. It was brown and white and had floppy ears. It wagged its tail and licked Will's face. Will hugged the puppy and said, "Thank you, mom and dad. Thank you, thank you, thank you. This is the best surprise ever. I love you, puppy." His mom and dad said, "You're welcome, Will. We love you, too. Happy birthday, Will." Will was a wise boy who liked to notice things. He noticed that he had a new friend, a new family member, a new adventure. He noticed that he was very lucky. He noticed that he was very happy.

Willie was an incredible little boy who loved to explore. One day, his mom said: "Willie, I need you to stay inside the loop around the house." Willie was excited to explore the little loop and see what he could find! Unfortunately, he quickly noticed something strange. There was a big monster destroying everything! "That's incredible!" he yelled, "I have to find a way to stop it." He ran as fast as he could, and saw the monster getting bigger and bigger. He ran past the loop and started picking up rocks and throwing them at the monster. But it was too strong and it kept on destroying everything in its path. Willie had to go back inside the loop so he wouldn't get hurt. Sadly, he realized that all his efforts were in vain. The monster destroyed everything in its way and nothing could stop it.

"Come on, let's go collect the bookshelf," said Tim. Tim and his sister Sam were excited to pick up the colourful, cheerful bookshelf. When they arrived at the store, they saw it and were overjoyed. It was bigger than they had expected. They carefully put the bookshelf in their car and rushed home. When they opened the door, they saw the empty corner where the bookshelf should go. They started to unpack the pieces, and Tim said to Sam, "Let's build it!" They started to assemble the bookshelf, but suddenly, Tim's hand got stuck. The bookshelf came crashing down on him and they were so shocked. Tim was rushed to the hospital and Sam was left alone and sad. The bookshelf was ruined, and the cheerful feeling was gone.

Wendy was playing in her bedroom. Suddenly, she heard a loud noise and saw that her makeup had broken on the ground. She was so sad and frustrated because her makeup was her favorite. The noise had come from across the room. Wendy quickly ran over to the other side of the room and saw her brother had broken her toy egg. Wendy was even more angry now. "Why did you break my egg?" Wendy shouted. Her brother shrugged his shoulders and replied, "I was just playing". Wendy was so mad that her face went sour. "Mummy!" she yelled as tears began to fill her eyes. At that moment, Wendy's mum walked in the room. She saw the broken makeup, the broken egg and the two children. Quickly, she went to Wendy and gave her a big hug. "Let's try something," said Wendy's mum. "We'll clean up the mess and then make sour lemonade together". That made Wendy cheer up and the three of them got to work cleaning up the mess. Wendy was so happy that her mum helped her feel better. They all made a big pitcher of sour lemonade and Wendy drank the most of it. In the end, Wendy still missed her makeup but was glad that she had her mum and brother to help turn a sour moment into something sweet.

John took the glass and began to play with it. He threw it around and even kicked it before it smashed on the floor. His mom became very angry. She yelled at John for breaking the glass and told him that he was not allowed to do what he wanted. John screamed and cried. He was so helpless. He had made a terrible mistake and was now being punished for it."

Trixie was very proud of her work. She had designed a trophy for her brother's birthday. It was dry and golden with graceful curves. Her brother was delighted to see his own trophy. He held it carefully, and said "It's perfect, Trixie!". She was so proud and excited, she could hardly contain her joy. The trophy was a big hit with all Trixie's friends. They wanted to know who had designed it and where they could get one too. Everyone was impressed with the strong workmanship and Trixie was very proud of her design. The next day, Trixie was surprised to learn that she had won first prize in the school's design competition. She was presented with a big shiny trophy. All her friends cheered and clapped

A little girl was playing in a park. She saw a woman slide down the slide. The woman kept going up and down, up and down. The little girl thought the woman was so silly. She laughed and thought the woman was being stupid. When the woman was finished sliding, she waved at the little girl and said "hello!" The little girl smiled and waved back. She was excited to have seen the lady slide down the slide. The little girl wanted to slide down the slide too, so she asked her mom if she could try. Her mom said yes, and the little girl felt so happy. She slid down the slide and felt so brave. She even beat the woman! The little girl smiled, feeling proud of herself.

Once upon a time, there was a modern prize. It had a bright colour and shone in the sun. Everyone wanted to have it. But they couldn't figure out how to get it down. Until one day, a little girl named Anna came up with an idea. She went to a big rock nearby and she rocked it back and forth until it was able to tilt. Finally, the prize tumbled down and landed right in Anna's hands. She was so excited and happy. Everyone cheered and clapped for her. Even the rock was happy when it saw how pleased Anna was with her new prize. Anna showed her prize off to everyone in the village. Everyone was amazed by the brilliance and beauty of the modern prize. From that day forward, the little girl and her prize were the talk of the town.

Once upon a time there was a large thumb. This thumb belonged to a little boy called Tom. Tom liked to rub his thumb. He would rub it when he was happy and he would rub it when he was sad. One day, Tom was feeling particularly sad. He decided to rub his thumb to make himself feel better. As he was rubbing his thumb, he noticed something strange. His thumb was growing bigger and bigger! Tom couldn't believe it. His thumb had become very large. He looked at it in amazement and smiled. Now every time he felt down, he would just rub his thumb and it would make him feel so much better!

Young Joe was feeling an urge to remove his shirt. He watched as his older brother took off his shirt and ran around the yard. Joe wanted to join in the fun, but he knew he had to remove his shirt first. He struggled with the buttons, but eventually removed his shirt. Now Joe could enjoy running around with his brother. He felt so happy and young.

A bull was walking across the field. He was so excited to be taking a walk! As he walked, his feet made little puddles in the mud. He kicked his feet up and laughed as he went. He saw a big tree in the field and decided to take a rest. He lay down in the tall grass and felt the sunshine on his back. He closed his eyes and dozed off for awhile. Suddenly, he heard a noise and his eyes flew open. It was a different bull walking towards him! The two bulls ran up and touched noses, and then they walked together, side by side. They were so excited to be walking together! The sun was setting and they had to go home. The two bulls walked back, feeling happy and content. It had been an exciting day, and one they would never forget!

Zoe loves waffles. She likes to eat them with honey and butter. Every morning, her mom makes her a waffle for breakfast. Zoe is happy. One day, Zoe sees a new toy in the store. It is a red car that can zoom very fast. Zoe wants the car. She asks her mom, "Can I have the car, please?" Mom looks at the car. She sees a sign that says "Rare". The car is very expensive. Mom says, "No, Zoe, we cannot buy the car. It is too much money. We have to save money for other things." Zoe is sad. She really wants the car. She thinks it is the best toy ever. She starts to cry. She says, "But I want the car, mom. It can zoom so fast. It is so cool. Please, mom, please." Mom hugs Zoe. She says, "I know, Zoe, I know. But we cannot have everything we want. Sometimes we have to be happy with what we have. You have many toys at home. You have your books, your dolls, your blocks. And you have your waffles. You love waffles, right?" Zoe nods. She wipes her tears. She says, "Yes, mom, I love waffles. They are yummy. Can we go home and have a waffle?" Mom smiles. She says, "Yes, Zoe, we can. Let's go home and have a waffle. And maybe we can play with your toys. Maybe you can make your dolls zoom like the car." Zoe smiles too. She says, "Okay, mom, that sounds fun. I love you, mom." Mom says, "I love you too, Zoe. You are my rare and precious girl."

A little girl called Jane was very sad. She wanted to be at the top of her class but her marks were always low. She felt like she couldn't do better. But then one day, Jane decided to practice and improve. She worked hard every day and soon she started to understand things better and get better marks. Pretty soon her marks were higher than anyone else's. She was thrilled to see that she was now at the top! Jane was so happy that she kept on practicing and kept on improving all the time. Now she was always at the top and never sad anymore.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to draw with her crayons. One day, she found a fake crayon that her brother had left behind. It was not a real crayon, but it looked like one. Lily decided to use the fake crayon to draw a picture of a big, stretchy snake. She stretched the snake all!

Yesterday, a wealthy man went to a restaurant to eat. He looked at the menu and pointed at the most expensive dish. He was very hungry and wanted to eat as much as possible. The waiter brought a big plate of food and the wealthy man began to eat. He was so happy and ate all the food. His plate was empty in no time. The waiter was impressed. He asked the wealthy man if he wanted something else to eat. The man shook his head and smiled. He said he was very full and thanked the waiter for the delicious food. The wealthy man left the restaurant with a big smile on his face. He was very happy because he had eaten a lot of food yesterday.

A bald woman was walking through the park with a little girl. They came to a big hole. The woman picked up a shovel, and started to bury something. The little girl was curious, so she asked the woman what she was doing. "I'm burying something special," the woman said. "What is it?" asked the little girl. The woman smiled and said "A secret!" The woman kept digging the hole until she was done. Then she put something inside and covered it with dirt. She patted it down and said "There! It is all safe now." The woman and the little girl went on their way. The little girl was very curious, but she knew the woman's secret was safe and sound inside the hole.

Tommy loved to zoom around the park on his bike. He liked to go fast and feel the wind on his face. He also liked to make loud noises with his mouth, like a car or a plane. One day, he saw a big tent in the park. He was curious and wanted to see what was inside. He zoomed towards the tent, but he did not see the sign that said "Quiet please, lecture in progress". Inside the tent, a man was talking to a lot of people. He was wearing a fancy suit and a tie. He had a pointer and a screen with pictures and words. He was telling the people about something important, but Tommy did not understand. As Tommy zoomed into the tent, he made a loud noise with his mouth. "Vroom, vroom, zoom, zoom!" he shouted. The man stopped talking and looked at Tommy. The people turned their heads and stared at Tommy. Tommy felt scared and embarrassed. The spark was so happy to be with the boy that it kept on glowing and glittering, lighting up the sky around them. From that day, the boy and the spark were always together. The spark made the boy feel happy and safe, and they twirled and twisted together in the sky. It truly was a magical thing to see".

Anna and Ben are at the zoo with their mom. They see many animals, but their favorite is the panda. The panda is big and black and white. It eats bamboo and plays with a ball. "Look, mom, the panda is so cute!" Anna says. "Yes, it is, honey. Do you know where pandas live?" Mom asks. "In China!" Ben says. He knows a lot of things. "That's right, Ben. Pandas live in China, where there are mountains and forests. But there are not many pandas left in the wild. They need our help to protect them," Mom says. Anna and Ben want to help the pandas. They see a sign that says "Adopt a Panda". They ask Mom what it means. "It means that you can give some money to the zoo, and they will use it to take care of the pandas and their habitat. You can also get a picture of your panda and a certificate with its name," Mom explains. "Can we adopt a panda, Mom? Please?" Anna and Ben beg. Mom smiles. She thinks it is a good idea. She gives some money to the zoo lady, and they get a picture of a panda named Li

Yesterday was a fun day. Mommy took me to the park and I saw lots of birds singing. But one bird was special. It was deaf and couldn't hear the other birds singing. I wanted to help it, so I sang my own song. Then the deaf bird and I sang together. It was so much fun. Today, I can't see the deaf bird anymore. I miss it and I want to sing with it again. So I'm going back to the park to look for it. I'm sure I'll find my friend again soon. I hope it hears me singing and comes over to join me. I just know it will be as fun as it was yesterday!

"C'mon, Toby, let's go outside and bury the fall leaves!" Toby's mom said with a smile. Toby eagerly grabbed his little shovel and followed his mom outside. He watched as she grabbed a handful of fallen leaves from the lawn and placed them in the pile he had made. "Oh, Toby, you're so dependable!" she said, and hugged him tightly. Toby smiled, feeling very proud of himself. He then began to shovel dirt onto the leaves. When he was finished, his mom said, "Wow, Toby! That looks so nice. Good job!" Toby was very happy and smiled, knowing that he had done something good.

Yesterday, a little girl named Lily went to the park with her mommy. Lily was very happy because she loved going to the park. She played on the swings and the slide, and even made a new friend. But then, something happened that made Lily feel fearful. She heard a loud noise and didn't know what it was. She looked around and saw a big dog barking at her. Lily was scared and didn't know what to do. Just then, the dog's owner came over and revealed that the dog was friendly and just wanted to play. Lily felt relieved and happy again. She played with the dog and had lots of fun. Yesterday turned out to be a great day after all!

a flashlight! She was so excited that she ran to it. Sara picked up the flashlight and started to build it. She put in the battery and pushed the button. The light shone bright and lit up the garden. It felt so harsh at first, but Sara was happy that she had built the flashlight and could still stay outside to play. Sara kept playing until it was completely dark. She grabbed her flashlight and thanked it for lighting her way. She then went inside for dinner with a smile on her face.

Will was very excited. He was going to go to the big, enormous zoo. His parents had been talking about it for weeks and, today, they were finally going. He grabbed his red hat and ran out to the car. When they arrived, Will couldn't believe his eyes. The zoo was so enormous. Everywhere he looked, he could see big, colorful cages filled with animals. He couldn't decide where to look first. His parents gave him a map of the zoo and told him to mark all of the cells he wanted to visit. He carefully drew a little circle around all of the cells he wanted to see. Then, his parents told him it was time to start exploring. They spent the whole day at the zoo. Will marked off each cell he visited and, by the end of the day, his map was filled with little circles. It was a great day and he was very tired but happy. Will will never forget his visit to the enormous zoo.

Amy was a 3 year old girl, and she loved to play. One day, she had a new toy and was so excited to get it out of the room and start playing with it. As soon as she opened the box and took out the toy, she quickly ran outside. It was a hot summer day, and the sun was very strong. As Amy ran outside, the sun started to melt her new toy. She was very sad and she started to cry. She ran back into the room to get help from her mom. Her mom was kind and understanding. She thought of a plan to help Amy. She went to the kitchen and grabbed some ice cubes. Amy's mom put the ice cubes on the toy. In no time, the toy started to feel nice and cool. Amy was so happy to see that her new toy was normal again.

Yesterday, a little girl was walking in the park. She followed a deep path that went into the forest. Suddenly, she sneezed. She heard a noise from behind her. She slowly looked back and saw a rabbit! The rabbit hopped and jumped around her. She laughed and ran after it. She chased it through the trees and the grass. All around, she had fun with it! After a while, the rabbit hopped away and the little girl stopped to catch her breath. Then, she sneezed one more time and went back home. She was smiling and she thought of the fun she had yesterday.

"Billy was ready for the school day. He got dressed in his warm clothes and brushed his teeth so he was ready to go. When he was finished, he set his alarm. Billy said to himself, 'When I hear the alarm, I will be ready to go'. Soon enough, the alarm went off. Billy heard it and he felt ready. He ate a quick breakfast and said goodbye to his Mom. Then he was off, walking to school on his own. When he got to school, he was glad he was ready and glad he heard the alarm. He went off to join his friends and start his day!"

Zip was a lively fish. Zip lived in a lake filled with other fish. Every day Zip swam around the lake looking for food. Zip liked to swim fast and would swim circles around the other fish. One day Zip saw a bug on the edge of the lake. Zip swam towards it but his fins were too small to get there. Zip swam faster and faster but still couldn't catch the bug. Just then a big fish came along. He had a big fin and he swam very fast. He quickly caught the bug and offered it to Zip. Zip was so happy that he swam around the lake with the big fish. They had a lot of fun and Zip felt very lively.

A young girl named Sarah was lying in her bed one night. She was excited to be in her bed and ready for bedtime. Suddenly, a harmless bug appeared on her bed. Sarah was a bit scared, so she decided to get out of bed. She ran to the kitchen to tell her mom and dad about the bug. Her parents were happy to hear the news and they quickly decided to take care of the bug. They grabbed a jar and cup and used it to trap the harmless bug. After they were sure the bug was safe, they took it outside and released it back into the wild. Sarah was happy that she and her parents were able to help the harmless bug in its own home. She waved goodbye to the bug and went back to bed with a big smile on her face.

Two little children were playing in their back yard. They were running and laughing together. Suddenly, one of the children noticed a tall structure. The other child had noticed it, too. "Can we reach the top?" one of the children asked the other. The other child laughed. "No way! It's too high!" The first child then looked around, before grabbing an old ladder. "Yes we can!" the first child shouted excitedly. The two children quickly dragged the ladder over to the tall structure. But then they stopped, as they heard a loud voice. "What do you think you are doing?" their mother asked, hands on her hips. The children quickly explained that they wanted to reach the top of the tall structure. "No way," their mother said sternly. "It's dangerous. You must stay away from it." The children reluctantly agreed and quickly left the tall structure alone. They continued to play but they couldn't hide their disappointed looks.

"Mommy, can I get a tutor?" asked David. "Yes, honey, but why do you want one?" David smiled. "I want to be good at math!" So Mommy spent the day looking for a good tutor. She searched online and asked her friends. Finally, Mommy found the perfect tutor for David. David was very excited when the tutor arrived for their first lesson. He showed the tutor his math book and said, "Let's do it!" The tutor was very patient and good at explaining math to little kids. After the lesson David was so proud of himself. He thanked the tutor and hugged his mom to say thank you for finding a good tutor for him. David could not wait for the next session. He was sure that he would become a math expert with the help of his tutor.

Yesterday, Mommy and Daddy took me to a store. It was very big! We looked at lots of things. But Mommy and Daddy didn't buy me anything. They said it was too expensive. Then, we went to another store. This store was smaller, but just as exciting. I saw a toy truck I wanted and asked Mommy if I could have it. She said yes, but it looked very expensive. Mommy went up to the counter and talked to the lady at the shop. Then she came back with a smile and handed me the truck! I was so happy! Dad gave the lady some money and we went home. All day, I played with my new truck. I was so glad Mommy and Daddy bought me such a nice toy.

"Look, see it move!" shouted Lucy. Each day, Lucy and her mom watched the sun rise above the horizon. It was so beautiful. On this day, Lucy was surprised to see a laser rising up with the sun. It rose faster than anything they had seen before. How interesting! "Mom, is the laser special?" asked Lucy. "Yes, it is very special," said her mom. "It is a special laser that lights up the sky with pretty colours. So together they watched the lively laser show. Lucy clapped in excitement. She wanted the show to never end. She laughed and jumped around. But, all too soon, the sun was high in the sky and the laser was gone. But Lucy knew, that tomorrow, the laser would rise again.

once there was a dog who loved to carry things. One day, it found a yoga mat in the park and decided to carry it home. The dog was so excited and ran around, being careful not to drop the mat. When it arrived home, the yoga mat was still dry, but the dog was exhausted. That evening, the dog decided to try out the yoga. But no matter how hard it tried, it's legs were too short to reach the poses. So the dog just lay down and watched the stars instead. The next day, the dog wanted to show off its tight back flip. But the yoga mat had gotten wet in the night and now was slippery. The dog crashed down on the hard ground and got a bump on its head. The moral of this story is to not try too hard. Sometimes it's best to be content with what you can do and not do something if you can't do it perfectly.

"Stumbo!" shouted Mary as she stumbled backwards. She had been running too fast and tripped on the big, soft rug in the classroom. Her teacher smiled and said, "It's okay, Mary. Let's try again." Mary nodded, determinedly. She stepped carefully, measuring her steps to the big blackboard in the front of the classroom. She stretched out her hand. White chalk was in her fingers. "Now, Mary," said the teacher, "Show us what you did today at the park". Mary turned and ran across the room, stumbling once again but this time keeping her balance. She hopped to the wall and quickly drew a sun, a tree and a swing. The teacher nodded in approval and said, "Very nice, Mary. Now that's something to be proud of." Mary smiled, her eyes twinkled, and she nodded her head. "Stumbo," she said.

Young Rob and his mummy were out exploring in the forest. Rob was captivated by the beauty of the trees and the sunbeams peeking through the branches. They heard a rumble in the distance and both stopped in their tracks. Mummy turned to Rob and said, "It's getting closer, let's go." Rob trembled in fear and eagerly followed mummy. Then, mummy asked Rob to hide behind a nearby tree and not make a sound. Rob was scared but obeyed. Mummy closed her eyes and began to hum a song. Suddenly, a huge and brilliant beast came into view. It had a big skull and tusks which glittered in the sun. Rob was amazed, but also scared. Then, with a few powerful leaps, the beast jumped over Rob and his mummy and charged away. Rob grabbed hold of his mummy, trembling in amazement. They had just escaped a mighty creature! The forest was peaceful again.

"Look, look!" shouted Jack excitedly, pointing at the curious landscape. "What do you see my darling?" asked mummy. "It's melting!" replied Jack. Mummy and Jack then watched in awe as the landscape melted into beautiful, rainbow colours. Jack giggled and clapped his hands excitedly. "It's so pretty!" he said. Mummy smiled and said, "Yes, it is curious but so very beautiful." The two of them watched in awe for a few more moments before heading home.

True was a dog who loved his family. He liked to play with them, sleep with them, and eat with them. He was happy and good. One day, his family had to leave for a long time. They put True in a big box with some toys and food. They said, "We love you, True. We will come back soon. Be a good boy." True did not like the box. He felt sad and scared. He did not want his family to leave. True tried to be good in the box. He played with his toys and ate his food. But he missed his family a lot. He barked and cried. He wanted to see them and hug them. The box was in a place with many other boxes. Some had dogs, some had cats, some had birds. They all made a lot of noise. True did not like the noise. He felt lonely and angry. He did not want to be with them. One day, True heard a familiar voice. He looked out of the box and saw his family. They came to get him. They opened the box and hugged him. They said, "We missed you, True. We are sorry we had to leave. You are a good boy." True was so happy. He licked their faces and wagged his tail. He did not care about the box or the noise anymore. He only cared about his family. True left the place with his family. He was glad to be with them again. He never wanted to be in the box again. He thought it was a terrible place. He thought his family was the best place. He loved them and they loved him. He was happy and good.

"Look, Mummy!" shouted Jimmy as he ran towards his bedroom window. "A bird is outside in the garden!" Mummy quickly followed Jimmy. She was very alert and she could see the bird had a net in its beak. "It must have found the net in the garden and come over to explore," said Mummy. Jimmy watched as the bird landed in the garden and started to shake the net. He could see it was full of bugs and worms. "Can we feed the bird?" Jimmy asked excitedly. Mummy smiled and carefully handed Jimmy some breadcrumbs. Jimmy opened his window and sprinkled the breadcrumbs around the net. Just then, the bird flew over to the net and shook it before gathering the crumbs in its beak and taking off into the sky. "Goodbye, little bird!" shouted Jimmy. Mummy smiled. "That was so kind of you to feed the bird, Jimmy. Well done!"

Tyler was a little boy who had a bright sparkle in his eyes. He was always excited to explore outside, but today he was even more excited than usual. Tyler was going to the beach with his mom. Tyler tugged on his mom's hand as they approached the beach. His mom chatted to him with a smile, "Let's find the perfect spot, Tyler! Wouldn't that be fun?" Tyler grinned and nodded his head. The sand was soft and warm beneath his toes, and the bright sun made him squint. Tyler raced ahead of his mom and could see something far away in the blue waves. It was silver and shiny, like a giant iron. Tyler couldn't believe his eyes! He raced towards it, but as he got closer, Tyler felt his heart start to tremble. He realized it wasn't an iron at all, it was a giant fish! Tyler gasped with delight and his mom laughed. This was going to be the best day ever!

"Come on, let's go!" shouted the little boy. He had found a big branch in the park and was very excited about it. The mother smiled and said "Ok, let's see what you have." They both went to the branch and examined it. The little boy was very clumsy with it and nearly dropped it several times. Mother said "Be careful, it's very heavy!" The little boy replied, "But I need it for my games!" Mother smiled and said, "Ok, let's take it home then." And so they did. The little boy was so excited to play with his new branch, and the mother was glad to see him so happy.

once upon a time there was a poor family who did not have much. One day the family heard a noise coming from the chamber. When they opened the door they found a thief! The thief had stolen their precious jewels and had hidden them in the chamber. The family was so sad and angry. So, the dad ran after the thief and caught him. He made the thief return all the precious jewels to the family. The family was so happy that the thief was caught and their precious jewels were safe. They thanked the dad for being brave and catching the thief who had tried to steal from them. The End.

Kate smiled and shot her tiny toy gun up into the sky, trying to hit a shooting star. They both laughed, and soon, it was time for bed. The next morning, Kate went outside to explore again. This time, she went up to the roof and tried to find shooting stars by using only her eyes. She was happy to have so much to explore and discover, even at such a small age.

Yesterday, a little birdie was flying in the sky. The sun was shining bright and the sky was blue. Suddenly, the birdie saw a harsh wind and it started to blink its eyes. The wind was so strong that it made the birdie fly away to a different place. The birdie was scared and didn't know where it was. It looked around and saw a big tree. The birdie flew to the tree and sat on a branch. It closed its eyes and rested for a while. After a few minutes, the wind stopped and the birdie opened its eyes. It felt happy to see that it was safe. The birdie flew back to its home and felt relieved. From that day on, the birdie knew that it had to be careful when the wind was harsh.

"'Look!' said Mom. She pointed up at the sky. Molly blinked. She saw a colorful kite flying high above her. It was a giant kite with lots of bright colors. The string was tight, stretching up to the sky. Molly was excited. She wanted to fly the kite too. 'Can we fly the kite?' she asked Mom. 'Yes, let's go to the park and give it a try!' said Mom. So they went to the park. Mom smiled as they ran to the open field. They put the kite up in the sky, and pulled the tight string. The kite flew higher and higher. Molly watched in awe. She was so happy. She laughed, clapped her hands and blinked. She couldn't believe it! Mom and Molly held onto the string and watched the kite fly away. 'Look how high it is!' said Mom. 'Yes,' said Molly, 'I can still see it!' It was a wonderful day. The sun was shining and the sky was bright blue. Molly and Mom flew the kite all afternoon, and finally it was time to go home. Molly hugged the kite string tight, and promised to fly it again soon. She knew that it would be the best day ever."

William was a brave little boy who loved being outdoors. One day he decided to go for a walk but suddenly stopped when he heard a strange noise. It was like a deep rumble and it made William tremble. Then around the corner he saw something he had never seen before. It was lots of cars and trucks all driving together. William had never seen traffic before and he thought it was unique. He wanted to watch the cars but he was a little scared because of the noise they made. But he was brave and stayed to watch until the traffic was gone. He was so excited to discover something new and his courage made him proud.

"Look, Mommy!" said the little girl as she saw a dove in the park. Her mother smiled and said, "That's a beautiful bird, isn't it?" They watched the dove for a while, until the girl said, "I want to put it in my pocket." Mommy laughed and said, "No, that's not a good idea. It might be frightened." The little girl looked sad. "What can I do then?" she asked. "Well, we can make a little house for it, like a nest." Mommy said. She helped the girl find some leaves and twigs, and together they put them in a pile in the grass. The dove flew down and looked at the pile. It hopped in and settled down, chirping happily. The little girl smiled. "I think he likes it!" she said. Mommy smiled too, and said, "Yes, it looks like our dove found a safe place to stay."

Zero was a rare animal that lived in the woods. All the other animals were scared of him because he looked different. One day, Zero decided to start a journey to find some friends. He crossed rivers and valleys and, after some time, he met a dog. The dog looked friendly, so Zero started to talk to him. The dog was surprised to see Zero and told him that he had never seen an animal like him before. The two animals soon became friends, and every day they started to play together. They told jokes, sang songs and even had a few races. They became the best of friends. Zero was so happy to finally have a friend. He realized that even though he was different, he could still find someone who liked him for who he was. The two friends had wonderful times together and Zero was so busy with his new friend that he forgot all about his journey.

"Mommy, what did you pour yesterday?" asked little Ally. "I poured some hot chocolate," Mommy said. "It looks so yummy!" Ally said, her eyes widening. "It sure does," Mommy said. "But it was icy yesterday, so it was too cold to drink. But today it's nice and hot and ready for you to enjoy." Ally's smile grew. "Yay!" "Go ahead, try some," Mommy said. Ally eagerly grabbed the cup and took a big sip. It was sweet, chocolaty and warm, and the perfect treat for a cold day. "Mmmm!" Ally said, smiling up at Mommy. "Thank you, Mommy!" Mommy smiled back. "You're welcome, sweetheart."

While the sun was shining, happy bird flew around in the sky. Little girl was playing with her toy car in the park. She sang to herself as she drove around. Suddenly, the clouds rolled in and rain began to fall. Little girl ran home to stay dry. She opened the door and saw her mom standing with a big, white, fan. The fan was spinning around in circles and making a lot of noise. Little girl smiled, for she knew the fan would keep her warm and dry. A few days later, the sun came out once more. Little girl took her fan outside to enjoy the day. Soon, the fan was spinning with the breeze. Little girl pulled out her toy car and drove around the fan like it was a race track. Little girl laughed as the fan made her car go quicker and quicker. Little girl was now an independent and happy girl. She was able to do things all on her own. She was no longer scared of the rain, for she and her fan had made it Spring again!

Anna and Ben are friends. They like to play at the park. They like to slide, swing and run. But they also like to win. They are competitive. One day, they see a big water fountain at the park. It has many colors and shapes. It looks fun. They want to play with the water. "Let's see who can touch the water first!" Anna says. "OK, I will beat you!" Ben says. They run to the fountain. They try to catch the water. But the water is fast and high. It splashes them. They get wet and cold. "Ha ha, I touched the water first!" Anna says. "No, I did!" Ben says. They argue. They are not happy. They are not friends. A lady sees them. She is nice. She has a towel. She gives them the towel. "Here, dry yourselves. You are both brave and fast. You both touched the water. You don't have to fight. You can share and play together." She says. Anna and Ben look at each other. They feel sorry. They say sorry. "Thank you, lady. You are right. We can share and play together. We are friends." They say. They smile. They hug. They use the towel. They go back to the fountain. They play with the water. They have fun. They are happy. They are friends.

Tommy was in his room playing with his toys when he heard something outside. It sounded like a loud rumble. He knew it must be from the traffic, so he got up to look. He saw the cars driving quickly. They shook the ground as they passed. Tommy felt his body tremble a little too. He looked up at the sky and noticed how clear it was. Tommy saw birds flying around the sky and was amazed at how graceful they looked. Then Tommy heard the rumble of the traffic again. He couldn't help but tremble. He ran to his window, amazed at how fast the cars were going. Tommy was so fascinated by the traffic that he decided to spend the rest of the day looking at it. He watched the cars go by, feeling his body tremble each time. The sky above him was clear, the sun shining brightly. Tommy was mesmerized by the beauty of the traffic outside his window.

"Look Mommy, what can I eat?" asked Clara. She was a cute little three year old girl. "Let's see," said Mommy. "We have iron here." Clara was surprised. "Can I eat the iron?" Mommy laughed. "No, iron isn't food. Iron is used to make things like clothes." "Oh," said Clara. She thought for a moment, then asked, "But can I eat something cute?" Mommy smiled. She picked up a cookie and gave it to Clara. "Here, this is cute and delicious. You can eat it." Clara smiled and took the cookie. She bit into it and said, "Yum! I love eating this cute cookie!"

Yesterday, Mommy and Daddy took Jimmy to the park. Jimmy loved playing on the swings. He was very gentle, as Mommy and Daddy asked. They watched as he swung high into the sky. For the rest of the day, Jimmy behaved himself. He smiled when he saw Mommy and Daddy watching, and ran over to them when they called his name. When they had finished at the park, they went to the store. Here, Jimmy behaved too. He didn't run around or make too much noise. He was gentle and it made Mommy and Daddy very proud. At the end of the day, Jimmy was tired. But he was happy he had behaved himself yesterday.

Anna and Ben are friends. They like to play together. Today is Anna's birthday. She has a party at her house. She is very happy. Anna wears a pink dress and a crown. She looks like a princess. Ben wears a blue shirt and a hat. He looks like a pirate. They go to the party room. There are balloons, cake, and toys. They see many other kids. They say hello. "Anna, you are so pretty!" says Ben. "I like your dress and your crown." "Thank you, Ben!" says Anna. "I like your shirt and your hat. Do you want to play with me?" "Yes, I do!" says Ben. "What do you want to play?" "Let's play with the dolls!" says Anna. "They are my favorite toys. I have many dolls. You can choose one." "OK, let's go!" says Ben. They run to the doll corner. There are many dolls. Anna picks a big doll with long hair. Ben picks a small doll with a dress. They sit on the floor and play with the dolls. They pretend the dolls are their friends. They talk and laugh. They have fun. But then, something bad happens. A big boy comes to the doll corner. He is mean. He does not like dolls. He wants to play with cars. He sees Anna and Ben. He gets angry. "Hey, you two!" he says. "What are you doing? Dolls are for girls. You are silly. Give me those dolls. I want to throw them away." He grabs the dolls from Anna and Ben. He pulls and tears. He breaks the dolls. He throws them in the trash. Anna and Ben are shocked. They cry. "Stop it! Stop it!" they say. "Those are our dolls. You are bad. You are mean. Go away!" But the big boy does not listen. He laughs. He is not sorry. He runs away. He looks for other toys to break. Anna and Ben are very sad. They hug each other. They look at the broken dolls. They do not want to play anymore. They do not like the party. They want to go home. The end.

Alex had a cool pastel shirt. He was so proud of it because it was the first shirt he ever picked out himself. Even though it was pastel and cool, it made Alex just a bit embarrassed. He loved the shirt; the pastel colors of pink and blue looked perfect together. His friends thought it was cool too. But when it was time for school, Alex got a bit scared. He was worried that his friends would make fun of his shirt. He was so embarrassed he began to cry. But when Alex got to school, his friends did not laugh at his shirt. Instead, they said it was cool and admired the pastel colors in it. Alex felt so happy. He was no longer embarrassed and was so glad of his cool pastel shirt.

old, Mark, what happened. He looked scared and said, "I struck the event". Mama and Papa were disappointed and said, "That's not okay, Mark. You should be sorry." Mark hung his head. He had heard them say "sorry" before and knew it was not a good thing. He said he was sorry and his face was sad. Mama and Papa gave him a hug and said, "It's okay, Mark. We forgive you. Just make sure not to do it again." Mark smiled and said, "I won't, Mama and Papa!" He knew he had learned his lesson and was very happy that he was forgiven.

"What's that?" asked three year old Sarah as she pointed to a big building in the distance. "That's the shelter," her mom said. "It's a place where people who need it can find a safe place to stay." "What do they do there?" Sarah asked. "Well," her mom said, "they have someone who takes care of them, who makes sure everyone is safe and fed and taken care of." Sarah wanted to go and see it. So, her mom took her for a walk around the shelter. Sarah was careful as she walked, looking around at all the people staying there. Some people were playing, some were talking and some were just peacefully sitting outside. Sarah was so impressed. She said, "I'm glad we have this shelter. Everyone looks so happy here."

Tommy was so excited to have a new toy. His mom gave him a bright yellow ball, but it was not like any of his other balls. It had a long string attached to it. Tommy held the string in his little hands and he felt something funny. He knew the string was soft and he liked rubbing it between his fingers. He was puzzled why this ball was so different from all the other ones. His mom said every time he moved the string, the ball would move too. Tommy was amazed. He pulled and tugged on the string and was so happy when the ball moved around. Maybe if he pulled the string hard enough, he could make the ball fly! Tommy tried over and over again, but the ball only moved a little bit. Tommy was disappointed his ball would not fly, but he thought it was still very fun to play. Then one day he saw a kite fly by and he realized he could use his string to make the ball fly just like the kite. He held onto the string and he felt something magical. With a flick of his wrist, the ball soared up and across the sky. Tommy was so proud and happy. By using the soft string, he had made the ball fly!

"I'm so nervous," said Jack as he stepped into the room. It was filled with mirrors that spun in all directions. One small grey mirror caught his eye and he stepped closer to take a better look. Just then, a loud voice said, "Spin the mirror, Jack!" Jack jumped back in surprise. "Who said that?" he asked nervously. Then a small wink of light came from the mirror. Jack stepped closer and saw a magical sparkle in the glass. "It's the Mirror Fairy," he said in amazement. The Fairy said, "Spin my mirror and make a wish, Jack. I can make your wish come true!" Jack was so excited! He spun the mirror round and round and made a wish. Then the Mirror Fairy said, "Your wish has come true!" Jack smiled and thanked the Mirror Fairy. Then he stepped out of the room, feeling so much more confident and happy.

Yesterday was terrible for little Tommy. He was so sad and feeling down. He thought he'd open the door and go outside and play. But as he opened the door, he saw that it was raining. The rain was coming down hard and he couldn't go outside. He started to cry. But then he heard a noise, a noise he hadn't heard before. He looked up and saw a rainbow touching the ground and he smiled. He looked up into the sky and saw all the bright colors of the rainbow and felt so happy, like yesterday never happened.

"Mommy, let's go to the store!" said the little flying saucer. Mommy smiled and said, "all right, let's go to the store". When they arrived, the store was full of things. The little flying saucer saw a big table with lots of things on it. He wanted to touch them all, but Mommy said no. "No, don't touch the table," said Mommy. The little flying saucer was disappointed, but then he noticed that the floor around the table was wet. "What's that wet stuff?" he asked. Mommy said, "That's water. Someone spilled it on the floor. That's why I asked you not to touch the table." The little flying saucer understood, and he was careful not to make a mess. The moral of the story is that it's important to pay attention to our surroundings and respect other people's things.

"Let's go for a walk!" said Mommy. Daddy, Mommy and baby all went for a walk together. They walked up the big hill to see the view. "Look, there is a large tree at the top of the hill!" said Mommy. Daddy, Mommy and baby smiled. Suddenly, a loud voice shouted out. "Look! It is a race to the top of the hill. Who will win?" Mommy, Daddy and Baby all laughed. "Let's race each other to the top of the hill!" said Daddy. Mommy, Daddy and Baby all ran as fast as they could. Mommy was the first to the top of the hill. She won the race. She was so happy. "We won because we had so much fun!" they said.

once upon a time there was a generous pick. He yawned because he was so tired from carrying so much wood. He needed to take a rest. He found a nice spot underneath a tree. He lay there and felt the cool breeze and let out a big yawn. The pick was so comfortable that he couldn't help but drift off to sleep. He stayed there for a nice, long nap. After some time had passed he woke up refreshed. His stomach was rumbling so he set off to find something to eat. On his journey he came across some lovely pink apples. He was delighted and so hungry that he nabbed one and took a big juicy bite. "Yummm," he said with a yawn of satisfaction. He was so thankful for the generous apple tree. He decided that he wanted to show his appreciation so he began to pick all the apples from the tree. Then he carefully placed them aside for others to enjoy. The pick was so happy that he could share the delicious bounty with others. He finished his collection of apples and returned to his restful spot beneath the tree with a smile on his face. He lay back down and let out a satisfied yawn.

"Come on!" shouted Grandad as he mounted the bicycle. Grandad was an elderly man, but he was strong. Molly watched him excitedly. She was only three years old, but she knew it was time for a bicycle ride. Grandad and Molly started to pedal together. It was a sunny day and they were soon high in the sky. Molly shouted with glee and her grandfather laughed. Suddenly Molly saw some people coming down the path. She knew they weren't friendly and she knew they were dangerous. "Grandad, let's escape!" she shouted. Grandad pedalled faster and faster until they were out of sight. Molly hugged Grandad tightly, "Thanks Grandad, that was great!" she shouted. Grandad smiled. He was glad he had been able to help his little Molly escape.

Tommy was miserable. He wanted to go outside and play, but it was raining. He looked out the window and saw big puddles on the street. He wished he had his boots and raincoat, but they were at Grandma's house. He asked his mom if he could go outside anyway, but she said no. She said he would get wet and cold and sick. She said he had to stay inside and play with his toys. Tommy did not want to play with his toys. He wanted to splash in the puddles. He waited until his mom was busy in the kitchen. Then he sneaked out the door. He ran to the street and saw a huge puddle. He smiled and stepped in it. He felt the water splash on his legs and feet. He laughed and jumped in the puddle. He felt happy and free. But then he heard his mom's voice. She was angry. She saw him from the window and came outside. She grabbed his hand and pulled him out of the puddle. She scolded him for being naughty and disobedient. She took him inside and dried him off. She said he had to stay in his room until dinner. She said he was in big trouble. Tommy was miserable again. He wished he had listened to his mom. He wished he had his boots and raincoat. He wished he could go back to the puddle. He cried and hugged his teddy bear. He hoped his mom would forgive him. He hoped it would stop raining soon.

"Mommy, can I have a grill?" asked the 3 year old. "No, that's too expensive," said mom. The 3 year old was sad, but then mom said, "Let's go outside and find some sticks instead. We can make our own grill from the sticks." They found some sticks and arranged them into a circle, like a grill. Suddenly, all the sticks started to fall apart. Mom said, "It's ok, we can try again." So, they started over and made a new grill, this time securing the sticks together so that they wouldn't fall apart. They gathered twigs and grass and put them inside the grill. Mom said, "Let's see if it works." She lit a match and put it on the twigs. Soon, a low flame was burning. The 3 year old was very excited and said, "We did it! We made our own grill!" Mom smiled and said, "Yes, we did."

He knew he shouldn't go too close, so he asked one of the children what it was doing there. The child said the puppy was lost, so Jack wanted to help. After a lot of searching, Jack found the puppy's dad. He was so happy to know his puppy was okay. The puppy's dad thanked Jack for finding him and gave him a big hug. Jack walked home with a big smile on his face. He knew he had done something very nice yesterday.

Her friends were amazed and asked her how she found it. Lucy smiled and said, "An old man helped me. He's a real friend!"

once upon a time, there was a furry old bear. He was feeling very tired, so he decided to take a dip in the lake. He splashed around and around in the cool water. Suddenly, he heard someone talking to him. He looked up and saw a little girl standing on the shore. The girl said, "What are you doing, furry old bear? Are you splashing in the lake?" The bear smiled and said, "Yes, I am. It's a great way to refresh myself." The little girl smiled and said, "Can I splash too?" The bear said, "Of course! Come on in and let's go for a swim." So the little girl joined the bear and they splashed and played in the water for a long time. They both had so much fun.

"Look up there, Mama!" said Emma. Mama looked up to the sky and smiled. "What do you see?" "A bird!" Emma said, admiring its graceful flight. The bird flew up the stairs of a tall building. Mama chuckled. "That bird must be having an adventure!" The next day, they were walking past the building and they heard loud, cheery singing coming from upstairs. "It's the same bird from yesterday," Emma said, smiling with admiration. Mama laughed. "It's been so fun watching its journey. Let's listen for a little bit more." The singing echoed louder and louder until, eventually, a flock of birds flew out of the building's window, taking off into the sky. Mama and Emma watched until the birds had disappeared. "It's been so amazing to watch the bird's adventure," Mama said. Emma smiled at the sky. "Yes, it has."

Mom was not happy. She took his cars and put them on the shelf. She urged Tommy to get up and follow her. She said, "You need a bath to be clean and fresh. You can play with your cars again tomorrow. Now, let's go." Tommy was sad and angry. He did not like to leave his cars. He did not like to be wet and soapy. He walked slowly behind his mom. He hoped she would change her mind. But she did not. She filled the bathtub with warm water and bubbles. She put Tommy in the water and gave him a washcloth and a rubber duck. She said, "Look, you have a duck to play with. And the bubbles are fun. You can make shapes and pop them. Try it." Tommy looked at the duck and the bubbles. He did not want to admit it, but they looked a little fun. He took the duck and squeezed it. It made a quack sound. He smiled. He dipped the washcloth in the water and made it wet. He threw it in the air and watched it fall. He laughed. Mom smiled too. She said, "See, bath time is not so bad. You can have fun and be clean at the same time. Now, let me wash your hair and then you can play some more." Tommy nodded. He let mom wash his hair and rinse it. He did not cry or fuss. He felt the water and the bubbles on his skin. He felt good. He said, "Thank you, mom. I like bath time." Mom hugged him and said, "You're welcome, Tommy. I'm proud of you. You're a good boy. Now, let's get you dry and put on your pajamas. Then we can read a story before bed." Tommy agreed. He got out of the bathtub and wrapped himself in a towel. He felt warm and cozy. He followed mom to his room. He saw his cars on the shelf. He did not miss them so much. He was ready for bed. He said, "Mom, can you read me the story about the big red car?" Mom said, "Of course, Tommy. I love that story. Let's go to your bed and I'll read it to you." They went to his bed and mom opened the book. She read the story about the big red car and its adventures. Tommy listened and imagined. He felt happy and sleepy. He closed his eyes and drifted to sleep. Mom kissed him and said, "Good night, Tommy. I love you." Tommy murmured, "I love you too, mom. Good night."

The flea held tight and drove even faster. Finally, the wind stopped and the flea was able to safely drive to its destination.

He knew that his aunt couldn't hear but he also knew she was happy and that made him feel good. He looked around at his family and they were all smiling and happy. Brian was so glad that his family was happy and he thought it was wonderful that they were able to celebrate yesterday.

"Once upon a time there was a small peanut. The peanut was frightened, so it decided to try and gain some courage. The frightened peanut decided to ask the nearby tree what it should do. The tree said 'just be brave and take this path'. So the peanut followed the tree's advice and took the path. As the peanut walked along the path it noticed a small mouse that was even more frightened then it was. The peanut shared its courage with the mouse and slowly the mouse stopped being afraid. The peanut and the mouse became friends and hugged each other. The moral of the story is that when you share courage and kindness, even the tiniest of creatures can benefit greatly. So remember to always be kind, no matter how scared you are."

Yesterday, the sky turned grey and it started to rain. All the children grabbed their umbrellas and ran outside to play. But Tom was different. He took out his camera and started taking pictures of the grey sky. He was not worried at all. Tom loved taking pictures. He smiled every time he snapped a photo. Every time the rain got heavier he took more pictures. The rain splashed on his face. He could feel how happy he was. After a while, everyone else got tired of the rain and started running home. Tom kept taking pictures until the last drop of rain had fallen. Everyone thought that he was worried about the rain but he wasn't. He was just taking pictures. He was smiling and didn't mind being the last one standing in the rain.

A family drove to the park. They found a big trunk on the ground. Mommy and Daddy thought it was strange. What could be inside? The children were excited. They wanted to open it. Daddy grabbed a big rock and used it to open the trunk. Inside it were lots of blocks. The family smiled. They could build something fun. Daddy and Mommy quickly got to work. With the blocks, they built a really big tower. It was very tall. The girl wondered what else they could do. Then, she had an idea. She took out some of the blocks and made a trunk of her own. Yesterday, a white kitten was walking down the street. Suddenly, it heard a loud noise and jumped in surprise. It quickly ran away, and did not want to stop. The kitten was trying to resist and keep running away. Soon, it came across a big playground. The kitten saw a group of children playing together, and it went over to take a closer look. Suddenly, one of the children grabbed it and tried to pick it up. The kitten resisted, and it was able to escape from the child's arms. It ran away from the playground and looked around for somewhere safe to hide. All of a sudden, the kitten saw a white rabbit who was eating some grass. The rabbit saw the kitten and ran away, so the kitten followed it. The rabbit disappeared into a hole in the ground and the kitten was so scared. It was about to run away again, but then it noticed something glimmering in the hole. The kitten reached in and found a diamond necklace! The kitten was so excited and eagerly ran home with the necklace. The kitten resisted the temptation to turn back, and yesterday it was the happiest kitten in the world.

"Good morning, everyone!" said the adorable 3 year old. He was standing in the kitchen with his mom and dad. He was so excited because he had seen something that he wanted to show them. The 3 year old was disappointed. He wanted to keep the old chair. He liked it, but he knew it was time for something new. "We'll go shopping and find a new chair for the kitchen," said his mom. The 3 year old was sad, but he knew his mom was right. So, he said goodbye to the old chair and went shopping with his parents. When they came home, the 3 year old was delighted. The new chair was even more adorable than the old one! He couldn't wait to spend his afternoons reading stories in it. The chair replaced the old chair in the kitchen and now the 3 year old was a happy child.

"I want to catch the bird, but I can't," Zero says. He meows softly. "Don't be sad, Zero. You are a good cat. You don't need to catch birds. You have me and your toys and your food. You have everything you need," Tom says. He kisses Zero on the head. Zero feels better. He purrs and licks Tom's face. He loves Tom. He thinks Tom is the best friend ever. He forgets about the bird. Yesterday, a turtle named Timmy was walking slow in the forest. All of a sudden, he saw his friend, a rabbit named Benny, run past him. Timmy wanted to play with Benny, so he started to run too. Benny was very fast, but Timmy tried his best to catch up. They ran and ran until they reached a big tree. Benny stopped and said to Timmy, "You're a slow runner, but that's okay. We can still play together." Timmy was happy to hear that and they played together all day. They ran, jumped and had so much fun. Timmy realized that even though he was slow, he could still have fun with his fast friend Benny.

A boy was walking along the beach when he found a pot of clay. It was smooth to touch and smelled delicious. He started playing and shaping the clay into different figures. He realized that from playing with the clay, he felt better and began to heal inside. He felt happy and peaceful. The boy then took the clay home with him. He was excited to share his discovery with his family. He carefully put the clay in a bowl and baked it in the oven. When it was finished, it smelled even more delicious. The boy's family were so proud of him and how he had used the clay to heal himself. They ate it with joy and tasted the deliciousness of the baked clay. It was a delicious and special way to heal.

Tommy was a farmer who had a big dog named Spot. Spot was Tommy's best friend and helped him with his work. They liked to dig holes in the ground and plant seeds for the crops. Sometimes, they also found bones and rocks in the dirt. One day, Tommy and Spot were digging a hole near the fence when they heard a loud noise. It was a big truck that was driving very fast on the road. The truck did not see Spot and hit him with its wheels. Spot made a sad sound and stopped moving. Tommy ran to Spot and hugged him. He was very upset and cried. He said, "Spot, Spot, wake up! You are my best friend, please don't go!" But Spot did not wake up. He was gone. Tommy did not know what to do. He wanted to keep Spot with him, but he also knew that Spot needed a place to rest. He decided to bury Spot in the hole they had dug. He used his shovel and his hands to cover Spot with dirt. He said, "Goodbye, Spot. I love you. You were a good dog." Tommy put a wooden cross on the spot where he buried Spot. He wrote Spot's name on it with a marker. He said a prayer and thanked Spot for being his friend. Then he went back to his house. He was very lonely and sad. He missed Spot very much. He wished he could see him again. But he never did. The end.

Zoe and Ben love to play outside. They like to run, jump, slide and swing. They have a lot of fun with their toys and friends. But sometimes, the sky gets dark and it rains. Then they have to go inside and wait for the sun to come back. One day, Zoe and Ben see a big box in the living room. It has a picture of a zigzag on it. They wonder what is inside. They ask their mom, but she says it is a surprise. She says they can open it tomorrow, if it does not rain. Zoe and Ben are very curious and excited. They hope it does not rain. The next day, Zoe and Ben wake up early. They look out the window and see a bright blue sky. They are very happy. They run to the living room and open the box. Inside, they find a big and expensive bike. It has two wheels, a bell, a basket and a zigzag pattern. It is the most beautiful bike they have ever seen. They hug their mom and thank her. She says it is a gift from their dad, who is away on a trip. She says he loves them very much and he will be back soon. Zoe and Ben can't wait to ride their new bike. They put on their helmets and go outside. They take turns to pedal and steer. They go fast and slow, left and right, up and down. They make a lot of noise with their bell. They fill their basket with flowers and leaves. They have a lot of fun with their bike and friends. They don't notice the clouds that are forming in the sky. They don't hear the thunder that is rumbling in the distance. They don't see the rain that is falling on the other side of the street. They are too busy enjoying their zigzag bike.

A dog named Fred was very nervous. He was standing on the beach, looking at the water. All of a sudden, he noticed a laser moving through the water. He had never seen anything like it before. He was so scared that he began to shake. Suddenly, a small fishing boat appeared from around the corner. A man stepped out and asked Fred, "What's the matter, little buddy? What are you so nervous about?" Fred pointed towards the water, where the laser was still moving. The man smiled and said, "Don't worry, that's nothing to be scared of. That's just a fish catching robot. It uses lasers to move around inside the water." Fred was relieved to hear this. He felt much better and began to wag his tail. He said goodbye to the man and ran home, happy that he now understood what he had seen.

Wednesday went by really quickly for Jill. She was so excited because she knew something amazing was happening that day. She saw amazing animals, such as elephants and lions, and even juggled balls. She laughed and cheered as the clowns performed their stunts. Then, at the very end of the show, the ringmaster opened a big chest and inside Jill found a teddy bear. She was so excited she hugged the bear tight, and she still has it now, many years later. It was a truly amazing Wednesday!

The creature closed its eyes and waved its long thin arms. It began to laugh. Tommy tried to run away, but the creature was too fast. The creature chased Tommy until he fell over and couldn't get away. The creature grabbed Tommy and then disappeared. Tommy was never seen again.
