She explained that when he washes his hands, the picture will wash away and his hands will be clean. Tommy was unsure, he wanted to keep his picture. His mother smiled and said 'That is why you don't put too much soap in your hands. If you do, the picture will shrink and it won't be on the soap anymore!' Tommy learned an important lesson that day: using just the right amount of soap will help keep things clean and avoid wasting things.

His eyes lit up and he hopped faster with delight. When he got close, he could feel the wetness of the ladybug's wings. He skillfully used his tongue perfectly and soon the ladybug was caught. The frog looked around and seeing nothing else, he hopped away, feeling proud of himself. After all, he had recognized two creatures, and had caught them both with fast moves!

"I had it on the window sill, but I fell and it flew away," Tommy said. "Maybe it's outside. Let's go and look for it," his mom said. She took Tommy by the hand and went to the door. She opened it and saw something shiny on the grass. It was Tommy's triangle. "Look, Tommy, there's your triangle!" his mom said. She pointed to the grass. "Yay, my triangle!" Tommy said. He ran to the grass and picked up his triangle. He was happy and relieved. He hugged his triangle and thanked his mom. "Are you feeling better now, Tommy?" his mom asked. "Yes, mom, I'm feeling better. Thank you for finding my triangle. I'm sorry I was careless," Tommy said. "That's okay, Tommy. I'm glad you're okay. Just be careful next time, okay?" his mom said. Tommy was careful not to drop it again. He learned his lesson. He was a furry cat who liked to play with his toys. He had a ball, a mouse, and a triangle. He liked the triangle best, because it had three sides and three corners. He could roll it, bite it, and scratch it.

Can I keep it?" "Yes, of course," said Mommy, "but we need to fix it first." Mommy took the broken bean and sprayed it with a mysterious liquid. Then she held it up to the sunlight. The doctor came to their house. He had a big bag with him. He looked at Tommy and said, "Hello, Tommy. I am here to help you. Let me check your temperature and listen to your chest." The doctor put a stick in Tommy's mouth and a thing on his ear. He rubbed Tommy's back and chest with a cold thing. He said, "Hmm, you have a fever and a bad cold. You need some medicine and some rest. I will give you a syrup and a spray. They will make you feel better." Tommy did not like the syrup and the spray. They tasted yucky and made him gag. He cried and said, "No, no, I don't want them. They are bad. They hurt me. Go away, doctor. Go away." The doctor said, "I'm sorry, Tommy, but you have to take them. They are good for you. They will make the red nose and the sore throat go away. Trust me, I am a doctor. I know what I am doing." But Tommy did not trust the doctor. He pushed him away and ran to his bed. He hid under his blanket and said, "Leave me alone. Leave me alone. I don't need you. I don't need anyone." The doctor shook his head and said, "Tommy, you are making a big mistake. You are very sick. You need to take your medicine and let me help you. If you don't, you will get worse and worse. You will not get better. You will not be happy. You will be sorry." But Tommy did not listen. He did not take his medicine. He did not let the doctor help him. He stayed in his bed and cried. He got worse and worse. He did not get better. He was not happy. He was sorry. He was very sorry.

Jerry put on his favorite hat and started dancing around the room. His friends followed him and they all laughed as they moved around. Mia joined the group and asked, "What kind of dance is this?" Two friends, Mason and Abbi, went to the park together. "Mason, look at the birds!" said Abbi. Mason looked up and saw the birds flying. His eyes shone. He wanted to fly too. The Angel smiled at the two friends and said, "You can fly if you wish it." Mason smiled and said, "Let's go flying!" He and Abbi held hands, closed their eyes and flew away. They were so happy!

Alice and her mom went on a fun walk one day. On their way, they saw a big old tree. Alice got a bit scared and asked her mom, "What's that big tree for?". Her mom smiled and said, "That's a jolly old tree, sweetie. Come, let's give it a rub!" She took Alice's hand and they approached the tree. She told Alice to rub her hands on the tree, so Alice did. As soon as Alice's hand touched the tree, it began to shake, which scared Alice. She let out a scream, "Mommy! What's happening?". Her mom laughed and said, "Don't be scared, that just means the tree is happy to be getting a nice rub. See, it's jolly now!" Alice smiled and rubbed the tree some more. The tree grew more and more jolly, and Alice knew it liked her rubs. She smiled, happy to have made a jolly old tree happy.

Zara was a zebra who liked to talk a lot. She talked to the birds, the trees, the rocks and the sky. She talked when she was happy, sad, bored or curious. She talked so much that sometimes she did not listen to anyone else. One day, Zara saw a big lake with clear water. She wanted to talk to the fish in the lake. She ran to the edge of the lake and shouted, "Hello, fish! Do you want to talk to me?" But the fish did not answer. They were scared of Zara's loud voice and hid under the water. Zara did not notice. She kept talking and talking. She did not see the crocodile that was creeping up behind her. The crocodile opened its big mouth and snapped at Zara's tail. Zara screamed and jumped away. She ran back to her herd of zebras. She was very scared and hurt. "Zara, what happened to you?" asked her mother. "A crocodile tried to eat me!" cried Zara. "Why did you go to the lake alone? You know it is dangerous!" said her mother. "I wanted to talk to the fish!" said Zara. "Zara, you are very foolish. Fish do not talk. And you should not talk so much. You should listen and learn from others. Then you will be safe and smart." said her mother. Zara felt ashamed. She realized that she had been very foolish. She decided to talk less and listen more. She thanked her mother and hugged her. She learned a valuable lesson that day.

"Once upon a time, there was a little girl who lived alone in the woods. She was very lonely, but she loved the animals and plants around her. One day, she found a curious creature in her garden. It was a strange, furry creature that had a big head and two shoulders. The creature asked her to do something. It demanded that she come with it and help find some food. The little girl hesitated, but she agreed. She followed the creature deep into the forest. After walking for a long time, the creature stopped in front of a steel gate. Behind the gate, a giant wolf was waiting. The creature demanded that the little girl feed the wolf. She was scared, but she put her shoulder to the gate and began to push it open. The little girl was about to enter the gate when the wolf bounded forward and attacked her. He growled and bit her arm, before running off into the deep forest. She had to lay there, all alone in the woods, injured and bleeding. The little girl never returned home. She was never seen again."

Zip was a little fish who liked to swim fast and play with his friends. He was not afraid of anything, not even the big sharks who sometimes came near his home. One day, he saw a shiny thing at the bottom of the sea. He wanted to see what it was, so he swam down, down, down, until he reached the deep part of the water. "Wow, what is this?" he said to himself, as he touched the shiny thing. It was a ring, with a pretty stone that sparkled in the light. Zip put it on his fin and felt very happy. He decided to show it to his friends and swam up, up, up, to the shallow part of the water. But as he was swimming, he did not notice a big shadow behind him. It was a shark, who had seen the shiny thing and wanted to have it for himself. He opened his mouth and tried to bite Zip, who was too busy looking at his ring. "Help, help!" Zip cried, as he saw the shark coming closer. He was scared and did not know what to do. He wished he had stayed with his friends and not gone to the deep part of the water. But then, he heard a loud splash and saw a big tail. It was his friend, Fin, who had heard his cry and came to save him. Fin was a dolphin, who was very strong and smart. He hit the shark with his tail and made him go away. "Are you okay, Zip?" Fin asked, as he swam to Zip and hugged him. "Yes, thank you, Fin. You saved me. You are my best friend," Zip said, as he hugged him back. "I'm glad you are safe, Zip. But what is that shiny thing on your fin?" Fin asked, as he noticed the ring. "Oh, this? I found it in the deep part of the water. It is very pretty, but it is also very dangerous. The shark wanted to have it and tried to eat me," Zip said, as he took off the ring and gave it to Fin. "Here, you can have it. You deserve it. You are my hero," Zip said, as he smiled. "Thank you, Zip. But I don't need it. You can keep it. It is a gift from the sea. Just be careful next time and don't go to the deep part of the water alone. There are many things that can hurt you there," Fin said, as he gave the ring back to Zip. "Okay, Fin. I will. And I will always stay with you and our friends. You are right. There are many things that can hurt me in the deep part of the water, but there are also many things that can make me happy in the shallow part of the water. Like you," Zip said, as he put the ring back on his fin. "Me too, Zip. Me too," Fin said, as they swam away together, happy and safe.

The bear was very excited and said, "Is it my birthday? Is this a birthday card?" The cat nodded and said, "Yes, it's your birthday! You are now three years old!" The bear was so happy, he lay down on the card and rolled around like a small puppy. The bear and the cat celebrated the bear's birthday for a long time. They ate cake, played games, and told stories until it was time to go to bed. The bear hugged the cat goodbye, and then carefully tucked the card under his pillow. He settled in, feeling happy and special on his very first birthday.

"Mommy, look!" shouted Sally, pointing to a funny mask on the ground. The mask was green and had a long, pointy nose. Mommy smiled. "Oh, Sally! Let me take a look at that mask!" She picked it up and examined it. Then, she put it on her own face and said with a funny voice, "Hello! I'm the mask!" Sally giggled. Mommy laughed and said, "That was a foolish thing to do. Let's put it back where it belongs." She bent down and placed the mask back on the ground. Then, she looked at Sally and said gently, "Remember, it's not a good idea to pick up masks from the ground. It's best to leave them there." Sally nodded and smiled. Then, she grabbed Mommy's hand and said, "Let's go explore the park!"

Zara was a zebra who liked to eat yummy grass. She had many friends who were also zebras, but she wanted to see other animals too. One day, she saw a big bird with bright colors and a long tail. She thought it was very pretty and wanted to talk to it. "Hello, bird. What is your name?" Zara asked. "Hello, zebra. I am Pepe, the peacock. You are very pretty too. Do you want to see my feathers?" Pepe said. "Yes, please. I want to see your feathers. They look like rainbows." Zara said. Pepe opened his tail and showed Zara his feathers. Zara was amazed by the colors and patterns. She wanted to have feathers like Pepe. "Pepe, can I have feathers like you?" Zara asked. "Of course, zebra. You can have anything you want. You just have to follow me to the magic pond. There, you can become anything you want." Pepe said. Zara was very happy and curious. She wanted to become a peacock and fly with Pepe. She followed him to the magic pond. But Pepe was not a nice bird. He was a mean bird who liked to trick other animals. He wanted to eat Zara, but he knew she was too big and fast for him. So he lied to her and wanted to make her smaller and slower. When they reached the pond, Pepe said, "Zebra, look at the water. It is very clear and shiny. If you drink some, you will become a peacock. Trust me, it is very yummy." Zara looked at the water. It was very clear and shiny. She wanted to drink some and become a peacock. But she also felt something was wrong. She remembered her friends, who were zebras. She remembered her mommy, who told her to be careful of strangers. She remembered her yummy grass, which she liked to eat. She did not want to lose them. She did not want to become something else. "Pepe, I changed my mind. I do not want to become a peacock. I want to stay a zebra. I like being a zebra. I have friends and family and yummy grass. Thank you for showing me your feathers, but I have to go now." Zara said. Pepe was angry and hungry. He wanted to eat Zara, but he knew he could not catch her. He tried to push her into the water, but Zara was stronger and smarter. She kicked him with her hooves and ran away. She ran back to her friends and told them what happened. They were glad she was safe and smart. They hugged her and ate yummy grass together. Zara was happy and proud. She liked being a zebra. She did not want to become anything else.

Anna and Ben are friends. They go to the same school. They like to play and learn together. One day, they have a lesson about eyes. The teacher shows them a picture of an eye. She says, "This is an eye. It helps you see. The black part in the middle is called the pupil. The white part around it is called the white. The pupil can get bigger or smaller depending on how much light there is." Anna and Ben are curious. They want to see their own pupils. They look at each other's eyes. They see the black and the white. They see the pupil change size when they move closer or farther from the window. They think it is fun and amazing. They decide to play a game. They take turns poking each other's white gently with their fingers. They say, "Poke, poke, poke!" They giggle and laugh. They see how the pupil reacts to the poke. They are careful not to hurt each other. But then, the teacher sees them. She is not happy. She says, "Stop that! You should not poke your eyes or your friend's eyes. It is not safe. It can hurt your eyes. You need your eyes to see. You should be gentle and respectful with your eyes and your friend's eyes." Anna and Ben feel sorry. They did not mean to be bad. They say, "We are sorry, teacher. We were just playing. We wanted to see our pupils. We did not know it was not safe. We will not do it again." The teacher smiles. She says, "I am glad you are sorry. I know you were curious. But you have to be careful with your eyes. They are very important and delicate. There are other ways to learn about your pupils. You can use a mirror, or a flashlight, or a magnifying glass. But you should never poke your eyes or your friend's eyes. Do you understand?" Anna and Ben nod. They say, "Yes, teacher. We understand. Thank you for teaching us. We will be careful with our eyes and our friend's eyes. We will use other things to learn about our pupils." The teacher hugs them. She says, "You are welcome. I am proud of you for being honest and polite. You are good friends. Now, let's go back to the lesson. I have more things to show you about eyes."

He wanted to play with the knob. One day, Mommy was busy in the other room. Tommy saw the knob and wanted to play with it. He turned it and heard the click sound. He smiled. He turned it more and more. He did not see the fire. He did not smell the smoke. He did not hear the alarm. Mommy smelled the smoke and ran to the kitchen. She saw the fire and Tommy. She screamed and grabbed Tommy. She ran out of the house. She called the firemen. The firemen came and put out the fire. They said the house was spoiled. Mommy was sad. Tommy was scared. Mommy was angry with Tommy. She said he was a bad boy. She said he spoiled the house. She said he could have hurt himself and Mommy. She said he did not listen to Mommy. She said she was not proud of Tommy. Tommy cried. He said he was sorry. He said he just wanted to play with the knob. He said he did not know about the fire. He said he loved Mommy. Mommy hugged Tommy. She said she loved Tommy too. She said she was glad he was safe. She said he had to learn to obey Mommy. She said he had to be careful with fire. She said he had to be a good boy. She said she hoped he would make her proud someday. Tommy nodded. He said he would try. He said he did not want to spoil anything again. He said he did not want to play with the knob anymore.

Anna and Ben are friends who like to play in the garden. One day, they find a big pumpkin that is orange and round. They both want to take it home and make a pie. "I saw it first!" Anna says. "It is mine!" "No, it is mine!" Ben says. "I touched it first!" They quarrel and pull the pumpkin from each other. They are not happy and not nice. A bird is watching them from a tree. He feels sorry for them and flies down to talk to them. "Why are you quarreling?" he asks. "The pumpkin is big enough for both of you. You can share it and be friends." Anna and Ben look at the bird and then at each other. They feel ashamed and sorry. "You are right, bird," Anna says. "We should share and be friends. I am sorry, Ben." "I am sorry, too, Anna," Ben says. "We can take the pumpkin home and make a pie together." They hug and smile. They thank the bird and carry the pumpkin to Anna's house. They cut it and scoop out the seeds. They make a deep hole in the middle and fill it with sugar and spice. They bake it in the oven and make a crust. They have a delicious pumpkin pie and eat it with cream. They are happy and nice. They share the pie with the bird and their families. They are good friends.

Dad grabbed the file and they went back to the car. He said, "Hold onto the file, Zoe!" Then, he pressed down on the gas and the car began to speed again. Soon, they were home. Dad said, "Thank you for holding the file, Zoe." Zoe smiled and said, "Thanks for the ride, Dad!"

But it was not a good acorn. It was a spicy acorn. It burned his mouth and made him cough. He spit it out and tried another acorn. But it was also a spicy acorn. "This is a very special ring. It belongs to someone very important." "Who, Mommy, who?" Zara asked. Mommy looked at the ring. She gasped. She recognized it. It was the ring of the queen. She had seen it on TV. "Zara, Ben, you found the queen's ring!" she said. "She lost it yesterday when she visited the park. She was very sad. We have to give it back to her." Zara and Ben were surprised. They did not know they had found the queen's ring. They felt sorry for the queen. They wanted to make her happy. "OK, Mommy, let's give it back," they said. Mommy called the palace. She told them they had found the ring. They were very happy. They said they would send someone to pick it up. Soon, a big car came to the park. A man in a suit came out. He had a badge. He was the queen's helper. "Hello, I'm here to pick up the ring," he said. "Thank you for finding it. The queen is very grateful. She wants to meet you and thank you personally. Would you like to come with me to the palace?" Zara and Ben looked at each other. They nodded. They were excited. They wanted to meet the queen. They gave the ring to the man. They said goodbye to their parents. They got in the car. They drove to the palace. They met the queen. She was very nice. She gave them hugs and kisses. She gave them medals and gifts. She thanked them for finding her ring. She invited them to have tea and cake with her. Zara and Ben had a wonderful time. They felt like princes and princesses. They were happy they had found the ring. They were happy they had made the queen happy. They were happy they had picked the zigzag flower.

Anna and Ben are friends. They like to play in the park. One day, they see a big bus. The bus has many pictures of animals on it. The bus is going to the zoo. "Look, Ben, a zoo bus!" Anna says. "I want to see the animals. Do you?" "Yes, Anna, I do. But we need tickets to go on the bus. Do you have tickets?" Ben asks. "No, I don't. Do you?" Anna says. "No, I don't. We are helpless. We can't go to the zoo." Ben says. He is sad. Then, a nice lady comes to them. She has two tickets in her hand. She smiles at Anna and Ben. "Hello, children. I have two extra tickets for the zoo bus. Do you want to go with me?" She offers. "Really? Can we?" Anna says. She is happy. "Yes, you can. I am going to the zoo with my son. He is your age. He would like to have friends to play with. Come on, let's go." She says. "Thank you, lady. You are very kind." Ben says. Anna and Ben take the tickets and follow the lady. They get on the bus and sit next to her son. He is friendly and shares his toys with them. They all go to the zoo and have a lot of fun. They see many animals and learn their names. They are not helpless anymore. They are happy.

Zoe and her Mommy went to the store to buy some food. Zoe wanted to help, so Mommy gave Zoe a small basket. Zoe was very excited and put lots of food in the basket. Sometimes Zoe didn't know what to do when the basket was heavy, so Mommy would help her reverse it and the food wouldn't fall out. Then Zoe would be very pleased and she would smile and say "thank you Mommy." After the food was bought, Zoe and Mommy went for a walk. Zoe wanted to show off her basket, so she carried it with her. Zoe started to get tired, so Mommy helped her reverse the basket on her back. Zoe smiled and said "thank you Mommy" and she felt so proud! They walked for a while and then Mommy had to go home. Zoe was sad, but she was happy to carry her small basket back home. Mommy smiled and said "You look so proud of your basket, Zoe. I'm proud of you for carrying it all the way." Zoe smiled and gave Mommy a big hug.

"Once upon a time there was a little girl called Elsa. She was very anxious to do her best at school and be a good student. Every day she would work hard and when she got the right answers, her teacher gave her a reward. This made Elsa very happy, and every time she would get a reward, she would repeat the same thing over and over again. 'I'm so happy! Thank you, thank you!'. So every day Elsa worked as hard as she could and got lots of rewards from her teacher. She was always smiling, and everyone saw how proud she was. The end."

Tommy was so excited. It was time to go to the barber. He jumped out of bed, put on his clothes, and ran out the door. His mom smiled as Tommy hopped into the car. "We are almost there," she said. When they got to the barber, Tommy saw the barber with a big smile on his face behind the door. He asked, "Are you ready for me?" The barber nodded and said, "Yes! I will unlock the door." Tommy's eyes got wide with excitement. The barber opened the door and Tommy hopped inside. He was ready for his first trip to the barber!

"That's far enough!" said Mom. Little Tommy was exhausted. He had been running around all day, trying to keep up with his two older siblings. He stopped and looked at his mom sheepishly. "It's time for you to go to school, Tommy," said Mom. "You need to pay attention in class and learn as much as you can." Tommy felt very dull and didn't really want to go to school. He'd rather just stay home and play with his friends. But Tommy realized he had to go. He walked to school, but the closer he got, the slower he walked. His footsteps got so heavy he felt like he was never going to get there. When he finally reached school, he barely had time to catch his breath before he was swept into the classroom. Once he got through the door, his teacher began calling on him. "Can anyone tell me what a pupil is?" the teacher asked. Tommy knew the answer, but he was scared to raise his hand. He just stared down at the floor. Suddenly, his teacher gave him a gentle smile and said, "It looks like someone already knows the answer! Can you please tell us what a pupil is, Tommy?" Tommy nervously raised his hand and said, "A pupil is someone who learns things in school."

Tommy was very tired after playing with his toys all morning. He wanted to nap, but he could not find his pillow. He looked under his bed, in his closet, and behind his chair. He asked his mom, "Where is my pillow, mom?" Mom smiled and said, "Your pillow is in the laundry, Tommy. It was dirty and I had to wash it. Do you want to use another pillow for your nap?" Tommy shook his head. He did not want to use another pillow. He only liked his pillow. His pillow was blue and soft and had a picture of a dog on it. He said, "No, mom. I want my pillow. When will it be ready?" Mom checked the dryer and said, "Your pillow will be ready in a few minutes, Tommy. Why don't you read a book or draw a picture while you wait?" Tommy nodded and picked up a book. He sat on his bed and tried to read, but he was too sleepy. He yawned and closed his eyes. He fell asleep without his pillow. Mom came back with his pillow and saw him sleeping. She smiled and tucked him in. She put his pillow under his head and kissed him gently. She said, "Sweet dreams, Tommy. I love you."

"Mommy," said Sam, "can I go play in the park?" His mom smiled and nodded. She watched him as he ran and jumped towards the park. As Sam was playing, he found a purse in the sand. He felt around inside and felt some coins. Suddenly, a voice yelled, "Hey! That's my purse!" Sam turned around and saw a lady standing there. She was pointing at the purse. Sam quickly threw the purse back at the lady. Getting closer, the lady looked angry. Sam was scared. He started to cry. The lady softened. "I know why you took the purse", she said. "It's okay." Sam was relieved. He wiped his eyes. He then noticed the lady had a bitter look on her face. She said, "My purse was full of money, meant for groceries. Now, I don't know how we're going to eat this week." She slowly walked away. Sam was sad. He had thrown away someone's hope.

Tom was a rude boy. He did not like to share his toys or say sorry. He did not listen to his mom or dad. He did not pray before he ate or went to bed. One day, Tom got sick. He had a fever and a sore throat. He could not play or go to school. He felt very bad. His mom made him some soup to help him feel better. She brought it to his room on a tray. "Here, Tom, eat some soup. It will make you warm and strong," his mom said. But Tom did not want soup. He wanted candy and cake. He pushed the tray away and said, "No, I don't like soup. It is yucky. Go away, mom. You are mean." His mom was sad and angry. She said, "Tom, you are being very rude. Soup is good for you. You should be thankful for what you have. And you should pray to God to heal you and forgive you." Tom did not care. He turned his face to the wall and closed his eyes. He did not eat the soup or pray to God. He just lay in his bed and felt worse and worse. That night, Tom had a bad dream. He dreamed that he was alone in a dark and cold place. He was hungry and thirsty and scared. He looked for his mom and dad, but he could not find them. He looked for his toys, but they were gone. He looked for candy and cake, but there was none. He only saw a bowl of soup on a table. But the soup was old and moldy and had worms in it. It smelled bad and made him sick. Tom cried and cried. He wished he had been nice to his mom and dad. He wished he had eaten the soup and prayed to God. He wished he could go back to his home and his bed. He was sorry for being rude. He woke up with a start. He saw his mom sitting by his bed. She was holding a new bowl of soup and a spoon. She smiled and said, "Tom, are you feeling better? I made you some fresh soup. Do you want to try some?" Tom nodded and reached for the soup. He said, "Yes, mom, I want some soup. Thank you, mom. I love you, mom. I'm sorry for being rude." His mom hugged him and said, "I love you too, Tom. I'm glad you are sorry. God loves you too, Tom. He wants you to be well and happy. Do you want to pray with me?" Tom nodded and said, "Yes, mom, I want to pray with you. Thank you, God. I'm sorry for being rude." They prayed together and ate the soup. Tom felt warm and strong. He did not have a fever or a sore throat anymore. He was happy and thankful. He learned to be nice and polite. He learned to share his toys and say sorry. He learned to listen to his mom and dad. He learned to pray before he ate and went to bed. He was not a rude boy anymore. He was a good boy.

"Come on Mommy, let's go!" said Lisa. "Where do you want to go, Lisa?" asked Mommy. "I want to go to the store!" said Lisa happily. So, Mommy and Lisa went to the store. When they arrived, Lisa ran inside and saw lots of lights. She pointed at them and said, "Look, Mommy! Pretty lights!" Mommy smiled and said, "Yes, they are very pretty. Let's look around to see what else we can find!" Lisa and Mommy went around the store and found lots of toys, clothes, and other things. Lisa was so excited! After looking around, Mommy and Lisa checked out and went back home. As they drove away, Lisa said "Wow, that was fun! Can we go to the store again?" Mommy chuckled and said, "Yes, of course! We can go to the store as often as you like!" Lisa smiled and was filled with excitement as they drove away.

Before she left the park, she had one more surprise. People were giving out delicious candy. She grabbed a few pieces and went home. When she got there, she turned on the radio. "Mommy, can I stay in the large park?" Lisa asked. "Yes, but stay away from the old paint can," her mom warned. Lisa was so excited that she ran to the park. She saw some birds, a few squirrels, and even a rabbit. Then, she spotted the large paint can full of colorful paint. Lisa wanted to play with the paint, so she opened the can, but she heard her mom's voice again. "Stay away from the paint," her mom warned. Lisa looked around at the fun things to do in the park. She decided to play hide and seek with the creatures she saw. The afternoon flew by and soon the sun was setting. Lisa's mom called her to come home. But Lisa thought that the park was so much fun that she didn't want to leave. "Oh, please can I stay?" Lisa begged. Her mom smiled and said, "Okay, as long as you stay away from the paint." Lisa smiled and ran to join the other creatures at play. She had a wonderful day and knew that she could always stay in the large park and enjoy the fun things to do.

Yesterday, Mandy was playing in her bedroom. She saw something interesting on the ceiling. She wanted to take a closer look. She jumped up onto her bed and stretched her arm up to the ceiling. But it was too high. Mandy's mum noticed that she was trying to reach something on the ceiling. She smiled and said, "Let me help you." She lifted Mandy up to the ceiling. Mandy touched the ceiling. It was dry. She slowly closed her hand around something. It was an old toy that she had forgotten about. She was so happy to find it! Then, her mum set her back down on the bed. Mandy held onto the toy and smiled. She looked back up to the ceiling and said "Bye bye!" Then she went back to playing.

Yesterday, there was a restless girl. She was always wanting to move and explore. Every morning she would stretch her arms and legs and enjoy feeling her body move. All day, she ran and climbed and laughed and played. But at night time, she would stretch one last time, with a contented sigh, before settling down to sleep. Early the next morning, she was awake and ready to go. She stretched her arms up to the sky and smiled. Again, she would go on an adventure! She ran out the door and soon was stretching her legs as she climbed a big hill. As she reached the top, she smiled and looked out. What an exciting life she had. Tomorrow, she would stretch her limbs again and explore something new. And for today, she was content in the knowledge that she had made the most of yesterday.

Anna and Ben are going on a big trip with Mom and Dad. They are very happy and excited. They pack their bags and toys and get in the car. Mom and Dad have passports. Passports are papers that let you go to other places. They drive to the airport and get out of the car. They have to wait in a long line to show their passports. Anna and Ben are bored and tired. They want to play and run. But Mom and Dad say they have to be quiet and stay close. In front of them, there is a man who is very rude. He is loud and angry. He pushes and shoves other people. He yells at the lady who checks the passports. He says he is in a hurry and he does not care about anyone else. Anna and Ben do not like the rude man. They think he is mean and scary. They hold Mom and Dad's hands and hide behind them. They wish the rude man would go away. When it is their turn, the lady who checks the passports smiles at them. She says they are very cute and polite. She asks them where they are going and what they want to see. Anna and Ben tell her they are going to see their grandma and grandpa, and they want to see the animals and the flowers. The lady says that sounds wonderful and gives them stickers. She tells them to have a nice trip and be safe. Anna and Ben are very happy and grateful. They say thank you and give the lady a kiss on the cheek. The lady laughs and hugs them. She says they are very sweet and kind. She says they are the best part of her day. Mom and Dad are very proud of Anna and Ben. They say they are very good and brave. They say they love them very much. They give them a kiss and a hug. They say they are ready to go on their big trip. They say they are going to have a lot of fun. Anna and Ben smile and nod. They are ready too. They say they love Mom and Dad very much. They say they are the best family ever.

he was going to collect something in the morning! Every morning he left his house and walked to the park. Today he was going to find something. He had no idea what it was but he was sure he would find it. Some of the other park goers thought Will was a little weird. They had no idea what he was doing walking around the park every morning. As the sun came up, Will couldn't help but feel a bit excited. Will walked around the park until he found a huge pile of leaves. He had no idea why it was there, but he thought it would be the perfect place to collect something. He began gathering the leaves until he made a huge pile of them. Then, to Will's surprise, he noticed something weird in the middle of the pile. It was a beautiful shiny stone! Will had no idea why it was in the pile of leaves, but it gave him such joy that he immediately decided to take it home. Will had searched and collected the perfect thing to make his morning special. From now on, Will knew he could always count on the pile of leaves to bring him something he loved.

"Mommy, why is everyone so busy?" asked little Jake. "They're all preparing for winter," mommy answered. Jake looked around, puzzled. "What is winter?" "Winter is the coldest season of the year," she said. Jake's eyes lit up. "Does that mean I can play in the snow?" Mommy smiled. "Yes, you can play in the snow if it snows where you live." Just then, a snowflake fluttered down. Jake screamed with excitement. "What else can I do in the winter?" he asked. "Well," mommy replied, "you can wear silly hats and coats and mittens." But Jake shook his head. "No, that's not fun or important," he declared. "I want to do something really stupid!" Mommy laughed. "Then you can always try to catch snowflakes on your tongue," she said. Jake grinned. That sounded like fun. "Can we start now?" he asked. "Yes," mommy answered. "Let's go!"

True is a soft toy dog. He likes to play with his friend Ben, who is a little boy. Ben and True have a lot of fun together. They run, jump, roll and bark in the garden. They also cuddle and read books in the bedroom. One day, Ben and True hear a loud noise. It is a big truck. The truck comes to Ben's house. It has a lot of boxes. Ben's mom and dad say they have to move to a new house. They say they have to pack all their things in the boxes. Ben and True are sad. They do not want to leave their house and garden. Ben's mom and dad give him a big box. They say he can put his toys in the box. Ben puts his cars, his blocks, his balls and his books in the box. He looks at True. He does not want to put True in the box. He loves True. He wants to keep True with him. "Can I take True with me?" Ben asks his mom and dad. "Of course, you can, Ben," his mom and dad say. "True is your best friend. You can hold him in the car. He will be safe and happy with you." Ben smiles. He hugs True. He says, "I'm glad you are coming with me, True. You are my soft and good dog. I will never shut you in a box. I will always play with you and cuddle you." True wags his tail. He licks Ben's face. He says, "Woof, woof. I'm glad you are my friend, Ben. You are my kind and brave boy. I will never leave you. I will always be with you and love you."

A boy wanted to ride his bike, but his mom was worried. She worried the road was too dangerous so he couldn't go outside. The boy was feeling sad, so he asked his dad to help. Dad knew the road was not safe, but he wanted his son to be happy. So he found a special place that was safe to ride. The boy was so excited. He put on his helmet and hopped on his bike, ready to go. Away they rode, past houses, across fields, and down a long hill. As they rode, the boy felt so free. He felt like he could go anywhere and do anything. They kept riding until the sun went down. As they rode, the boy learned about being safe and respectful on the roads. He also learned never to be ignorant to the dangers around him. The boy and his dad rode home in the darkness, happy and tired. Now the boy never needed to worry about riding, because he knew how to be careful.

Yesterday, it was very cold outside. I put on my warm coat and went to play in the park. I saw a big tree with lots of leaves. I believe the tree was happy to see me. I ran around and played with my toys. Suddenly, I felt very cold and wanted to go home. I said goodbye to the tree and went back to my house.

old, Lily, to the fair. Lily was so excited to see the rides, popcorn and candy! They stopped in front of a strange chamber. A man asked them to enter. Inside the chamber was a beautiful show. It was all fair. Lily looked amazed! Then the man asked Mama and Papa to stand beside Lily. The show ended with a burst of magical lights. Lily clapped her hands and said, "That was fair!" Mama and Papa smiled, happy that Lily enjoyed the show. They laughed and hugged and said, "Let's go for some popcorn now!" And so, the happy family went off to the fair and had a wonderful day.

Tommy was a little boy who liked to wander. He liked to see new things and go to new places. Sometimes he wandered too far from his family and got lost. He did not like that. One day, he wandered to a big park with many trees and flowers. He saw a big slide and a swing and a sandbox. He wanted to play with them. He ran to the slide and climbed up. He slid down and laughed. He did not see his family. He ran to the swing and pushed it. He jumped on and swung high. He felt the wind in his hair. He did not hear his family. He ran to the sandbox and picked up a shovel and a bucket. He dug and filled and dumped. He made a castle and a moat. He did not notice his family. He looked up and saw a big open gate. He wondered what was behind it. He wanted to wander some more. He ran to the gate and went through. He did not know his family was looking for him. He saw a big road with many cars and trucks and buses. He saw a big store with many toys and books and candies. He saw a big dog with a collar and a leash. He wanted to touch them. He did not see the danger. He ran to the road and tried to cross. He did not look both ways. He did not see the car coming fast. He heard a loud horn and a screech. He felt a bump and a pain. He cried out loud. He heard his family calling his name. He saw his mom and dad and sister running to him. They hugged him and kissed him and checked him. They were scared and angry and sad. They told him he was hurt and he was wrong. They told him he should not wander without them. They told him they loved him and they wanted him to be safe. Tommy was sorry and ashamed. He said he was sorry and he loved them too. He said he would not wander anymore. He learned his lesson. He learned to stay with his family. He learned to be careful and obey. He learned to be happy and grateful.

once upon a time, two best friends went to the park. One of them was a little girl and the other was an elephant. The girl and the elephant decided to play together. The elephant began to give a deep roar as the girl watched and giggled. The roar was loud, but it was harmless. The girl felt full of joy, so she ran to the elephant's trunk and said, "Let's have a picnic! I brought a big sandwich". The elephant smiled and began to help the girl. He used his trunk to pick the sandwich up and passed it to the girl. The elephant opened his trunk wide and said, "Climb on!" The girl climbed on to the elephant's back and they set out for a picnic in the park. They enjoyed their sandwich under the tree, where they laughed and talked about what fun things they could do next. The girl and the elephant quickly became best friends and as they did, the elephant roared again, this time with joy!

"Mommy, what is an invitation?" asked the curious three year old. "An invitation is a special way to tell people you would like them to come to an event or party. It's like when we invited Grandma to your birthday," Mommy responded. The three year old nodded their head and smiled. "Can I have an invitation?" Mommy laughed. "Yes, you can have an invitation. We will have to make it very special for a special event, though." "Thank you, Mommy!" said the three year old as they hugged their Mommy. That night, Mommy gave the three year old an invitation. The three year old read the invitation carefully: they were invited to a special party! However, when they arrived, they realized the invitation was a foolish mistake. They had been invited to a party for grown ups! The three year old sighed, but luckily the other guests were kind and friendly, and they were able to use their special invitation to have some fun.

Yesterday morning, Bill the bear was feeling mighty. He had a secret plan, and he was ready to put it in action. He had decided to serve his friends breakfast in bed! So, he got to work, gathering bread and honey and making a lovely breakfast. He carefully filled four trays with food and a glass of milk for each of his friends. With the trays loaded up, he set off on his special journey. As he knocked on each door, Bill heard a chorus of cheers. Each of his friends were overjoyed to see him and his served breakfast. "Thank you, Bill!" one of his friends said. "You're a very kind bear," said another. Bill beamed with pride, he was so happy his plan had worked. "You're welcome!" said Bill. "I'm happy to serve you."

"Look Mommy, a mug!" shouted little Suzy, pointing to a mug in the supermarket. "Yes, that's a mug," said Mommy, with a smile. Little Suzy was excited, she picked up the mug and wanted to buy it. "Can I have this mug, Mommy, please please please?" she asked. Mommy looked at the mug, it had a blue pattern on it and little Suzy liked it a lot. "Sure, what will you name your new mug?" Mommy asked. Suzy thought for a moment and said, "Freddie!" Mommy laughed, "That's a great name. Now, let's go pay for it." Mommy paid for the mug and they started to walk home. When they arrived, they put the mug on the table but Suzy found it uncomfortable. "Mommy, can I put a cushion in Freddie's home?" she asked. "Yes, that's a great idea," Mommy said. So Suzy carefully put a cushion inside the mug. Now Freddie had a comfy home and little Suzy was very happy!

Tommy was feeling embarrassed, because he had dropped his ice cream on the beach. He started to cry, as he looked at the mess. Suddenly, a dolphin jumped out of the water. It smiled at Tommy and said "Don't cry! I'm here to help you." The dolphin then sprayed water on the ice cream and the sand. Tommy was surprised and asked the dolphin why it was helping him. The dolphin replied: "I just want to make sure that you're happy and comfortable. That's what friends are for." Tommy smiled and thanked the dolphin. Then, the dolphin stepped closer and comforted Tommy with its fin. Tommy laughed and the dolphin swam away. He was no longer embarrassed, but was grateful for his new friend.

"Look at me, Mommy!" exclaimed little Jack. He was trying to balance a book on his finger. "That's amazing, Jack!" said his Mom. Suddenly the book fell off of his finger. "Oh no!" cried Jack. "That's okay, Jack," said his Mom, "just try again." Jack tried again, but the book still wouldn't stay on his finger. Then he noticed his finger was very filthy. "Mommy, my finger is all dirty," Jack said, "that's why the book won't balance." "Let's get it cleaned up, then," said his Mom. So his Mom cleaned his finger and Jack had another go at balancing the book. This time it stayed on his finger! Jack grinned. "I did it, Mommy!" he said. "That's great!" said his Mom.

He put his face close to the bowl and smiled. Then he could smell the mix. It was a sweet smell! It made him feel so happy. Tom was careful as he stirred the mix with a spoon. He scooped some mix into a cup and said, "Look, I made a special mix!" Everyone cheered and clapped. Young Tom was so proud of his special mix.

Two kids, Joe and Mark, were walking in the park. They passed by each other and started to fight. Joe pushed Mark, making him drop his bag. Mark shouted, "That's mine!" Joe said, "I'm stronger than you so I get to keep it!" Joe was not very intelligent. Mark didn't like what Joe said. He was angry and said, "I'm not letting you get away with this!" He stepped forward and grabbed the bag back. Joe got scared and started to run away. Mark followed after him. Joe ran faster and Mark couldn't keep up. Joe got away and Mark didn't get his bag back. He was sad and angry. He knew he couldn't fight someone bigger and stronger than him. Joe was too smart for him. Mark went home feeling frustrated and sad. He was furious that Joe had taken his bag, and disappointed in himself for not being intelligent enough to outsmart Joe. He learned his lesson that day

"Let's go play in the woods, Momma," said Jimmy eagerly. His mom nodded and they both headed outside. They soon saw a big brown bear in the middle of a clearing. Jimmy was scared, but he wanted to be brave. So he took a deep breath and cautiously approached the bear. The bear smiled at Jimmy and said, "Come play with me!" Jimmy smiled back, happy to have a new friend. They played together for a while until a bee buzzed around the bear's head. The bear didn't like it and tried to swat the bee away. But his big claws were too clumsy and he accidentally slapped Jimmy on the arm. Jimmy wasn't hurt, but he was scared and started to cry. His mom rushed over and gave the bear an angry look. The bear knew he'd done something wrong and scurried away quickly. His mom hugged Jimmy tight and said, "It's ok, honey. You were very brave and the bear won't bother us anymore!" Jimmy smiled and they both went home, eager to tell their family about their new experience.

True was a dog who loved to play with his ball. He was very enthusiastic and would run and jump and catch the ball in his mouth. He liked to keep the ball for himself and did not want to share it with anyone. One day, he saw a boy walking in the park with his mom. The boy had a ball too, but it was bigger and brighter than True's ball. True wanted that ball very much. He thought it would be more fun to play with. He ran towards the boy and barked loudly. The boy got scared and dropped his ball. True grabbed the ball in his mouth and ran away. He was very happy and proud. He thought he had the best ball in the world. But the boy was very sad and cried. His mom tried to comfort him and looked for True. She saw him hiding behind a tree with the ball. She was angry and shouted at True. She said he was a bad dog and he had to give the ball back. True did not want to give the ball back. He growled and showed his teeth. He thought the mom would go away and leave him alone. But he was wrong. The mom had a stick and she threw it at True. The stick hit True on the head and made him drop the ball. He felt a lot of pain and whimpered. The mom picked up the ball and gave it to the boy. She hugged him and said he was a good boy. She said they would go home and get him a treat. The boy smiled and thanked his mom. He said he loved her and his ball. True was left alone in the park. He had no ball and no friend. He was very sad and sorry. He wished he had not been so greedy and mean. He wished he had shared his ball with the boy. He learned a hard lesson that day. He realized that keeping things for himself was not the way to be happy.

"Mommy and Daddy invited Auntie and Uncle over for tea," said Sally, a three year old. "Yay!" exclaimed Sally. Mommy and Daddy prepared the meal and then put on their fanciest outfits. Daddy recorded the moment so they could save it. After they finished their tea, they enjoyed some pastries, chatted and shared stories. By the time Auntie and Uncle left, Sally was feeling happy and full. She knew that this was a moment she would never forget.

Tommy loves to watch the reindeer on TV. They have big horns and shiny noses. They help Santa bring gifts to good kids. Tommy wants to be a good kid too. She shows him how to glue on some brown crayons for the horns and a red one for the nose. Tommy draws eyes and a mouth with a black crayon. He is very proud of his reindeer. "Look, mom, I made a reindeer!" Tommy says, holding up his craft. "That's wonderful, Tommy! You did a great job!" Mom says, hugging him. "What's his name?" Tommy thinks for a moment. He remembers the names of the reindeer on TV. He likes one name a lot. He says, "His name is Rudolph. He is not a regular reindeer. He has a shiny nose." Mom smiles and says, "That's a perfect name for your reindeer, Tommy. He is very special, just like you." Tommy hugs his reindeer and says, "Thank you, mom. I love you and I love Rudolph." Mom says, "I love you too, Tommy. And I love your reindeer. Do you want to hang him on the wall?" Tommy nods and says, "Yes, please. Then he can watch me finish my milk and cookies." Mom helps Tommy hang his reindeer on the wall. Then they go to the kitchen and have some milk and cookies. Tommy is very happy. He has a new friend and a new craft. He can't wait to show Rudolph to Santa.

The reindeer were so happy and thanked Wendy for such a fun game.

aid on it and gave her a hug. She said, "Don't worry, Anna. Your knee will heal soon. You are a brave girl." Anna wanted to play with her bike again, but Mommy said she had to rest. Tommy was sad. His mom was in the hospital. She was sick and needed help from the doctors. Tommy missed her a lot. He wanted to see her and hug her. One day, his dad took him to the hospital. They walked in a big hall with many doors. They found the door with mom's name on it. They knocked and went in. Mom was lying on a bed. She had a tube in her nose and a bandage on her arm. She looked tired but happy to see Tommy and dad. She smiled and said, "Hello, my loves. I'm so glad you're here." Tommy ran to her and climbed on the bed. He gave her a big kiss and said, "I love you, mom. Are you feeling better?" Mom hugged him and said, "I love you too, Tommy. I'm feeling a little better. The doctors are very nice and they're giving me medicine to make me well." Dad sat on a chair next to the bed. He held mom's hand and said, "You're very brave, mom. We're very proud of you." Mom said, "Thank you, dad. You're very kind and you're taking good care of Tommy." Tommy looked around the room. He saw a window with a blue sky and a white cloud. He saw a flower in a vase and a teddy bear on a table. He saw a picture of him and mom and dad on the wall. He felt happy and peaceful. He said, "Mom, this is a nice room. It's like our home." Mom said, "Yes, it is, Tommy. But it's not our home. It's the hospital. And soon, we'll go back to our real home. And we'll be together again." Tommy said, "I can't wait, mom. I miss our home. Tommy was a little boy who liked to eat a lot of candy. He always asked his mom for more candy, even when she said no. He did not like to eat healthy food, like fruits and vegetables. He only wanted sweet things. One day, his mom went to the store and left Tommy with his dad. Tommy saw his chance to get more candy. He ran to the kitchen and opened the refrigerator. He saw a big bowl of candy on the top shelf. He reached for it, but it was too high. He got a chair and climbed on it. He grabbed the bowl and smiled. But then he heard his dad's voice. "Tommy, what are you doing?" his dad asked. He came into the kitchen and saw Tommy with the candy. He was not happy. "Tommy, you know you are not supposed to eat candy before dinner. Put it back in the refrigerator, please." Tommy refused. He held the bowl tightly and said, "No, I want candy. It is mine. Go away." He stuck out his tongue at his dad. His dad was very angry. He took the bowl from Tommy and put it back in the refrigerator. He said, "Tommy, you are being very rude and selfish. Candy is not good for you. It can make you sick and hurt your teeth. You need to eat healthy food to grow strong and smart. And you need to listen to your parents and be respectful. If you don't, you will have no candy at all, and you will have a time out." Tommy felt bad. He realized he had made a mistake. He said, "I'm sorry, dad. I was wrong. I don't want to be sick or hurt my teeth. I don't want to be rude or selfish. I want to be good and nice. Can I have some fruit instead of candy?" His dad smiled and hugged him. He said, "That's better, Tommy. I'm glad you understand. Yes, you can have some fruit. And maybe later, you can have a little candy as a treat, if you eat your dinner and behave well." Tommy nodded and smiled. He learned his lesson. He decided to eat healthy food and be polite. He knew that candy was not everything, and that his dad loved him. The moral of the story is: Don't eat too much candy, and listen to your parents.
