They have a lot of fun. They laugh and learn. They become best friends. Tom likes his new cube. He thinks it is the best toy ever. He is glad he heard the weird sound from his toy box. He is glad he found the robot cube. He is glad he gave it a chance. He is glad he has a new friend.

A little girl named Lucy loved gardens. Whenever she could, she would hop in a daddy's lap and he would take her to the garden. Today, it was especially nice outside, so Lucy and Daddy went to the garden. The garden was so beautiful. The flowers were big and bright and it smelled so good! Lucy couldn't wait to see all the plants and touch the soft grass. They started walking and suddenly, Lucy noticed something running across the garden. It was a colourful frog! Lucy was so excited! She sprinted across the garden to try and catch it, but the little frog hopped away. Lucy went back to the nice, clean garden. Daddy and Lucy looked around and saw a lot of delicious vegetables and flowers growing. Daddy pointed out a patch of carrots, and Lucy eagerly picked some of the sweet carrots and ate them right away. They also found some really juicy tomatoes and some fragrant herbs. They stayed in the garden until the evening, picking fresh food and watching the sun set in the sky. They were so happy. The garden was clean and full of life and love. As they left, they looked forward to their next visit, when the flowers and veggies would have sprung up even more!

Tommy and Lily were twins who liked to play together. They had many toys, but their favorite was a big red ball. They liked to bounce it, roll it, and throw it in the air. Sometimes they played with the ball in the yard, but when it was cold or rainy, they played with it in the house. Their mom and dad told them to be careful with the ball in the house. They said the ball could break things or hurt someone. They also said the ball could make them fall down the stairs if they were not careful. Tommy and Lily said they would behave and listen to their mom and dad. One day, when it was raining, Tommy and Lily decided to play with the ball in the hall. They bounced it, rolled it, and threw it in the air. They had a lot of fun, but they forgot to be careful. The ball bounced too high and hit a picture on the wall. The picture fell down and made a loud noise. Mom and dad heard the noise and came to see what happened. They saw the broken picture and the ball. They were not happy. They told Tommy and Lily that they had been naughty and that they had to go to their room. They also said they had to eat their vegetables for dinner, because vegetables were healthy and good for them. Tommy and Lily felt sorry for what they had done. They said they were sorry and that they would behave better next time. They went to their room and put away their toys. They also decided to play with the ball only in the yard, because they did not want to break anything or fall down the stairs. They learned their lesson and became more careful and respectful.

A boy named Tom wanted to play with his friends. He liked to run, jump, and kick a ball. He was a normal boy who liked to have fun. But Tom had a problem. He had to stay at home because he was sick. He had a red nose, a sore throat, and a hot head. He felt very bad. He did not want to play with his friends. He wanted to sleep. His mom came to his room. She gave him some water and a hug. She said, "Tom, I know you are sick. But you will get better soon. Then you can play with your friends again. You are a brave boy." Tom smiled a little. He said, "Thank you, mom. I love you. But I miss my friends. Can I call them?" His mom nodded. She said, "Of course, you can. They miss you too. They want to hear your voice. They are your normal friends who care about you." Tom felt a little better. He picked up his phone and called his friends. He said, "Hi, friends. I am sick. But I will be okay. How are you?" His friends said, "Hi, Tom. We are sorry you are sick. But we are happy you are okay. We are fine. We are playing with the ball. But we miss you. We want you to play with us." Tom said, "I miss you too. I want to play with you. But I have to rest. Mom says I will get better soon. Then we can play together again. You are my normal friends who make me happy." His friends said, "We are your normal friends who love you. Get well soon, Tom. We will wait for you." Tom said, "Thank you, friends. I love you too. Bye." He hung up the phone and smiled. He felt a little better. He had a normal boy who had normal friends. He wanted to play with them. And he would. Soon.

once upon a time there was a boy named Rob who had a gun. He kept it in a safe place and always was careful. He was excited when he held it outside and pointed it at the sky. Suddenly he heard a loud bang and something destroyed the tree next to him. Rob was very upset and he shouted "who destroyed the tree?". The police officer nearby answered Rob and said "you destroyed the tree with your gun". Rob was very afraid and ran away. Rob was very careless and he had destroyed something precious. Luckily, no one was hurt and the tree was the only thing that was destroyed. But Rob still got in a lot of trouble and had to learn a lesson about being careful when playing with a gun. That's why it's important to always be careful and think of the consequences.

"Come and get your dinner!" called Ma one hot evening. Jenny looked up from her toys and grinned when she saw the dinner on the table. She ran over and took a seat. Ma smiled at Jenny as she put a plate in front of her. On the plate was a juicy steak, some crunchy vegetables and a bowl of mashed potatoes. Jenny grinned hungrily before starting to eat. Ma chuckled at Jenny's enthusiasm. Ma noticed Jenny struggling with the steak, so she leaned in and started to tease her. "You'll never finish this big steak," she laughed. Jenny only laughed and continued to eat until she was full. Then she stuck out her tongue playfully. Ma laughed and said, "Time to go and clean up, my smelly little girl!" Jenny grumbled but followed Ma's order and ran to the bathroom to wash her hands.

Yesterday, Tom was very excited. He was going to eat his favorite meal, yummy pancakes. He woke up early and put on his favorite shirt. Then he skipped out of the house. On the way, he saw a lot of animals. He laughed and smiled at them, until he smelled the pancakes. He ran and jumped into his seat, ready to eat. Tom took a big bite of the fluffy pancakes. He smiled, it was the yummiest breakfast he ever had. Then he got very tired and yawned. His mom smiled and said, "You must be really tired after all your adventures today. You can go take a nap. " Tom smiled and said, "Yes! I am very tired. I need a nap." He yawned again and then toddled off for a nap.

"Mommy, what's in your purse?" asked Bob, who was only three years old. "It's where I keep all my important things," Mommy said. "Like cash and cards." Bob wanted to help mommy so he asked, "Can I help put things in your purse?" Mommy smiled and said, "Sure, that would be great. You can put my cards in there, too." Bob was very careful with mommy's cards. He made sure to put them in the right pocket and organized them in order. Mommy was so happy with Bob's help. She said, "Bob, you're really reliable. I'm glad I have you around to help me with my purse." Bob smiled and said, "I'm happy to help Mommy!"

Yesterday, the family went to a new store. They saw a big wall with lots of colorful signs. Each sign had different words on them. Everyone was excited to see what it said. When they got close, they saw that it said "Welcome! We're glad you're here". Mom and Dad both smiled. They pointed to a sign that said "Come in and take a look around". Mom and Dad laughed and signed the sign. Then they walked into the store. They saw lots of new things. Mom pointed to a new dress and Dad said it was beautiful. They continued to look around the store, admiring all the new things. Finally, it was time to go home. They had a great time and left with lots of new things. The family had a great time yesterday and made lots of new memories.

"Once upon a time, there was a gray house. Inside, a little girl wanted to play outside. Her mom said no, so the little girl was sad. The little girl's mom said that it was too dangerous and wanted to prevent her from getting hurt. The little girl had a different opinion. She thought she could be careful, but her mom said no. The little girl was so sad. She tried to talk to her mom and tell her why she should be allowed to go out. But her mom said no, and would not change her opinion. The little girl was very sad. She sat in the gray house and looked out the window. She wished she could go outside and play, but her mom would not let her. The little girl still wishes she could go outside and play. But she knows that her mom's opinion will prevent her from doing so."

Will was a little boy who was feeling very nervous. He was walking through the park with his mom, when he suddenly saw it: a huge sandwich! It was sitting on a wooden table in a bright and sunny spot, and it looked delicious. Will was so amazed by the sandwich that he forgot about being nervous. He walked quickly over to the table and stood in front of it. His mom laughed, but she was also worried. "Will, we don't know who made that sandwich. We have to be careful," she said. After thinking for a minute, Will decided he wanted to try the sandwich. He asked his mom to wait while he tested it. He took a tiny bit of the sandwich and ate it. It was so yummy! He ate the rest of the sandwich and was so happy. Then Will and his mom held hands and went for a walk around the park. Will felt so good. He wasn't nervous anymore

he didn't understand what it was. Rachel carefully showed him how to tear the paper into little pieces. "See! Tear!" she said happily. When she was finished, she'd made a colorful pile of small paper shapes. "Ah!" said her brother. "Paper!" He smiled in delight. Rachel laughed. She quickly taught him how to make even more shapes. Soon, the room was covered in paper. Rachel and her brother spent the rest of the day playing with the paper pieces and making more and more fun shapes. Rachel was so proud of her brother. He had gone from being confused about the newspaper, to becoming a paper

Uncle was a very kind man. He always spoiled his nephew, Julian. Whenever Julian was sad, Uncle would take him for ice cream. Julian loved the smooth, cold treats. Whenever Julian was feeling brave, Uncle would take him to the park. They would swing back and forth on the swing and Julian always thought it was so much fun. Uncle was always there to spoil Julian. He read him books, listened to stories and gave him lots of hugs. Julian always felt special around his uncle and loved spending time with him. Uncle always did his best to make sure Julian felt loved and cared for. He never forgot to spoil his nephew and always made sure Julian was happy.

"Run, Max!" shouted Mom. Max was a very loyal 3 year old. He followed Mom to the fence. When he reached the fence, he wanted to climb it. But Mom said, "No, Max. It isn't safe". She put her arm around him and said, "We can have an adventure, if you like. Let's explore the other side of the fence". So they did. Along the way, they saw butterflies and bees. Max loved it. Then they reached a meadow full of wildflowers. Max ran through the meadow, picking flowers. Mom laughed and clapped. They finally reached the end of the fence. Max was a bit sad. He didn't want the adventure to end. But Mom promised they would come back soon. Max thanked his Mom for their adventure and promised himself he would always be loyal to her.

Tommy likes to play with his watch. It is shiny and has many buttons. He can make it beep and light up. He wears it on his wrist and feels like a big boy. One day, Tommy sees his mom's watch on the table. It is bigger and prettier than his watch. It has a pink band and a shiny face. Tommy wants to play with it. He thinks his mom will not mind. He takes the watch and puts it on his wrist. He pushes the buttons and makes it beep and light up. He feels very happy. He runs around the house with the watch. But his mom does mind. She sees Tommy with her watch and gets angry. She says, "Tommy, that is my watch! You should not take it without asking! You could break it or lose it! That is very naughty!" She takes the watch from Tommy and puts it back on the table. She says, "You are punished, Tommy. You cannot play with your watch or any other toys for one hour. You have to sit on the couch and think about what you did." Tommy feels very sad and sorry. He does not like to be punished. He does not like to sit on the couch. He thinks his mom's watch is weird. He likes his watch better. He says, "I'm sorry, mom. I won't take your watch again. Can I have my watch back, please?"

"Bounce, bounce, bounce," shouted the little boy as he jumped on his bouncy rubber ball. He loved to feel independent while playing outside by himself. As he jumped higher and higher, he felt so happy. Then suddenly, he heard a voice. "Hello there," it said. The little boy looked around and saw a big, brown dog standing by him. He felt a little scared at first, but then he smiled. "Hello," he said back to the dog. The dog smiled and said, "Why don't you show me how you bounce on your rubber ball? It looks so fun!" The little boy happily agreed and soon he was bouncing higher and higher on his ball, feeling so independent and so happy. The dog laughed and smiled, seeing how much fun the little boy was having. "Thank you for playing with me!" said the little boy. "You're welcome!" replied the dog, and then it bounded away. The little boy watched the dog disappear and then he resumed his bouncing, smiling with joy. He was thankful for his wonderful day playing independently with his rubber ball.

Yesterday, Jack decided to go to the park. It was a noisy place, with lots of people and birds chirping very loudly. But Jack didn't mind. He liked to watch the birds flutter around and see the other children run and play. He decided to swing on the swing first. It was a lot of fun, but it made a lot of noise. Jack laughed and waved his arms in the air as he swung back and forth. Then, he decided to try the slide. He climbed to the top and slid down, shouting with joy. He was so happy he went down the slide again

Anna and Ben are friends who like to play in the snow. They build a big igloo with blocks of snow and make a door and a window. They pretend it is their house and they have a lot of fun. One day, a new boy comes to play in the snow. His name is Tom and he has a red hat and a blue coat. He sees Anna and Ben's igloo and he wants to join them. But he does not ask nicely. He says, "Your igloo is silly and small. I can make a better one. Move away and let me show you." Anna and Ben are sad and angry. They do not like Tom. He is mean and rude. He teases them and tries to break their igloo. They say, "No, Tom. This is our igloo. We made it together. You cannot play with us. Go away and leave us alone." Tom does not listen. He pushes Anna and Ben and kicks their igloo. He makes a hole in the wall and laughs. He says, "Ha ha, your igloo is weak and ugly. Look, I can make a bigger hole. Watch me." But Tom is not careful. He kicks too hard and the igloo falls down. It makes a loud noise and a lot of snow falls on Tom. He is cold and wet and scared. He cries and says, "Help, help, I am stuck. Get me out of here." Anna and Ben hear Tom's cries. They are still sad and angry, but they are also kind and helpful. They say, "Tom, you were mean and rude. You teased us and broke our igloo. But we will help you. We will dig you out of the snow. But you have to say sorry and be nice." They use their hands and their shovels to dig Tom out of the snow. They are careful and gentle. They pull him out and brush him off. He is shivering and sniffling. He says, "Thank you, Anna and Ben. I am sorry, I was mean and rude. I teased you and broke your igloo. I was wrong. Can you forgive me? Can we be friends?" Anna and Ben look at each other. They smile and nod. They say, "Yes, Tom. We forgive you. We can be friends. But you have to be nice and polite. And you have to help us build a new igloo. A bigger and better one. One that we can all share and play in." Tom smiles and nods. He says, "Yes, Anna and Ben. I will be nice and polite. And I will help you build a new igloo. A bigger and better one. One that we can all share and play in." They hug and make up. They work together and build a new igloo. A bigger and better one. One that they can all share and play in. They learn that being nice and polite is better than being mean and rude. And that being kind and helpful is more useful than being mean and rude. And that being friends is more fun than being enemies.

Tommy was very brave. He had to go to the doctor and get a needle. He did not like needles. They made him feel ouchy. But Mommy said the needle would help him stay healthy and not get sick. The doctor was nice. She had a white coat and a big smile. She told Tommy to sit on a big chair and look at a book. Mommy held his hand. The doctor said, "This will be very quick and not hurt much. Just relax and settle down." Tommy tried to be calm. He looked at the book. It had pictures of animals and colors. He liked the yellow duck and the blue fish. He did not see the needle. The doctor put it on his arm and said, "One, two, three, all done!" Tommy felt a little pinch. He said, "Ow!" But it was over soon. The doctor put a band

aid on his arm. It had a red heart on it. She said, "You did great, Tommy! You are very brave. Here is a sticker for you. You can choose one." Tommy smiled. He was proud of himself. He looked at the stickers. There were many kinds. He picked a green dinosaur. He liked dinosaurs. He said, "Thank you, doctor!" He showed Mommy his sticker and his band

"Bob was a hunter. He came out into the woods in search of a rabbit. He was so excited! He had never seen one before. Suddenly, Bob heard a rustle in the leaves. He saw a little rabbit! He slowly sneaked up behind it, but the rabbit noticed him. It ran away, hopping and jumping over the grass. Bob was so upset. He chased the rabbit, but he couldn't catch it. Then he realized something. He couldn't catch the rabbit, because he didn't have a net! He dropped to his knees and said "Oh no! I forgot to bring my net!" Bob was so embarrassed. He knew that he needed to think of a different plan. Then he had an idea. He said to the rabbit, "Please stop running! I promise I won't hurt you, if you just stay put for a little while." The rabbit heard Bob's voice and stopped running. He realized that he could use his hands to catch the little creature. So he slowly reached out and grabbed the rabbit. The rabbit was so scared, but soon it realized Bob meant it no harm. Bob smiled, happy that he had been able to catch the rabbit without a net. The rabbit was safe and Bob was satisfied.

Willow was so excited! She was going to the library for the very first time. When she arrived, she was amazed. Everywhere she looked were neat rows of books. She spotted a table with a chair next to it and ran over to it. Suddenly, Willow heard a voice. "Hello! Welcome to the library! I'm going to close soon, so please make sure the library is nice and tidy when you leave," said the librarian. Willow nodded and smiled. She said she would. Willow spent hours at the library, reading book after book. When it was time to go, she made sure to stack all the books she had used neatly. The librarian smiled and thanked her for leaving the library so tidy. Willow smiled as she left. She couldn't wait to return to the library again.

once upon a time, there was a mild day. it was a sunny afternoon, and a little boy wanted to have some fun. He decided to go outside and explore what was around him. He walked on the path and he found a small hole. He squatted down and peered inside. What he saw made him smile. There were tiny bugs zooming around and around! He reached out his hand to try and catch one of them, but they were too fast. He sat back and watched them, watching them zoom around and around and around. He smiled and laughed. The little boy had a lot of fun playing with the bugs! He stayed there until the sun started to set and it was time to go back home. He left the hole, still smiling, happy and excited of what he had just seen.

"Mommy, what are you doing?" asked Pat. "I'm cleaning the kitchen," replied Mommy. Pat squinted her eyes and peered into the kitchen as she watched Mommy work. "Look at all the dishes! This one needs a good clean," said Mommy, pointing to the sink. Pat nodded. She loved to help Mommy with cleaning. "Can I help too?" asked Pat. "Yes, you can help me clean," said Mommy. Mommy gave Pat a safe cloth and some water. Pat smiled and made sure the cloth was nice and wet, and then she began to clean. The dishes were soon sparkling and they smelled nice too. Mommy patted Pat on the head and said, "Well done!" "Thanks, Mommy!" said Pat, and she gave her a big hug.

Yesterday was a gentle day. Mommy and Daddy left the house early in the morning. They said they would be home later in the day. All morning, the little boy waited for them to come back. He watched out of the window, but he didn't see them. He was worried. But later in the afternoon, Mommy and Daddy came home. They had been to the store and brought lots of treats for the little boy. He was happy! They gave him big hugs and asked him how his day was. The little boy smiled and said his day had been gentle. Mommy and Daddy said they were going to leave again soon, but they promised to come back tomorrow. The little boy was still worried, but then he just remembered that Mommy and Daddy had said "tomorrow". So he smiled and said goodbye. He knew that when tomorrow came, Mommy and Daddy would come back. He fell asleep with a happy smile on his face.

A famous little boy was crawling through the airport. He was looking all around and marveling at everything he saw. He saw planes and children, adults and suitcases. It was so exciting to be in such a big place. As he crawled, he was sure to explore every corner of the airport. Suddenly, he heard a loud noise and he got scared. But it was just the sound of a plane taking off. He looked up and saw it go up into the sky and disappear. He thought it was amazing. He was happy to crawl through the airport. He had so much fun exploring and seeing things he had never seen before. It was a very famous place and he wanted to come back.

Wendy walked into the corner of her room, looking around. She pulled out a box and opened it. Inside the box was a beautiful veil, shimmering in the light. She thought to herself, "It looks special. I wonder what it is." Suddenly, Yuko appeared in the corner of the room. She smiled at Wendy and said, "I have something special for you Wendy". Yuko motioned for Wendy to come closer. Once she was close enough, Yuko carefully lifted the veil from the box, and held it out to Wendy. She said, "This veil is for you Wendy, it will make you look like the princess you are!" Wendy was delighted with the veil, and she happily put it on, spinning around in circles to display it. Yuko watched, with a hint of mischief in her eyes. Later that evening, Wendy was feeling restless, so she decided to put the veil back on and go for a walk. As she walked, the moonlight glinted off the veil, and to her surprise, she heard a voice calling her. The voice called out, "Wendy! Come, I have something special for you!". Wendy realized the voice was Yuko's and she ran, excited to discover what Yuko had in store. And so, Wendy followed the voice, and discovered there was a magical kingdom waiting for her beyond the veil.

"March," said mommy one day. Mommy had something very special in mind. She grabbed the hand of her little girl and started marching. The little girl smiled and marched with mommy. marching, marching, marching. They marched for a long time through the big, wide forest. Mommy and the little girl looked around and saw so many different things. They saw all kinds of animals, colorful flowers and even some tall trees. Suddenly, the little girl heard a sound. "Meow!" it said. It was a little kitty. It was looking for its parent and was so sad. But then the little girl saw something different. It was her mommy and she was giving the kitty some food and water. The little girl smiled and said, "Mommy, you are so kind and different." Mommy smiled and hugged the little girl. After that, they continued to march through the forest until they reached home.

Two birds were chirping on a bush. They were very strong and happy. The first bird said, "I can fly the highest!" The second bird said, "I can fly the farthest!" So they both flew up high in the sky, higher and higher. They flew and they flew, until they could hardly be seen. The first bird said, "I went so high!" The second bird said, "I went so far! I flew behind that big bush!" The first bird laughed and said, "Now let's come back down and swing on the bush!" So they flew back down and landed on the bush. They both laughed and enjoyed swinging on the strong bush.

"Let's go to the barn," said mommy. Billy was excited. He loved going to the barn. He loved to see the animals and to play in the hay. They got to the barn, but when they got inside, Billy noticed something was wrong. It was dark and quiet. "Mommy, why is it so dark?" asked Billy. Mommy looked worried. "We have to cover the animals so they don't get scared," she replied. So mommy and Billy worked together to cover the animals in the barn with blankets. Billy was scared but he kept working with mommy. When they were finished, mommy put her arm around Billy's shoulder. She was very worried. "Come on, let's go home," she said. Billy was confused. He didn't know why they had to leave so suddenly. But he followed mommy's lead and they went back home. When they got home, mommy told Billy that the barn had caught on fire and all the animals had died. Billy was so sad he started to cry. He had never seen anything so terrible. Mommy hugged him tight, and Billy knew that she was just as worried and sad as he was.

Yesterday, there was a fancy party. Lots of people came and they all had fun. There was cake and balloons and music. But one little girl remained sad. She didn't have a fancy dress like the other kids. She felt left out. But then, a kind lady saw her and gave her a pretty dress to wear. The little girl was so happy! She danced and played with the other kids. She didn't feel sad anymore. Today, the little girl still remembers how nice the lady was. She thinks about it every time she sees a fancy dress.

"Let's search for our friend!" shouted a little girl. She grabbed her friend's hand and ran to the park. They looked around the trees and bushes for their friend. Soon, they came across a big cardboard box and a man who was sitting beside it. "Why are you sitting outside the box my friend?" asked the little girl. "I'm so embarrassed," the man replied. "My friends are hiding in the box and they won't come out because they're scared to see me." The two children smiled and offered to help the man out. They opened the box and found the man's friends huddling inside. They said "Hello!" to the man and hugged him. The man was incredibly happy and thanked the children. After a few minutes of talking, the children and the man went their separate ways. The two little friends learned that it's important to always be willing to help people in need. They will never forget their search for the man in the cardboard box.

once upon a time, there was a little girl. she was three years old. one day she decided to go and play in the garden. she saw her spade in the garden and picked it up. she wanted to dig a hole. so she started to throw the spade into the ground. but the spade did not fit into the ground. it kept bouncing back up. the girl was sad and confused. she didn't know what to do. so her mother came outside. and said, 'you must be gentle with the spade, and move it in and out slowly. that way it will find a fit in the ground.' the girl followed her mum's advice and tried again. this time it worked! the spade fit in the ground. the little girl was excited to have made the hole. the Moral of the story is: be gentle, and things will fit.

"Mummy! What is that big balloon?" said 3 year old Amanda. "Oh, that's a big helium balloon. It's for the party," Mummy replied. Amanda was excited, but she was disturbed by a noise. "Mummy, who is making the noise?" she asked. Mummy looked around and saw a tidy grey cat peeking out from a closet. "Oh, it's just a cat. Don't worry, it's harmless," she said. Amanda was still curious, so she pulled a balloon off the string and rolled it towards the cat. The cat immediately got startled and ran away. "Amanda, why did you do that? You shouldn't have disturbed the cat," said Mummy in a stern voice. Amanda looked down and shook her head, feeling guilty for her mistake. Mummy smiled and gave her a hug. "It's ok, let's put all the balloons back in the right place," she said, and they quickly made the balloons look neat and tidy.

Yesterday, Jay was very excited. He was going to get a new toy to replace his old one. His old toy was so worn out that it was no longer fun to play with. Jay asked his mum, "Can I get a new toy?" Mum smiled and said, "Yes, you can get a new toy. Go and take a look at the toy shop. See what you like." Jay rushed to the toy shop. He saw a big, shiny blue car. He loved it. He asked the shopkeeper, "Can I have this car?" The shopkeeper said, "Yes, you can have this car. But it costs a lot of money." Jay's face fell. He was so troubled. He had no money to buy the toy. Mum was right behind him. She said, "Let's go home Jay. We can't buy this car today." Jay was disappointed. He didn't get to replace his broken toy with the shiny new one.

"Mommy, why is my orange hurt?" asked the little girl. She was only three years old, and had found an orange on the sidewalk by her house. She picked it up to show her mom. "Well, sweetie," explained Mommy,"Sometimes when fruit falls down from the tree, it can get all bruised and hurt. It still tastes just as sweet, though. Here, take a bite to see." The little girl put her tiny fingers around the orange, gave it a gentle squeeze, and took a bite. As soon as the juice hit her tongue, she started to cry tears of joy. "See, baby? It's still as sweet as ever," Mommy said, smiling. "So don't worry that it's hurt, because it still tastes just as good as new!" The little girl stopped crying and smiled, and hugged her mom. She was so glad the orange was still sweet and tasty, even though it was hurt.

Tommy was walking in the garden. He found a pot with a plant in it. It had big green leaves and it had beautiful flowers on it. The flowers were big and bright and they smelled spicy. Tommy touched the petals of the flowers and they felt so soft. He looked at the label on the pot and it said 'hibiscus'. He hadn't seen a hibiscus before. He took the pot home and put it on the window sill. He watered it and saw the plant start to bloom. The hibiscus plant had bright red flowers, with petals that felt like velvet. They smelled so spicy! Tommy was so glad he had found this special plant. Every day he came to the window sill and admired his hibiscus. Whenever he smelled the spicy petals, he knew he had found something very special.

"Come on! Bow, bow!" shouted Peter. Peter was three years old, and he wanted to shoot the black pigeon with his bow and arrow. His dad had given him the bow for his birthday, and today he wanted to use it. His mom gave him a warning. "Peter be careful," she said. "You don't want to hurt the pigeon." But he wasn't listening. Suddenly Peter pulled back the bowstring and shot an arrow. The black pigeon flapped its wings and flew away in a hurry. Peter was excited, so he ran after the pigeon. Peter's mom shouted, "Oh no! He liked the sound of thunder, and he was excited to see it one day. So, when the next storm rolled in, Simba and his mom went outside. They sat on the porch and watched the clouds move fast above. Suddenly, they heard a loud boom and Simba jumped up and pointed. "Look Mom, that was the thunder!" Simba shouted, thrilled to see it with his own eyes. They watched the clouds move and felt very thankful that they had such a beautiful view.

Mommy smiled and nodded. "Yes sweetheart, it is beautiful. What are you going to do with it?" The little girl grinned and said, "Let's roll it around the garden and see where it goes." I think it's time to put the glass back where it came from now." The little girl nodded and carefully rolled the glass back to its original spot. Mission complete!

Venus was very curious. She wanted to explore the world around her and observe everything she could. One day, Venus decided she wanted to observe the things in her kitchen. She walked around the room, looking at all of the objects. Suddenly she spotted a big white object in the corner. She saw it had a door and was very intrigued. Venus opened the door and peered inside. She was surprised to see all the colourful food inside. She knew that this object was a fridge. Venus was happy to find that there were lots of available snacks inside. She grabbed some snacks and put them on the counter. Venus was so excited to explore the fridge and was very proud of the snacks she had found. She was sure she had observed something very special!

A beautiful day was outside and Mollie the fox wanted to explore. She ran and ran and ran until she came to a big hill. She looked all around, but didn't see anyone else. Suddenly, her little fox battery quit and she couldn't move any more. Mollie was so sad and she didn't know what to do. Then, she saw a beautiful butterfly fly right in front of her and she smiled. The butterfly started to flutter away towards a big tree, so Mollie followed it. When she got to the tree, she saw a shiny new battery and she was so excited. With her new battery, she was ready to explore again!

Tommy was so excited when he saw the new vehicle. It was incredible! His mom took him outside to show it to him. He couldn't believe his eyes. The vehicle was bright red and sparkled in the sunlight. He loved it so much. He wanted to sit in the vehicle and pretend to drive it, so he asked his mom if he could. She smiled and said yes. Tommy sat in the driver's seat and grabbed the steering wheel. He drove around the courtyard and beeped the horn. He was so excited that he couldn't stop smiling. His mom and dad watched him drive around with smiles on their faces. They were so happy that Tommy was having so much fun. When Tommy was done playing, he gave the vehicle a big hug and thanked his parents for bringing him such an incredible surprise.

Anna and Ben are excited to go to the park with Mom. They put on their hats and shoes and run to the car. Mom says, "Listen, we have to be careful at the park. There are many people and cars and dogs. Stay close to me and hold my hand." At the park, Anna and Ben see a big slide and a swing and a sandbox. They want to play with everything. Mom lets them go on the slide and the swing, but she says, "No, you can't go to the sandbox. There is a big dog there and he might bite you." Anna and Ben are sad. They like the sandbox and they want to make a castle. They look at the dog. He is brown and furry and has a long tail. He is playing with a ball and a stick. He does not look mean. He looks happy. Anna says, "Mom, can we please go to the sandbox? The dog is nice. He is not biting anyone. He is just playing. Please, Mom, please?" Mom says, "No, Anna, I told you no. The dog might not be nice to you. He might think you are taking his ball or his stick. He might hurt you. You have to listen to me. I know what is best for you." Ben says, "But Mom, we want to play with the dog. He is cute and fluffy and he has a big smile. He might be our friend. He might share his ball and his stick with us. Please, Mom, please?" Mom says, "No, Ben, I told you no. The dog might not be cute and fluffy and friendly to you. He might be scared or angry or hungry. He might bite your leg or your arm or your face. You have to listen to me. I know what is best for you." Anna and Ben are very sad. They do not understand why Mom is so mean. They think the dog is nice and they want to play with him. They do not want to listen to Mom. They want to go to the sandbox. They wait for Mom to look away. Then they run to the sandbox. They do not see the dog. They do not hear him bark. They do not feel him jump on them. They only feel his teeth. They scream. Mom runs to them. She is scared and angry and sorry. She hugs them and takes them to the car. She says, "I told you to listen to me. I told you to be careful. I told you the dog might bite you. Why didn't you listen to me?" Anna and Ben are hurt and scared and sorry. They say, "We are sorry, Mom. We are sorry we didn't listen to you. We are sorry we were not careful. We are sorry the dog bit us. We love you, Mom. Please don't be mad at us." Mom says, "I love you, too, Anna and Ben. I am not mad at you. I am just worried about you. We have to go to the doctor and get you fixed. Then we can go home and have some ice cream and read a book. Maybe next time you will listen to me. Maybe next time you will be careful. Maybe next time you will be safe." Anna and Ben nod. They say, "Yes, Mom. Next time we will listen to you. Next time we will be careful. Next time we will be safe." They hold Mom's hand and go to the car. They hope the dog is okay. They hope he finds a nice home. They hope he does not bite anyone else. They hope he listens to his mom, too.

Yesterday, Sammy was very bored. He had no one to play with and nothing fun to do. So, he decided to make a request. He asked his mom if he could go to the park to play. His mom said yes and Sammy was so happy. He put on his shoes and ran outside. At the park, Sammy played on the swings, went down the slide and ran around the playground. He laughed and smiled the whole time. After a few hours of playing, Sammy was starting to get tired. He made one more request, this time to his mom. He asked if they could get ice cream on the way home. His mom said yes and Sammy was thrilled. They went to the ice cream shop and picked out the yummiest flavours. As they ate their treats, Sammy thanked his mom for all the fun they had. It was the best day ever!

once there was a little boy. he was happy and excited. every day he wished he could do something special. One day he was playing in the park when he heard a big noise. A harmless little ant and a giant grabbed hands and went for a long walk around the world. The little ant was excited to explore new places with the giant, but soon felt overwhelmed by the the giant's long and heavy strides. The ant felt so small and the world felt so big. Suddenly, the little ant spat out, "Stop! Don't you see how small I am?" The giant stopped in his tracks and squatted down. He looked at the ant and said, "Of course, I see how small you are. That is why your heart can show courage and kindness. Being small doesn't mean you can't make a difference." The two friends smiled. They held hands again and continued their journey around the world. The moral of the story is that no matter how small you are, you can still make a difference and you should never be afraid to show courage and kindness, no matter the size of the world.

So they changed into their swimwear and jumped into the sea. Suddenly the sea below them started to become very rough and waves were crashing against them. William was scared and he screamed, "Mummy, help me! I'm scared!" His mum grabbed him and carried him onto their yacht. The sea was still very harsh and William was still scared. His mum said, "William, you must behave and listen to me when I tell you what to do. That way, you'll stay safe." William nodded, he knew his mum was right. He stayed on the yacht and listened to what his mum said. After a while, the sea calmed down and William and his mum had a lovely time swimming and exploring the sea. The end.

aid. Maybe we can find your bike later," Tom said. He helped Sam get up and walked with him. He was nice and kind. He didn't say anything about the bike or how Sam was mean to him. Sam felt bad. Can you forgive me?" Sam asked. Tom smiled. He was happy to hear Sam say sorry. He was happy to be his friend. "Of course, Sam. I forgive you. You are my friend, too. Tommy was a restless boy who liked to run and play all day. He did not like to sit still and eat his food, especially when it had pepper on it. He said pepper was too hot and made his mouth hurt. One day, his mom made him a sandwich with cheese and pepper. She told him to eat it and drink some water, because it was good for him. Tommy did not want to eat it. He tried to hide it under his plate, but his mom saw him. "Tommy, you have to eat your sandwich. Pepper is not bad for you, it makes your food tasty and helps you grow strong. If you don't eat it, you will be hungry and tired later," his mom said. Tommy shook his head and pushed his plate away. He wanted to go outside and play with his ball. He did not care about being strong or tasty. He thought his mom was being mean and unfair. He ran to the door and tried to open it, but it was locked. He struggled with the knob, but it did not move. He started to cry and kick the door. He was angry and frustrated. His mom came to him and hugged him. She was not angry, but sad. She said, "Tommy, I love you and I want you to be happy and healthy. But you have to listen to me and do what I say, because I know what is best for you. Eating your food is not a punishment, it is a reward. It gives you energy and nutrients that you need to run and play and learn. Pepper is not a bad thing, it is a spice that adds flavor and variety to your food. Some people like it, some people don't, but you have to try it before you decide. Maybe you will like it, maybe you won't, but you will never know if you don't try. Please, eat your sandwich and drink your water, and then you can go outside and play with your ball. Okay?" Tommy looked at his mom and saw that she was not mean and unfair, but kind and caring. He felt sorry for making her sad and for being rude and stubborn. He nodded and said, "Okay, mom. I will try the sandwich. But can you cut off the crusts? I don't like the crusts." His mom smiled and said, "Sure, I can cut off the crusts. But you have to promise me to eat the rest of the sandwich, and to try new things when I give them to you. Deal?" Tommy said, "Deal." He ate his sandwich and drank his water. He found that the pepper was not too hot, but a little spicy and interesting. He liked the cheese and the bread, too. He felt full and satisfied. He thanked his mom and gave her a kiss. He said, "I love you, mom. You are the best." His mom said, "I love you, too, Tommy. You are a good boy. Now you can go outside and play with your ball. Have fun, but be careful." Tommy went outside and played with his ball. He had fun, but he also learned a lesson. He learned that his mom loved him and wanted him to be well. He learned that eating his food was important and good for him. He learned that trying new things was not scary, but exciting. He learned that pepper was not bad, but different. He learned that being restless was not always good, but sometimes he had to be calm and listen. He learned that being a good boy made him and his mom happy. He learned that he loved his mom and his sandwich, even with pepper on it.

A young girl and her mommy went on a walk one day. As they walked, they noticed a forest in the distance. The little girl was so excited to see the forest and asked if they could go. Her mommy said yes, and they started to make their way over. As they entered the forest, the girl looked around. Everything was so tall and green. The trees towered over the little girl, and she felt so tiny. She noticed a path and decided to go exploring. The little girl walked and walked. Soon, the forest started to look dull and boring. She started to get bored, so she called for her Mommy. Her mommy found her and said that it was time to go home. The girl was so sad to leave the forest, but she was excited to tell her friends about the adventure she went on.

His mom told him he shouldn't believe everything he sees and not to touch the sausage. But Tommy didn't believe her and kept trying to grab the sausage. His mom became very frustrated and she kept telling him not to believe it was a sausage, but Tommy just wouldn't listen. He wanted to be independent and he wanted that sausage. "Come, Mommy!" said the little girl. She was only three, but she was so excited to go on her first plane ride. She ran to the airport with her mom, clutching her white luggage tightly. When they arrived, it took many hands to help lift the luggage onto the conveyor belt to reach the plane. Finally, it was on its way up to the plane! The little girl was amazed. She had never seen anything go so fast! It disappeared in no time. "Wow, Mommy! When will it reach the plane?" she asked. "It'll be there soon," her mother said with a smile. "It's almost time for our plane ride." The little girl smiled as they waited. Soon enough, the luggage emerged. "Look Mommy! It reached the plane!" she exclaimed. Her mother laughed. "Yes, it did. Now, let's go find our seats!"

Tommy was a little boy who liked to play outside. He had a red coat that his mom gave him. He wore it when it was cold or rainy. One day, Tommy saw a new girl in his street. She was playing with a ball by herself. She did not have a coat. Tommy wanted to be her friend. He ran to her and said hello. "Hi, I'm Tommy. What's your name?" he asked. The girl looked at him and frowned. She did not say anything. She kicked her ball away from him. Tommy was sad. He did not understand why she was mean. He asked again, "Why don't you talk to me? Do you want to play with me?" The girl rolled her eyes. She said, "No, I don't want to play with you. You are ignorant. You don't know anything. Go away." Tommy was shocked. He did not know what ignorant meant. He thought it was a bad word. He felt hurt and angry. He said, "You are ignorant. You don't have a coat. You will be cold and wet. You are not nice. I don't want to be your friend." He ran back to his house and told his mom what happened. His mom hugged him and said, "I'm sorry, Tommy. Some people are ignorant. They don't know how to be kind and polite. They don't know how to make friends. You are not ignorant. You are smart and sweet. You have a coat and a heart. You can always play with me." Tommy smiled and said, "Thank you, mom. I love you. Can we play with my ball?" His mom said, "Of course, we can. Let's go outside and have some fun." They put on their coats and went outside. They played with the ball and laughed. Tommy forgot about the new girl. He was happy with his mom.

Anna and Ben are brother and sister. They like to play together in the park. One day, they see a big dog. The dog is brown and fluffy. It has a collar with a tag. "Look, Anna, a dog!" Ben says. He runs to the dog and tries to pet it. "Wait, Ben, be careful!" Anna says. She follows him and sees the tag. It has a name and a phone number. "The dog has a name. It is Max. And this is his owner's number. Maybe he is lost." Anna takes out her phone and calls the number. A woman answers. She sounds worried. "Hello, is this Max's owner?" Anna asks. "Yes, yes, this is me. Have you seen my dog? I have been looking for him everywhere. He ran away from the yard this morning. Where are you?" the woman says. "We are in the park. We found Max. He is safe and friendly. We can stay with him until you come." Anna says. "Thank you so much, you are very kind. I will be there soon. What are your names?" the woman says. "I am Anna and this is my brother Ben. We like dogs. Max is a good dog." Anna says. The woman arrives and hugs Max. She is very happy and grateful. She thanks Anna and Ben and gives them a reward. She also lets them pet Max and play with him for a while. Anna and Ben are happy too. They are glad they helped Max and his owner. They are grateful for their new friend. They say goodbye to Max and go home with their reward. They tell their mom and dad what happened. They are proud of themselves. They are good brother and sister.

Yesterday, Jill went to the park with her mom. She was feeling shy, but she was excited to go. When they got to the park, she saw that there were lots of other kids playing. There were swings that she could hang on. As she started swinging, she felt a little braver. Mom pushed her higher and higher, until she was giggling and shouting yahoo! She really liked to hang on the swings and feel the wind in her face. After a while, Jill went and played on the slide too. She was still sort of shy, but she was having lots of fun. At the end of the day, Jill was feeling very happy. She was no longer scared or shy

Yesterday, Mommy and Daddy took Benny and Bonny to the park. Benny and Bonny were so excited. They had an amazing time. They saw so many things. There were other children sliding down the slide, swinging on the swings, and playing in the sandbox. Benny and Bonny wanted to do it all. They played together and sorted out who could do which activities first. Benny won the slide so he went down it first. He screamed with joy as he went down. Bonny was so amazed she went down the slide again and again. But before long, it was time to go home. Benny and Bonny were sad but they knew they would come back to the park again soon. As they drove home, Mommy and Daddy smiled at each other. They had had an amazing day yesterday at the park.

A girl named Sam wanted to write a story. But when she looked for paper, there was nothing to write with. She searched her bed but it was empty. She was sad, feeling like she would never write a story. Then she remembered her mom's bag. Inside she found a pencil and some paper. She could write now! She was so excited and hopped into her bed to write her story. Sam wrote and wrote until she was finished. It was a special story about a cat and a mouse who were best friends. She was so proud of her story. And with a smile she went to sleep, dreaming of her special story.

Wendy was in the park with her dad. The sun was shining brightly and Wendy was happy. There was a lot to do. She saw a special game that her dad wanted her to try. Her dad gave her a cup and said, "Here you go Wendy! Let's measure the distance you can shoot." Wendy was excited. She put the cup on the ground. Then her dad gave her a small ball and showed her how to throw it. She took a deep breath and threw the ball. The ball flew through the air and landed in the cup. Wendy was so happy she clapped her hands and jumped up and down. "You did it!" Her dad said, grinning. "That was really cute!" Wendy was pleased. She and her dad continued to play. Every time she threw the ball, it seemed to be a little bit farther. By the end of the day, Wendy had quite a lot of fun.

"Look!" exclaimed Little John, pointing his finger towards the grass. In the corner of the garden lay a bed of poppies. They were a bright, vivid red, glimmering in the sun. John ran to the bed of poppies and bent over to take a closer look. He reached out and stroked one of them gently. It felt warm and soft. A tranquil golden glow surrounded the poppy, giving the garden an aura of peace. It was like a magical bubble. John giggled in delight. Suddenly, a voice called out from the other side of the garden. "John, the sun is setting. Come inside for dinner!" John looked at his Dad, smiled, and then ran off towards the house. As he left, the glow from the poppy bed slowly faded away.

Tommy liked to play with his toys in the bathtub. He had a boat, a duck, and a star. The star was his favorite. It was light and shiny. He made it go up and down in the water. He pretended it was a real star in the sky. One day, Tommy's mom said, "Time to get out, Tommy. You have been in the bathtub for too long. You need to dry off and get ready for bed." "But I want to play with my star more," Tommy said. He did not want to leave the bathtub. He loved his star. "Okay, you can play for five more minutes. But then you have to get out, okay?" his mom said. She went to the kitchen to get a towel. Tommy was happy. He played with his star more. He made it shine brighter and brighter. He threw it up in the air and caught it. He was having so much fun. But then, he threw it too high. The star flew out of the bathtub and landed on the floor. It broke into pieces. Tommy was sad. He cried. He lost his star. His mom came back and saw what happened. She hugged Tommy and said, "I'm sorry, Tommy. I know you loved your star. But you have to be careful with your toys. Sometimes, they can break if you play too rough with them. And then you can't play with them anymore." Tommy nodded. He understood. He said, "I'm sorry, mom. I was too excited. I won't do it again." His mom smiled. She said, "It's okay, Tommy. I forgive you. Come on, let's get you out of the bathtub and into your pajamas. Maybe we can find another star for you tomorrow." Tommy got out of the bathtub and dried off. He put on his pajamas and went to bed. He looked out of the window and saw the real stars in the sky. They were light and shiny. He wished he had one of them. But he knew he couldn't. He had to be happy with what he had. He learned his lesson. He closed his eyes and fell asleep.

Anna and Ben are friends. They like to play pretend. Today, they want to put on a show for their moms and dads. They have a stage in the backyard. It is made of boxes and blankets. Anna wants to be a princess. She has a dress and a crown. Ben wants to be a dragon. He has a mask and a tail. They practice their show. Anna says, "Help, help, a dragon is coming!" Ben says, "Roar, I am a scary dragon!" They have fun. But then, Lily comes. Lily is Anna's sister. She is little. She wants to play too. She says, "I want to be a princess!" She takes Anna's dress and crown. Anna is angry. She says, "No, Lily, that is mine! You can't be a princess!" Lily says, "Yes, I can! You are mean!" They start to fight. Ben frowns. He does not like fighting. He says, "Stop, stop, you are ruining the show! Why can't you share?" Anna and Lily do not listen. They pull and tug at the dress and crown. They make a big mess. Their moms and dads come. They see the stage and the fight. They are not happy. They say, "What is going on here? Why are you not playing nicely?" Anna and Lily feel bad. They say, "Sorry, sorry, we were silly." They hug and say sorry to Ben too. They decide to share the dress and crown. They ask Ben to join them. They say, "Let's be a princess, a dragon, and a knight!" Ben smiles. He says, "Okay, that sounds fun!" They fix the stage and the show. They have fun. Their moms and dads clap and cheer. They are proud. The end.

Tommy was playing in the park with his friends. They were running around and having fun. Suddenly, Tommy saw a shiny prize. He wanted to have it very badly. He wanted that prize more than anything else. But when he went to get it, his friend Tony got there first. Tony screamed with joy at his new prize. Tommy didn't know what to do. He felt angry and jealous. He was so upset that he said something mean to Tony. Even though this made Tommy feel better, it made Tony sad. When Tommy's mom heard what happened, she told Tommy that it was wrong to be jealous. She said that being jealous would not give Tommy the prize and might even cost him his friendships. She said that it was important to not be jealous and to think of others before himself. Tommy was really upset but he tried to do what his mom said. He said sorry to Tony and tried to be nice. Even though Tommy lost out on the prize, he learnt an important lesson. Jealousy may make you feel good in the moment but it can cost you something even more precious than a prize.

A boy saw a good umbrella. He wanted to have it so he waved his hands at it. He was so happy when the umbrella's owner waved back to him. He knew that the owner was giving it to him as a gift. The boy looked after the umbrella and kept it safe. He was happy to have something so good. He showed it to all his friends and family. They all said it was so nice. Whenever the boy went out, he took the umbrella with him. He liked to wave it around when it was raining as it made him feel even better. The boy loved his umbrella so much. It was always with him and always made him feel good.

Yesterday, Sarah and her dad were taking a walk in the park. It was a fun day, and the sun was shining. Sarah saw the big slippery slide and begged her dad to go down it. He said, "Ok, let's go!" Sarah's daddy piggybacked her to the top of the slide. She was so excited and had to take a deep breath before sitting down on the pink slide. She asked her daddy again and again, "Are you sure I can slide down it?" Her dad said, "Yes, Sarah. Slide down very carefully, not too fast and not too slow." Sarah did as her dad said and started sliding down very carefully. It was so much fun! But, when she was close to the bottom, something unexpected happened. She started to slide too fast and was scared she might fall. But her daddy was there cheering her on and finally, Sarah's feet hit the ground. She smiled and looked at her dad. He gave her a big hug and said, "See Sarah? If you take it slow and steady, like we talked about, then you can do anything!" Sarah smiled and nodded her head in agreement. This was Sarah's first lesson in life and from that day on, she knew to take her time, be brave and never give up.

"Yes!" he said with a smile. But when they got on the boat, Jerry had a funny feeling. He looked out across the lake and saw a big storm rolling in. He shrugged and said, "It's okay." Mom looked worried, but she decided to be honest and said, "Maybe we should go home." Jerry just nodded. He knew the storm was coming. Once they got back to shore, the rain started and the wind blew. Zara was a zebra who liked to store things. She had a big box where she kept her toys, her books, and her hats. She was very proud of her box and did not like to share it with anyone. One day, she went to the park with her mom and saw a new zebra. His name was Zack and he had a ball. Zara wanted to play with the ball, so she asked Zack if she could have it. "Can I have your ball?" she said. "No, this is my ball. You can't have it," Zack said. Zara was sad and angry. She thought Zack was mean and selfish. She decided to take his ball when he was not looking. She ran to his ball and grabbed it. Then she ran to her box and put it inside. Zack saw what Zara did and cried. He ran to his mom and told her what happened. "Zara took my ball and put it in her box. She is not nice," he said. Zack's mom went to Zara's mom and told her what happened. Zara's mom was not happy. She went to Zara and asked her why she took Zack's ball. "Zack did not want to share his ball with me. He is not kind," Zara said. Zara's mom shook her head. She said, "Zara, that is not right. You can't take things that are not yours. How would you feel if someone took your toys, your books, or your hats?" Zara thought for a moment. She realized that she would not like it if someone took her things. She felt sorry for Zack. She said, "I would feel sad and angry. I am sorry, mom. I am sorry, Zack. I will give you back your ball." Zara took the ball out of her box and gave it to Zack. Zack smiled and said, "Thank you, Zara. I am sorry, too. I should have shared my ball with you. Do you want to play with me?" Zara nodded and said, "Yes, I do. I like your ball. It is fun." Zara and Zack became friends. They played with the ball and shared their things. They learned that it is better to be kind and generous than to be greedy and selfish. They had a happy day at the park.

Anna and Ben are friends. They like to draw and color. They have many crayons and papers. They keep their crayons and papers in folders. Anna has a blue folder and Ben has an orange folder. One day, they want to draw a big picture together. They need a lot of crayons and papers. Anna opens her blue folder and takes out some crayons and papers. Ben opens his orange folder and does the same. They put their crayons and papers on the floor. "Look, I have a red crayon and a green crayon. I can draw a flower," Anna says. "I have a yellow crayon and a brown crayon. I can draw a sun and a tree," Ben says. They start to draw and color. They are happy. But then, Anna sees that Ben has a purple crayon. She likes purple. She wants to use the purple crayon. She reaches for the purple crayon. "Hey, that's my purple crayon. Give it back," Ben says. "No, I want it. It's mine now," Anna says. They pull the purple crayon. They are angry. "Stop it. You are not nice. You have to share," Ben says. "No, you stop it. You are not nice. You have to share," Anna says. They keep pulling the purple crayon. They are not happy. Then, they hear a voice. "What are you doing, Anna and Ben? Why are you fighting?" the voice says. It is their teacher, Miss Lily. She sees the purple crayon in their hands. "Miss Lily, Anna took my purple crayon. She won't give it back," Ben says. "Miss Lily, Ben won't let me use his purple crayon. He is mean," Anna says. Miss Lily shakes her head. She is sad. "Anna and Ben, you are friends. You have to be kind and share. You have many crayons and papers. You can use them together. You can make a beautiful picture together. But if you fight, you will break the crayon and tear the paper. You will make a mess. You will not have fun. Do you want that?" Miss Lily says. Anna and Ben look at each other. They look at the purple crayon. They look at the floor. They see their crayons and papers. They see their picture. They feel sorry. They shake their heads. "No, Miss Lily. We don't want that. We want to be friends. We want to be kind and share. We want to make a beautiful picture together," Anna and Ben say. They let go of the purple crayon. They smile. "Here, Anna. You can use my purple crayon. I can use your red crayon," Ben says. "Thank you, Ben. You are nice. Here, you can use my red crayon. I can use your yellow crayon," Anna says. They swap their crayons. They hug. "Thank you, Anna and Ben. You are nice. You are good at sharing. I am proud of you. Now, let's finish your picture. It will be wonderful," Miss Lily says. She helps them with their picture. They use their crayons and papers. They use their blue folder and their orange folder. They draw and color. They are happy.

Tommy was really excited. He was playing with his blocks and he was having so much fun. He wanted to play all day! His friend Sarah came to see him. She had a big book and she said she needed to study for her exam. Tommy asked what an exam was. Sarah said, "An exam is a test. I have to borrow your blocks and use them to help me study." Tommy agreed, so Sarah borrowed the blocks and started to study. She was so brilliant

old Charlie. He was ignorant of what was inside the attic. "Let's go and find out what's in the attic" said Mom. So, Charlie and Mom marched up the stairs to the attic. Charlie was scared and excited at the same time. Once they reached the attic, Charlie was surprised. It was full of boxes of old toys and clothes! "We can use the toys to play and the old clothes to wear," said Mom. Charlie was excited and started playing with the toys. Mom smiled and said they should end the day with something sweet. Charlie agreed and they went down to get something to eat.

Uncle was new. He had just moved in near and the kids were excited to meet him. Today, uncle was coming to visit. He was bringing something special for them. The kids waited and waited but uncle did not arrive. Mom said he was delayed. This made the kids sad. Then, finally, uncle arrived. He had a big box with him. He said he had something special for them. The kids cheered when they opened it and saw what was inside. It was a new toy! The kids loved it and thanked uncle for the special surprise. They promised they would take good care of it and tell everyone how kind he was. Uncle smiled and said, "You're welcome, but don't forget to thank mom. She was the one that arranged the surprise!"

"Come on!" said Mom. Tom walked with Mom and they saw a big door. Tom wanted to wander into the door and explore. "Where do you want to go, my boy?" asked Mom. Tom said, "I want to wander through the big door!" Mom smiled. She said, "Ok, let's go!" They both walked up to the door. Tom tried to open it but it was too heavy. Mom helped him and they opened the door together. Tom and Mom wandered into the room. It was big and it was full of toys! There were cars, stuffed animals, and even blocks. Tom was so happy. He laughed and ran around the room, exploring all the different toys. Mom watched him with a smile on her face. They stayed in the room for a long time, playing with all of the toys and having fun. Eventually, they had to go home. Tom was sad to leave but he was happy he'd had such a fun time.

Yesterday, Sally was in the park with her mom. She was playing with her doll when she saw a pesky bird. The bird kept flying around her, and it wouldn't go away. Sally became persistent, and she demanded that the bird leave her alone. But the bird kept flying around, and it wouldn't leave. Finally, Sally's mom got involved. She walked up to the bird and said very sternly: "Go away now. Let Sally play in peace." The bird listened to her, and flew away. Sally was relieved and went back to playing with her doll. Her mom smiled at her and said: "See, you just have to be persistent!"

"Come on!" shouted Lisa. She was leading her team on the playground. The bouncy ball came flying into her hands. "I caught it!" she said proudly. The other children cheered. "Where's the next one?" asked one of her teammates. "It's over there!" Lisa pointed to the sandbox. The team followed Lisa to get the ball. Suddenly, Lisa saw a little girl, who was all alone, crying. "Are you okay?" Lisa asked the little girl. The little girl sniffled and said, "I'm sorry. I dropped my ball in the puddle." Lisa felt so bad seeing the little girl sad. She ran to the puddle and looked in. Sure enough, there was the little girl's ball. "Let me help you," Lisa said. She reached in and quickly caught the ball. "Here you go!" Lisa handed it to the little girl. The little girl was so happy, her worries were gone. "Thank you," she said with a smile. Lisa smiled back and said, "You're welcome!"

"Come on," said Lisa to her brother Tommy. "Let's mix some fun!" Tommy nodded and Lisa led him to the elevator. Inside, it was dark and small. When the elevator door opened, Tommy and Lisa stepped out into a room. In the middle of the room was a big bowl filled with colorful things. Lisa said, "Let's mix these things together! It'll be fun!" So they mixed all the colorful things together. They mixed and mixed. Soon the room was a mess. And then they heard a loud sound coming from outside the room. It was loud and scary. "That doesn't sound too good," said Tommy. But Lisa said, "Don't worry. I'm sure it's nothing." They were wrong. When the door opened, a group of angry men stepped in. They weren't happy about the mess. One of the men said, "It looks like you two didn't do a very good job mixing!" Tommy started to cry and Lisa shook her head. She knew they were in trouble. The two were sent to their rooms with no fun mixing for the rest of the day.

mum was getting ready to celebrate. she got out the tomato. it was big and red and fit in her hands. she cut the tomato up into little pieces. the baby was excited when she saw the tomato. she ate it straight away. mum laughed and said to the baby, "aren't you going to celebrate with us?" the baby smiled and giggled. then she picked up a tomato piece and held it in her hands. it fit her hands perfectly. mum gave her some more tomato pieces to eat. the baby smiled and celebrated. she was so happy she started to dance. mum laughed and put the tomato pieces in a bowl. she said, "let's have a celebration food party!" so the family all sat around the bowl of tomato pieces and ate. they talked, laughed and celebrated. it was a wonderful day. everyone was happy and fit!

"Come on Mia, let's play a game!" said Mom. Mia shook her head and refused. "We can keep score, it will be fun!" said Mom. Mia refused again and said nothing. Mom smiled and said, "Fine, let's play together." Mia finally agreed and they started the game. It was exciting and they both laughed as they played. They kept score and soon it was Mia's turn to win. But when it came time to announce the winner, Mia said she didn't want to win! Mom was confused, but then Mia explained that she was happy for Mom to win this time. Mom was so touched that she gave Mia a big hug. They finished the game with both of them feeling fine.

Walter had been playing with his toys all day. He loved to build a stack of blocks and marvel at the tall tower he had built. Suddenly, his cat hopped on to the table and knocked the stack over. Walter was very upset. He started to tear up. His mom saw this and came over to help him. She hugged him tight and told him it was ok. She helped him to rebuild the stack and soon enough he was smiling again. His mom thought it was time for a snack and offered Walter a yummy apple. He happily accepted it and happily giggled as he enjoyed his treat. Walter had forgotten all about being upset. He was so excited when he saw his mom had managed to rebuild his stack and he started playing with it again. This time, making sure his cat didn't knock it over again!

"Mama, why do I have to take a test?" Little Timmy asked. His mother smiled and looked down at him. "Because it's important to know what you value. Tests help us understand that." Little Timmy looked around the room, feeling very confused and uncomfortable. Everything felt so unfamiliar, and he felt miserable. But he also knew his mother wouldn't have brought him here without a good reason. "But why do I have to value things?" he asked Mama again. Mama sighed and looked kind, despite the difficult question. "Value is important because it helps us know what things are important in life and what things are not. That way, we don't waste our time on things that don't matter." Little Timmy nodded his head. Though he was now feeling a little bit more confident, he was still nervous about taking the test. "It's OK to be scared," Mama said with a warm smile, "but it's also important to remember why you're here. Just remember what you value, and you'll do great." And, just like that, Little Timmy was ready for his test. With a determined look on his face, he remembered all the things he valued, and confidently walked forward, ready to start.

Yesterday, two young friends decided to join together. They each had a toy car and they wanted to have a race. So they joined the two cars together and started to make the moves of racing together. After a few minutes of racing, their cars joined together and the two young friends hugged each other in the middle of the room to celebrate the end of their race. They were very happy and enjoyed the race they had just had together.

A little girl was playing in her yard. She liked to run and play in the sunshine. One day while she was playing, she heard a loud noise. She was scared and she didn't know what to do. The little girl stayed still. Then, she saw her brother. He was wearing a brave face. He said, "Come on, let's go and see what the noise was." The little girl put on her favorite yellow blouse and was brave enough to follow her brother. They walked around the corner and saw a lot of people. All of them were clapping and yelling. In the middle of the crowd, was a circus! The little girl was so excited and happy. The brother and sister watched all of the shows together. They laughed, cheered, and even tried some of the tricks. At the end of the day, the little girl and her brother walked home, still wearing their brave faces.

Tommy was sick. He had a bad cough and a sore throat. His mom gave him some medicine to make him feel better. But Tommy did not like the medicine. It was bitter and yucky. He wanted to spit it out. "Tommy, you have to take your medicine," his mom said. "It will help you get well. Be a brave and honest boy." Tommy did not want to be brave or honest. He wanted to be happy and play. He looked at his mom and nodded. He opened his mouth and let his mom put the spoon in. But he did not swallow the medicine. He hid it in his cheek. "Good boy, Tommy," his mom said. "Now you can have some juice and a cookie." Tommy smiled and ran to the kitchen. He grabbed a glass of juice and a cookie. He was about to eat them when he felt the medicine in his cheek. It was still bitter and yucky. He wanted to get rid of it. He looked around. He saw his dog, Spot, lying on the floor. He had an idea. He bent down and whispered to Spot. "Spot, do you want some medicine? It is good for you. It will make you strong and healthy." Spot wagged his tail and licked Tommy's face. He thought Tommy was giving him a treat. He opened his mouth and Tommy spat the medicine into it. Spot swallowed the medicine and made a funny face. He did not like it either. Tommy laughed and gave Spot a hug. He thought he was clever and sneaky. He did not have to take the medicine anymore. He ate his cookie and drank his juice. He felt happy and proud. But then he heard his mom's voice. "Tommy, what did you do? Why did you give your medicine to Spot? That was not nice or honest. You have to take your medicine yourself. It is not for dogs. Spot might get sick too. Come here, Tommy. I have to give you another spoon of medicine." Tommy's smile faded. He felt guilty and scared. He realized he had done a bad thing. He wished he had been brave and honest. He wished he had taken his medicine the first time. He did not want to take it again. He did not want to make Spot sick. He did not want to make his mom angry. He looked at his mom and started to cry. He said he was sorry. He said he would take his medicine. He said he would never do it again. His mom hugged him and said she loved him. She said she was glad he was honest. She said she would forgive him. She said she would take Spot to the vet. She said she hoped he would feel better soon. She gave him another spoon of medicine. It was still bitter and yucky. But Tommy swallowed it. He did not spit it out. He did not hide it in his cheek. He did not give it to Spot. He managed to take his medicine. He was a brave and honest boy.

When they got home Bill put his hat away so that he wouldn't forget it the next time he went to the zoo. He wanted to make sure he could enjoy himself without forgetting anything again.

"I'm hungry," Ginny said as she hung from the big tree in the park. She could see a group of kids playing tag and she wanted to join them. But Ginny was waiting for her mom who had gone away for a little while. So instead, Ginny hung there, swinging and humming a little song. Suddenly, she felt a sharp pain in her arm. Ginny stopped swinging, looking around to see what it was that had caused the pain. She spotted a rare butterfly, hanging from a branch. Ginny smiled, forgetting the pain. She knew that seeing a rare butterfly must be an even better sign than joining a game of tag!

old, was running in the park. His mom was holding his hand, watching him and smiling happily. Suddenly, he stopped running and looked up at his mom. "Mommy, why are my legs so fragile?" he asked. His mom smiled and crouched next to him. "You know, Tommy, your legs are fragile because everyone's body is fragile. Even older people's bodies are fragile. That's why it's important to take care of it. That's why we have to be careful when we do things." Tommy nodded. "I understand, mommy. So I have to be careful when I play?" "Yes, that's right," his mom replied. "And I will remind you of it whenever you need it." Tommy smiled and ran off again with a newfound understanding. Suddenly, Johnny's hand burned and started to sting. The glowing insect had given him a nasty bite. Johnny started to cry. He was very sad that the smooth, shiny insect had hurt him. Yesterday afternoon, Mama and Daddy took Joe to the park. Joe played with the sand and got it all messy. He saw some little boys playing a game with a ball and asked Mama if he could borrow it. old boy who loved exploring. He had found a dirty piece of paper on the ground and wanted to share it with his best friend, Katie. Katie looked at the paper and smiled. Once they had finished, they jumped up and clapped their hands together in delight. "It looks great!" said Kevin. So off they went, Misha and Mom in the vehicle. It was a happy ride as they sang songs and watched the world go by. At the park, Misha played with her toy cars while Mom sat and watched with a content smile. They stayed until the sun started to set. On the journey back, Misha was so grateful for the fun day. A lady had a big apple tree in her yard. She liked to pick apples and make pies and juice. She was a good lady and shared her apples with her friends and neighbors. I can eat the bad bug and make it go away. Then your apples will be good again." The lady said, "Thank you, bird. You are a good friend. Please eat the bad bug and save my apples." The bird nodded and flew to the bad bug. It pecked the bad bug with its beak and ate it. The bad bug was gone. The lady clapped her hands and smiled. She picked the good apples and made pies and juice. She shared them with the bird and her other friends and neighbors. They all enjoyed the good apples and thanked the lady and the bird.

Her mom smiled and said, "Well, measuring things can be very helpful. Sometimes it's the best way to get things right." Lucy thought about it and said, "Okay, I guess that makes sense. I guess measuring things isn't so stupid after all." The mom nodded and said, "That's right. So, what else can you measure with your ruler?" Alya was very troubled. She had lost her favorite toy and she couldn't find it anywhere. She had looked under her bed, in her closet and even in the carpet. Nothing! A big lion lived in the forest. He was very strong and brave. He liked to hunt and roar. He did not like humans. He thought humans were weak and noisy. One day, he saw a thin human walking near his den. The human had a stick and a bag. The lion was hungry and angry. He wanted to eat the human. He sneaked behind a tree and waited. The human stopped and looked around. He saw a bird and pointed his stick at it. He wanted to catch the bird. He did not see the lion. The lion jumped out of the tree and roared. He ran towards the human. He wanted to scare the human and make him drop his stick and bag. But the human did not run away. He did not drop his stick and bag. He looked at the lion and shouted. He waved his stick and threw his bag at the lion. He dared the lion to come closer. The lion was surprised and confused. He did not expect the human to be so brave and loud. He did not like the stick and the bag. He stopped and growled. He did not want to fight the human. He wanted to find an easier prey. He turned around and ran away. He left the human alone. He did not want to see the human again. He learned that some humans were not weak and noisy. Some humans were strong and brave. Some humans dared to face a lion.
