Steve and Joe went up the steps together on that Sunday, and Joe showed Steve how to sit down and then slide down to the bottom. Steve loved it! He slid down the slide again and again, until a rude boy came up and pushed him aside. Steve was not happy. He started to cry, but Joe quickly came to the rescue. 'That's not very nice', Joe told the rude boy. 'You should always be kind to others. Now why don't you come down the slide with us?' The boy smiled and went down the slide with Steve and Joe. Wednesday was a calm day. All the animals in the forest were quiet and still. Even the birds weren't chirping. Suddenly, an elephant ignored the peace and trumpeted loudly. All the animals were startled and ran away. The elephant was so loud that the animals hid in their homes for the rest of the day. He was the loudest animal the forest had ever seen. But the elephant wanted someone to play with him. He tried asking the birds but they just flew away when they heard him. The elephant was sad. He wanted someone to pay attention to him, but nobody would come near. He just continued to trumpet louder and louder. Finally, after hours of shouting, a little fox peeked out from behind a tree. The fox was brave and decided to ignore the elephant's loud trumpeting. Instead, he quietly walked up to the elephant and they started playing together. They ran around the forest the whole day, until it was time for the fox to go home. The elephant was grateful that the fox chose to ignore his loud voice. From that day on, the little fox and the elephant were the best of friends.

They learned that something unknown can be a new companion and a teacher.

"It looks like a stage," said Alex. He was excited and curious. "Yes," said Mommy. "That is a stage. It is used for performances. Do you want to go see it?" Alex nodded his head and ran towards the stage. He put his hand on the doorknob and tried to open it. It was closed. "Let's try to open it together," said Mommy. Alex and Mommy both put their hands on the doorknob and closed it until it opened. They were both surprised to see that behind the stage was a costume closet with lots of different costumes. "Do you want to try one on?" asked Mommy. Alex's eyes grew wide with excitement. He quickly chose a clown costume and put it on. "Look at me!" said Alex proudly, twirling around in the costume. Mommy and Alex laughed and enjoyed the afternoon, exploring the stage and trying on all the costumes. It was a fun, but scary, adventure!

Yesterday, Mama and I went to the park. It was clean and sunny. We had fun! We saw a butterfly! Mama said we should play a game. She said I should throw a ball and try to break a tree! I held the soft ball in my hand. I threw it as hard as I could and it broke the tree! Mama was so surprised. She laughed and said, "I didn't think you could do it!" I was so proud. I knew I could break the tree! We had so much fun yesterday!

A little girl called Mia was very nervous. She was about to step out of her front door for the very first time. She had never seen the world outside. She slowly opened the door and stepped into the garden. Everywhere she looked she saw bright colours. The flowers were yellow, the grass was green and the sky was blue. Suddenly, Mia spots something amazing

a big rainbow in the sky! She giggles with happiness and steps closer to the rainbow. It is so beautiful! The rain starts to fall but Mia didn't mind. She steps through the rain, still staring at the rainbow. She loves it so much! Mia's mum calls her inside and she reluctantly steps back into the house. She can't wait to go out and play again soon.

Tommy was walking through the park holding his father's hand. Father pointed up to the sky and said, "Look at all these colours of the rainbow, Tommy!How beautiful." Tommy looked up and smiled, "Yes, daddy, so pretty!" Father noticed something in the distance, "Look what I found, Tommy." He pointed to a pile of lumber in the corner of the park. "Let's go pick some pieces up and make something special!" Tommy and his father ran to the lumber and began picking their pieces. Fathers chose the big ones while Tommy only picked the small ones. When they were done, they had a special wooden box. Father said, "Let's put something special inside it," and he pulled out a bag of sweet treats. Tommy's eyes lit up, "Yay! Sweets!" They put the treats inside the box and carried it home. Tommy was so proud of what they had made together, and whenever he missed his father he would take out the box to look inside. He was always reminded of how special their day in the park had been.

A little girl named Jane wanted to play with her big brother's toy, a lumber truck. She looked at it and wished it was hers. She was very jealous when he was playing with it. Her brother saw her looking and decided to let her borrow it for a while. He helped her push it around the floor. She was so happy and drove it around, making loud noises. Suddenly she heard a crash and the lumber truck was on its side. Her brother ran over to help her and set it upright again. She was sad that her truck was broken, but her brother helped her be brave. He gave her a hug and told her he was sorry. He then pushed it over to the toy box and they went outside to play. Jane was so happy that her brother showed her kindness and sharing.

Yesterday, my friends and I were playing a game. It was a mysterious game. We didn't know who would win. It was exciting! I was very happy when I won the game. My friends cheered for me! We were all so excited! Afterwards, I got a big treat. It was yummy and delicious. Then I went to bed and dreamed about winning the game a second time. I can't wait to play mysterious games again with my friends!

"Let's go, furry friend!" exclaimed John. His little girl, Olivia, skipped along after him, her bows bouncing in her hair. She was so happy to be able to take her beloved puppy for a walk. The sun was setting, so John knew it was the perfect time for a walk around the park. As they rounded the corner, Olivia saw something special. It was a loop. A big, colorful loop! Thrilled, she asked her dad, "Can I go on the loop?" John smiled, knowing he must permit her. He said, "OK, let's go. But be careful, alright?" He then looped Olivia's little hand in his and together they stepped onto the loop. Olivia was so excited that she couldn't keep her eyes open! She was getting sleepy, and as theywere just abut to get off the loop, she nearly dozed off. Luckily, John was there to catch her. He picked her up and said, "Let's head home. It's been a long day. Olivia yawned and smiled. She was so glad that her dad had permitted her to go on the loop!

Tommy was walking home from school when he heard a strange noise. His chest tightened, he felt scared and helpless. "What was that?" He asked. But no one was there. He was all alone. Suddenly, from behind a tall tree, a ghost appeared! The ghost said nothing but it's eyes seemed to remind Tommy of an old, scary story he had heard. He gasped and turned to run, but he felt so scared, so helpless, he just stood there shaking. "Don't be scared, Tommy," the ghost said. "I'm here to give you a message." Tommy wasn't sure what to do. The ghost continued: "If you ever forget this message, dreadful things will happen!" Tommy felt a cold chill run down his spine. Tommy never forgot the message and tried to do the things the ghost told him to. But the ghost still haunted Tommy, reminding him at every turn. In the end, the ghost's warnings meant nothing and Tommy was left feeling helpless and scared.

"Come on, Lucy!" shouted Mommy. "Let's go to the park!" Lucy was so excited. She loved the park, especially the slides. The warm sun was shining and soon they arrived. Lucy ran to the tallest slide first. She climbed up the slide and got ready to go. "No running, Lucy!" Mommy said in a bossy voice. "You have to be careful going down the slide." Lucy agreed but said she wanted to go fast. Mommy laughed and told her that she could slide fast, as long as she stayed safe. Lucy smiled and said, "Ok Mommy, I promise!" Then, she zoomed down the slide and laughed out loud.

A mom and her daughter were walking in the park. The daughter looked at the sky and said, "Mom, what is that fluffy thing?" The mom said, "Those are clouds, sweetie." The daughter looked around and said, "Mom, what is that big thing with numbers?" The Mom smiled and said, "That's a calendar. It helps us keep track of the days." The daughter said, "Wow, that looks cool!" She went up to the calendar and gave it a big hug. But then she made a disgusted face. She looked up to her mom and said, "Mom, this calendar is disgusting!" The mom laughed and said, "No, it's not disgusting. It's just dirty. Most calendars are like this." She wiped the calendar with her hand. The daughter smiled and said, "Thanks, Mom. Now I can give it a big hug again!"

Two friends, Tom and Sarah, were walking in the park. Tom saw a fountain and said, "Sarah, let's join the fountain!" Sarah was excited and said, "Yes!" They ran over to the fountain and saw all the different colors. Tom said,"Wow, this fountain is so pretty!" Sarah said, "I know, let's get some cheap coins to put in it." Tom said,"Ok, I'll go get some coins." Tom ran to the store and soon came back with the coins. Sarah and Tom each had a few coins in their hands and they joined together at the fountain. Sarah said, "Ready? On the count of three..." They both smiled and said together, "One, two, three!" They both threw their coins into the fountain and watched them sparkle as they hit the water. Tom and Sarah laughed and gave each other a big hug. "Let's come back here every day," said Sarah. "Yes, said Tom, "It's always fun to join the fountain!"

"Mommy! Look!" shouted Benny excitedly, holding up a plush toy. It was old, with a soft velvet touch. His mom smiled. "It's lovely," she said. Benny stared at it, shaking it gently from side to side. "I'm going to take good care of it," he said quietly. His mom touched his shoulder. "I'm sure you will," she said. A few weeks later, Benny was playing with his toy in the garden when a gust of wind blew it onto the grass. He rushed over to pick it up. To his surprise, the toy shook in his hands. Benny shook it some more, and soon heard a faint sound coming from inside. His mom, who had been working in the garden, came over with a curious look on her face. "What have you found?" she asked. Benny grinned. "It's a surprise!" he said, shaking the velvet toy harder. Suddenly, a little bird fluttered out of the toy and flew away into the sky. Benny and his mom watched in awe, smiling. "You never know what you'll find," said his mom with a wink.

Yesterday, Mommy, Daddy, and a little girl all went for a walk. Daddy brought his kite. Mommy and Daddy were walking, and holding the kite, when all of a sudden the wind blew very hard. They weren't careful and it flew away. Mommy and Daddy were so sad and the little girl started to cry. Then, Daddy had an idea. He told the little girl to lie down and close her eyes. He said it was a game. He and Mommy ran away, like the kite was flying. The little girl was very quiet and still. When Mommy and Daddy came back, they were laughing. They had the kite! They told the little girl that their secret was that they had been careless, but it all worked out in the end. The little girl was happy and the family continued on their walk. Together, they watched the kite fly away in the wind.

"Come on, let's go swimming," said mom to her daughter. "Yes!" said the daughter, excitedly running to get her swimsuit. Mom and the daughter put on their swimsuits and went to the beach. There were many people already swimming and playing in the shallow water. The daughter wanted to swim deeper and noticed that a group of fierce fish were swimming far out in the ocean. The fish were playing a game of chess! She was amazed by the sight and wanted to join, so she grabbed a board and swam towards them. The fish welcomed her warmly and allowed her to join the game. She played fiercely and with much concentration. When the sun began to set, mom called the daughter back. The daughter thanked the fish for their kindness, swam back to shore and ran back to mom, with stories of the chess playing fish.

Yesterday, there was a powerful disturbance in the park. Tom and his dad were there, and Tom was scared. 'What is that, Dad?' he asked. His dad smiled and said, 'That's just some thunder, Tom. It is powerful, but it won't hurt us.' Tom was still worried. He could hear the thunder rumble in the sky above. Suddenly, a huge flash of light filled the sky. Tom shouted, 'What's that Dad!'. His Dad laughed and said, 'That's just lightning, Tom. It's powerful, but it won't disturb us.' Tom felt better, but he still kept his eyes on the sky. He knew that powerful storms like this could be dangerous and he wanted to make sure they were safe.

"Look at the copper," said Grandma. The shiny metal sparkled brightly in the sun. Mommy and Grandma went out to find the copper, but it was hidden very well. "We have to be patient," said Mommy. The two of them looked and looked, but the copper was still nowhere to be seen. Finally, after a very long time, Grandma acted and suddenly the copper was in her hand. "I found it!" Grandma said with a smile. Mommy smiled too, she had been so patient, and now the copper was found. The two of them went back home and Grandma put the copper in a special place so it would always be safe.

Tommy was very curious about everything. He liked to ask questions and learn new things. Sometimes he asked too many questions and his mom and dad got tired. But Tommy was persistent. He wanted to know more and more. One day, Tommy went to the doctor with his mom. He had hurt his arm when he fell from his bike. The doctor said he needed an x

boo," he said. "Yes, Tommy, you can see your bones. They are white because they are hard and strong. But one of them has a fracture. That means it is broken. That's why your arm hurts. But don't worry, the doctor will fix it. He will put a cast on your arm. It will help your bone heal," his mom said. "A cast? What is a cast?" Tommy asked. "A cast is a bandage that wraps around your arm. It is hard and colorful. You can choose the color you like. It will protect your bone and keep it in place. You will have to wear it for a few weeks. Then the doctor will take it off and your arm will be fine," his mom said. "Wow, a cast sounds cool. Can I choose blue? Blue is my favorite color. Can I draw on it? Can I show it to my friends?" Tommy asked. "Yes, you can choose blue. Yes, you can draw on it. Yes, you can show it to your friends. But you have to be careful. You can't get it wet or dirty. You can't scratch it or hit it. You have to follow the doctor's rules. Then your arm will heal faster," his mom said. "OK, mom, I will. I'm sorry I hurt my arm. But I'm glad I saw my bones. They are amazing. Thank you, doctor, for the x

ray. It is a very useful tool. It helps us see what we can't see with our eyes. It helps us diagnose and treat injuries and illnesses. It helps us keep people healthy and happy," the doctor said. Tommy smiled. He learned something new. He saw something amazing. He got something cool. He was happy. He wondered what else he could learn and see and get. He was persistent. He wanted to know more and more.

"Let's play a game, Dave!" said Mom. "Yes, Mommy!" said Dave. Mom pulled out a dictionary. "This is a dictionary. You can use it to solve unknown words," said Mom. Dave smiled and opened the dictionary. "Let's see what we can find!" He flipped through the pages, looking for an unknown word. He stopped and pointed to a word. "This one!" he said. "Very good, Dave!" said Mom. "Can you try to solve it?" Dave thought for a few seconds, then said "Blossom!" Mom praised, "That's right!" Dave was so proud he solved the unknown word. Mom smiled and said "Let's find some more words now!"

Welly was a very stubborn kid. Most people knew that if he wanted to do something, he would. One day, Welly was playing outside when he noticed something strange in the tree. He went to investigate and saw a loose screw dangling from the trunk. Welly didn't know what it was, but he knew he had to have it. He tried to pull the screw out of the tree, but it wouldn't budge. No matter how hard he pulled, the screw wouldn't come out. He finally shouted: "I will not resist." That's when Welly's father appeared. He told Welly that the loose screw was an important part of the tree's structure and if it was removed, the tree wouldn't be as comfortable. He asked Welly if he would please leave the screw alone. Welly thought for a while, but he eventually decided to leave the screw alone. He knew that if he removed the screw, it could have ended up badly for the tree. If the tree became uncomfortable, Welly wouldn't be too happy about it. Welly was very proud of himself for resisting the urge to remove the loose screw. He thought about it for a long time, but then decided to leave it be. He was better off for it, and the tree was too.

old girl in excitement. She watched as the dancer, wearing her favourite sparkly dress, moved gracefully across the stage. Mommy watched the performance with pride, knowing the dancer was her daughter. "Yes, slipping is part of dancing. It is quite difficult to do but thankfully she has done it right this time," mommy said encouragingly. The young girl watched in awe as the dancer sped up, making leaps and jumps across the stage. But then suddenly, the dancer slipped and fell. The little girl felt uncomfortable and went over to the dancer. But before she reached the dancer, mommy was already there, offering a helping hand. "It's ok honey. Everyone slips sometimes, but you have to keep going no matter what," mommy said. Mommy helped the dancer up and the performance continued. The dancer was back to her graceful and confident movements. The little girl was so proud of her, she smiled and clapped as the performance ended.

Uri and Mommy went to the store. It was exciting! Uri looked around, but didn't know what he wanted. Mommy said, "Let's look at the menu." Uri said, "What's that?" Mommy said, "It's a list of things that we can buy." Uri looked around again. He saw some toys and said, "Can I get one?" Mommy said, "Let's take a look at the menu and see what we can pay for." Uri looked at the menu. He saw a toy car and said, "I want that!" Mommy said, "Let's pay for it. But remember, if it gets hurt, we won't be able to buy another one." Uri nodded and said, "Okay." They paid for the car and went home. Uri played with his new car all day and was very careful not to hurt it!

'Once upon a time there lived a generous giant. Each day the giant went out wearing his mask. It made him feel protected from the world. One day he decided to take a journey. He looked far and wide and discovered an exciting new land. It was so different from his home, the giant decided to stay there for a long time. But eventually the giant got homesick. He wanted to return to his beloved home and the people he loved. The mask the giant had been wearing became a symbol of his journey. It was a reminder to the giant of all his wonderful travels. Before he left, the generous giant gave the mask to one of his new friends. He wanted them to remember him by. The giant then said goodbye to his new friends and waved as he set off on his journey home. The giant arrived back at home in no time. He was so happy to see his family and friends, who had missed him dearly. They were pleased to see him safe and sound and the generous giant stayed home for many years. He was so glad he'd returned!'

When a monkey named Bongo looked down, he saw a pebble. He wanted to own it. So, he reached out and picked it up. He felt the bumps and knew it was a special pebble. It was hairy! Bongo decided to take the pebble home to his family. He wanted everyone to see it. So, he held it tightly in his hand and ran all the way. His family was excited to see the pebble. They laughed and smiled when they saw it! Everyone insisted that Bongo should keep the pebble for himself. He hugged it and smiled with joy. From now on, Bongo always kept the pebble with him. He was very proud to own such a special and hairy pebble!

A crane was eager to unpack. It knew the job would be fun. The crane spread out its wings and flapped until it was high in the sky. From here, it had a great view of the boxes it was going to unpack. Each box was packed so tightly with toys, clothes and books. The crane had to be careful. The crane moved one of the boxes with its beak and placed it carefully on the ground. Then, it rummaged through the box and began to unpack. It took out a teddy bear and a doll, a block and a truck. The crane worked quickly, but also carefully. Soon, everything was unpacked. The crane was proud of its work. It had unpacked all the boxes and the toys were ready to be used.

once upon a time there was a person who loved to clean. Every day they would clean the floor and the walls and the windows. One day they finally had the whole house sparkly clean. This made one of their friends very jealous. The jealous person wanted to have a house that was as clean as theirs. So they decided to watch the person who loved to clean and try to learn how to clean the way they did. Every day, the jealous person tried to clean the way their friend did, and slowly but surely their house was starting to look as clean. In the end, both the person who loved to clean, and their jealous friend, had beautiful, clean houses.

"Let's prepare a motorcycle!" said Mommy. Daddy got out a toolbox and looked at the motorcycle. He said, "This motorcycle looks very attractive!" Mommy agreed. She said, "We'll need to put the pieces together. Can you help Daddy?" The little boy nodded and went outside to help Daddy. He handed Daddy pieces of the motorcycle, and Daddy put them all together. After a few minutes, the motorcycle was ready. It looked shiny and new. Daddy put on a helmet and got on the motorcycle. He said, "Look, it's ready! Would you like to take a ride?" The little boy was so excited. He got on the back of the motorcycle and held on tight. The sun was shining brightly and the wind was blowing in their hair as they drove off. What an adventure!

Tuesday was here. It was a hot day, and Billie was restless. She wanted to go out and play, but she had to stay home. Billie was sad. She looked out of the window and saw a bird hopping in the garden. It was so bright and colourful. Billie pressed her nose to the window, watching the bird fly around. Mom saw Billie at the window and said, "Let's go outside, Billie. It's a beautiful day." Billie smiled and ran outside. She ran around in the grass, feeling the sun on her skin. She chased the bird and giggled as the bird flew away. Then, Billie lay down in the grass, staring up at the blue sky and the white clouds. Soon, it was time to go inside. Tuesday was gone and Billie was content.

"Look, a boat!" said Jake, pointing to the sea. Mum smiled. "Yes, it's sailing. Shall we go and see?" The two of them put on their hats and they sailed over to the boat. It was an old boat and it had a big secret. When they reached the boat, they saw a friendly dog. He was helpful and he showed them where the secret was. Mum and Jake opened the secret box and found lots of treasure. They were so excited they shouted loudly. The helpful dog smiled and returned to his boat. "Bye!" he said. Mum and Jake waved goodbye as the old boat sailed away. They had a great day and learnt a secret.

Zach was bouncing around the living room when his grandpa walked in. "Where are you going in such a hurry, Zach?" "I'm gonna zoom past the kitchen and the dining room," Zach said. Grandpa laughed and said, "Let me help you." Grandpa grabbed a label and stuck it on a thin box. He said, "Now this box must stay inside the house. Do you understand?" "Yes! I will make sure to only zoom around the living room," Zach said with a smile. Grandpa thanked him and left the room. Zach continued to zoom around the living room, careful not to go beyond the box with the thin label.

"Are you ready to go?" asked Max's Mom. "Yes!" answered Max. Max and his Mom were going to visit the lab. Max was excited. He knew the lab was important. When they got to the lab, Max was amazed! He saw lots of big machines inside the building. He saw people in white coats running around. Max's Mom talked to a scientist. She told him that Max was to be part of an important experiment. Max felt excited and scared all at the same time. The scientist said that he would show Max what to do. She showed Max a big screen with lots of numbers on it. Max loved it! At the end, the scientist smiled and said, "You did a great job Max. The experiment was a success!" Max and his Mom thanked the scientist and went home feeling very happy. Max knew he had an important job at the lab.

When she woke up, Sarah was so tired she just wanted to stay in bed. Instead, she had to pack for her trip. She got out of bed and grabbed her suitcase. She wanted to make sure she remembered to pack her most important things. "Mommy, what should I pack?" Sarah asked her. "Well, let's see. You need to pack your clothes, some snacks, and of course your special toy," said Mommy. Sarah was very excited. She knew it was important to pack her toy because it always made her feel safe. Both Sarah and her toy had come through a lot of special adventures. Sarah packed her things and put her toy in a special pocket of her suitcase. She zipped up the pocket and headed out the door, but she couldn't help but feel a little nervous. She knew it would be a long trip but she also knew her toy would keep her safe. From then on, she felt much more relaxed and, eventually, even a little excited. Even though Sarah was tired, she was ready for the trip. She smiled as she said good

"Come on, let's go outside!" said Mama. Mama and her son, Tom, went outside into the yard. There they saw a big tree with lots of leaves. Tom looked at the task set before him and started to giggle. "What's so funny?" asked Mama. Tom pointed to the tree. "I want to tear the leaves off the tree," he said. Mama smiled. "That's a lively task, Tom," she said. Tom eagerly started to tear off the leaves. He ripped them off the tree one by one until it was all bare. Tom stepped back to take a look at his work. Mama put her hand on his shoulder. "Good job, Tom!" she said. Tom smiled. He was so happy that he finished the task.

Tommy was walking around the park one day when he saw a shiny object in the grass. He bent down and picked it up and realised it was a diamond! He looked around to see where it had come from, but there was nobody nearby. He was sure this was a rare diamond, so he started to run towards his house. Along the way he asked everyone he saw if the diamond belonged to them. Nobody had ever seen it before. When Tommy got home, he showed his mum the diamond. She was so surprised to see it! She explained that diamonds are very rare, and that Tommy should always ask if something does not belong to him. Tommy was very happy about his find, and his mum was proud of him for asking around to see if anyone owned it. From then on, Tommy remembered to ask if he saw something he did not recognise.

Abbie had an important mission. She wanted to find a symbol. She looked in all the special places she knew, like under the bed and in the cupboard, but she couldn't find anything. Abbie was feeling frustrated. Just then, her mum came in. She saw Abbie looking sad and came over to talk to her. Abbie told her about her mission, and mum suggested that Abbie put the little toys that she had been playing with together in different ways, and see if she could make a symbol out of them. Abbie was excited. She loved playing with the toys, and arranging them quickly created a symbol that looked special. She was so proud of herself, and thanked mum for the great idea. Abbie was persistent in looking for the symbol, and her determination paid off in the end. It took some time, but she managed to find it, and she celebrated with a big smile.

Young Robert loved to explore and was very clever. One day he decided to visit the beach and see what he could find. He went walking along the shore, looking carefully. Suddenly, he spotted something appearing from the water. It was a big, green turtle! Robert was so excited and wanted to touch it, so he moved closer. The turtle seemed quite friendly and allowed Robert to pet its hard shell. Robert thought it was so cool and thanked the turtle for appearing. After a few minutes, the turtle disappeared back into the water, leaving Robert with a huge smile on his face. Robert went back home and told all his family about his magical meeting with the turtle. He was so proud of his clever adventure and the wonderful creature he found.

"Mama, what did you do today?" asked Alice. Mama smiled as she replied, "I opened the door and went to work. It was a mild day outside." Alice looked up at Mama with wide eyes, "What do you do at work?" she asked. Mama said, "I help people buy stuff. And I help them with their problems." Alice nodded thoughtfully. Then she smiled and said, "So you open the door, go to work and help people, and it's all mild?" Mama chuckled, "Yes! That's right." Alice was so proud that she knew what Mama did every day. She ran to the door and opened it wide, then ran back to Mama and hugged her. "You're the best Mama ever," said Alice. Mama smiled, hugged her daughter and whispered, "I love you, Alice."

Walter was playing in the park. His favourite game was to scatter stones across the grass. He would run around in circles throwing them up in the air. Then he went to the pond. Steam was rising up from the water. It was thick and white. Walter was fascinated. He wanted to see where the steam was coming from. So he jumped right in and shouted "Whee". His little splash created lots more steam and clouds of it filled the air. Walter laughed with delight. He enjoyed his cool adventure!

A lion was feeling very grumpy. He was hungry and wanted something to eat. He roared out loud looking for food. Just then a waffle fell from the sky. It was the perfect meal for the lion. On the waffle was written a message. It said "Be stubborn". The lion couldn't believe his eyes. He thought about what the message meant for a long time. He decided that he should be strong and brave and not give up. The lion roared loudly and with confidence. He quickly ate the waffle. He felt full and happy now that he followed the message. He was proud of himself for being so stubborn.

Two friends, Toby the bear and Sally the cat, were arguing. Toby wanted to play with his blocks while Sally wanted to color. "No! I want to play with my blocks!" shouted Toby. Sally was patient and said, "Let's both do something together. We can make a train with the blocks and color it!" Toby thought about it, and soon both friends were busy creating their train. Toby was patient and listened to Sally's ideas, and the result was better than they could have imagined. The train looked bright and colorful, and they were both excited to play with it. Their quarrel was forgotten and the two friends had a great time playing with the train.

"Let's go!" Mary said to her mom. Mary wanted to play outside, and she couldn't wait any longer. Her mom shook her head. "We have to delay, Mary," she said. "It isn't safe outside yet." Mary frowned and pouted. She stomped her weak little feet, but nothing happened. Her mom smiled and hugged her. "We'll go when I say it's safe out there," she said. Mary kept looking out the window, impatient for the day when she could go outside. After what felt like an eternity, her mom finally said it was safe. She and Mary ran out of the house, happy and excited. They had waited a long time, but it was worth it! Finally, they were free.

once upon a time there was a little girl. She was three years old and very creative. She had a dictionary of her own in her bedroom and she liked to read it. One day the little girl wanted to make her dictionary even more creative. She decided to pour paint on it. She looked in all the colors and chose the green paint. She took the paint and poured it carefully on all the pages of her dictionary. Once she finished, she put the dictionary aside to let it dry. When it was dry, the little girl opened the dictionary and looked at all the beautiful colors. Her dictionary had become much more creative. She was very pleased. The little girl had made a masterpiece of her own. She was so proud and she knew that her dictionary was the most creative dictionary in the world.

"Mommy, what is prayer?" asked Thomas, a three year old boy, while looking up at his mommy. "Prayer is when we talk to God and ask him to help us," his mommy said kindly. "Do you have something you want to pray for?" Thomas nodded. "I want to pray for some paper!" he said excitedly. His mommy laughed. "Do you need it for something special?" she asked. "Yeah!" said Thomas, jumping in the air. "I want to make something rich!" His mommy smiled. She said a prayer with Thomas, and asked God to help Thomas make something beautiful out of the paper he needed. When they finished praying, Thomas hugged his mommy tight. With a grateful heart, he skipped happily out of the room, ready to get to work on his project.

Tommy was walking around his backyard one day when he saw something on the ground. He bent down and saw that it was a big sun. It was so hot that he could feel the heat coming from it. He decided to take a bite out of it. He couldn't believe how sweet it tasted. He started to chew and chew until it was all gone. Tommy went back inside after his delicious snack. She decided to take the teaspoon home and put it away for safe keeping. The girl and her puppy continued their walk but every once in a while she noticed her faithful pup stopping to sniff the spoon in his pocket. The girl knew that the spoon was safe in her pup's pocket and smiled. She was so happy to have a dependable pup by her side.

A plane was flying in the sky. The sky was icy and the plane was high in the clouds. The plane flew around and around, counting as it flew. It saw one, two, three and four. A bird flew close and the plane flew a bit higher. It kept on counting until it reached ten. When the plane was done counting, it made a big circle in the sky. The icy sky sparkled in the sun. The plane flew until it couldn't see the sky anymore. Finally, the plane said goodbye and disappeared.

A girl named Max was very gifted. She was only three, but she knew lots of things! Her mom was always encouraging Max to use her gifts. One day, Mom asked Max to help her. She needed to attach something to the refrigerator. Max was excited to help. She dragged a chair to the refrigerator and climbed up on it. Max used her small fingers to attach the object to the refrigerator. Mom was very impressed with Max! She smiled and gave Max a big hug. Max was glad she was gifted. She had a fun day helping mom with the refrigerator.

Yuliana was a young girl who loved to play with her friends. One day she decided to try and fly like the birds she had seen in the sky. She looked up and with a huge leap she tried to take off, but instead she fell. She was sure that if she kept trying she'd be able to fly, but she needed help. Her best friend, Jack, saw what happened and came over to help. He said: "Yuliana, I can show you how to fly. All you need to do is trust me and have time. It will take a while, but you can do it." Yuliana was so excited! She said: "I trust you, Jack! I'm ready and I'm willing to take my time. How long do you think it will take?" Jack smiled, and said: "It's not going to be easy, but I think it could take a long time until you get the hang of it. Are you ready to give it a go?" Yuliana said: "Yes! Let's go!" And with that, Yuliana and Jack started their journey, determined to master how to fly.

"Mommy, can I please go to the backyard?" asked Danny. He had been looking out the window at the ancient backyard. "Yes, you can go," Mommy said. Danny smiled and ran out to the backyard. He ran and ran until he reached the backyard. What he saw made him gasp. In the middle of the backyard was an ancient tree. It had been there for ages! Danny walked up to it and put his hand on the trunk. He felt the ancientness of the tree beneath his hand. He closed his eyes and said, "Please, ancient tree, show me your magic." Suddenly, the tree started to glow! Danny opened his eyes in disbelief. He was amazed! He stayed there for a while and then finally went back inside. He knew that he had just seen something truly magical.

Tommy was a very curious 3 year old. He wanted to get a big surprise for his mom. He knew his mom liked jackets, so he searched around for the perfect one. He found a nice one at the store that was pink and had polka dots. It was very flexible too. Tommy took the jacket to the checkout and the clerk sorted it out for him. He paid the clerk and then went to the park to give it to his mom. When his mom saw the jacket she was so happy! It was her favorite color and the polka dots made it special. She put it on and said it was the most flexible jacket she had ever seen. Tommy was glad he was able to give his mom the surprise. She said she was going to wear it all the time! Tommy was so happy he made his mom so happy.

"Let's go bathe!" shouted Jack. He was feeling very jolly, and his smile lit up the room. His mom nodded, and she followed Jack to the bathroom. Inside, the cell was warm and cozy. Jack rushed to take off his clothes. "You need to take those off first," his mom said gently. Jack understood, and he smiled widely before quickly undressing. He stepped inside the cell and the warm water touched his skin. "Ah, this feels nice!" Jack exclaimed. Mom laughed and watched Jack enjoy his bath. When the bath was over, Jack's mom helped wrap him in a towel. Jack felt freshly cleaned and relaxed. He smiled, thanked his mom, and ran out of the bathroom, ready to go play.

Tommy was walking very slow in the garden. He saw a little bug on his knee. He smiled and bent down to look at it. He wanted to pick it up, but it moved away. He tried to move faster but it still moved away. Then he heard a noise. It was like something had snapped. He looked around and saw a naughty rabbit. The rabbit was eating some carrots in the garden. Tommy got angry and tried to catch it. He ran as fast as he could but the rabbit was too fast. Tommy felt frustrated. He wanted to catch the rabbit but it was too quick. He sat down on the grass and thought about what to do. Suddenly he had an idea. He stood up and raised his knee high in the air. He snapped his knee down suddenly and the rabbit jumped. Tommy caught the naughty rabbit and held it tightly in his hands. He laughed and ran back home with the rabbit in his hands.

A brother and sister wanted to go outside to play. The brother wanted to bring his ball. But the sister wanted to take her doll. The sister insisted on bringing her doll and the brother insisted on bringing his ball. Their mom knew it could be a problem so she made a plan. They could take both! But the brother was confused. He didn't understand why they could take two toys. The sister explained that they could each have something special to play with. The brother agreed and they ran inside to grab their toys. Soon they were outside playing together with a ball and a doll. They were so happy that they both had something fun to play with. The brother smiled and the sister laughed. They had a great day together!

Tommy was playing with his toy. He loved the toy but he could tell that his parents were not interested in it. They were busy talking and ignored Tommy. He felt a little sad but kept on playing. Suddenly, he heard a scary noise. He looked around but couldn't find the noise. He tried to ignore it, but it kept getting louder. Tommy got very scared and dropped his toy. He ran to his parents to show them the noise and make it stop. But they were still ignoring him. He tried to get their attention but they wouldn't listen. Finally he gave up. Tommy was very scared but he had to ignore the noise and find his toy by himself.

"Once upon a time there was a clever girl named Wendy. One day she had a cool idea. She decided to take a bike ride around the park. So Wendy hopped on her bike and started to pedal. She pedalled and pedalled until she came to a stop. Suddenly, she heard a strange noise coming from the bushes. She wondered what it could be! Wendy got off her bike and went to look. It was a puppy! Wendy thought it was a great idea to take the puppy with her. So she put the puppy in her bicycle basket and continued her ride. Then, when it was time to go home, Wendy stopped again. She didn't want the puppy to run away. So Wendy thought of a cool idea. She put a collar on the puppy and a tag with her name on it. Now the puppy belonged to her! And that is the story of how Wendy found her puppy. The end!"

Tommy was hungry. He wanted a waffle for breakfast. He asked his mom to make him a waffle. His mom said, "Okay, but you have to wait a little bit. I have to finish some work first." Tommy was restless. He did not want to wait. He looked at the clock. It was very slow. He looked at the waffle maker. It was very quiet. He looked at his mom. She was very busy. He felt very bored. He decided to make his own waffle. He climbed on a chair and reached for the waffle maker. He opened it and saw a hot plate. He thought it was a waffle. He grabbed it with his hand. He screamed. It was very hot. It hurt his hand. His mom heard him scream. She ran to him and saw what he did. She was very scared. She took him to the sink and put his hand under cold water. She said, "Tommy, what did you do? You should never touch the waffle maker. It is very dangerous. You could burn yourself or start a fire. You have to listen to me and wait patiently. I love you and I want you to be safe." Tommy felt very sorry. He cried and hugged his mom. He said, "I'm sorry, mom. I was hungry and restless. I wanted a waffle. I did not listen to you. I was very silly. I love you too and I want you to be happy." His mom smiled and kissed his hand. She said, "It's okay, Tommy. I forgive you. You made a mistake, but you learned from it. Next time, you will be more careful and respectful. Now, let me make you a waffle. It will be yummy and warm." Tommy smiled and nodded. He waited patiently for his waffle. He learned that he should not touch things that are hot or dangerous. He learned that he should listen to his mom and wait for his turn. He learned that he should be grateful for his mom and her love. He enjoyed his waffle and thanked his mom. He was happy.

Yesterday, there was an ordinary little bear who lived in the forest. The bear loved to play with his friends and climb trees. But one day, a big scary wolf came to the forest. The wolf wanted to hurt the little bear and his friends. The little bear knew he had to protect his friends. So he roared as loud as he could and stood in front of his friends. The wolf was surprised and ran away. The little bear felt proud that he could protect his friends. From that day on, the little bear knew that even though he was ordinary, he could do extraordinary things to help his friends.

"Come on, let's try it," said Mark to his friend Joe. The two were standing outside a big cage. "But it looks so tough," said Joe. "Don't worry, I know what I'm doing," Mark said. He grabbed the door and rattled it. "See, it's not so bad. You just have to try it." Joe took a deep breath and then stepped inside the cage. He looked around anxiously. Finally, Joe made it to the other side of the cage. He let out a big sigh of relief. "See, that wasn't so tough," said Mark. Joe nodded and smiled. He felt proud of himself for trying.

Tommy was feeling very anxious as he drove with his mom in the car. His mom kept looking back, with a worried expression. Finally, his mom said to him, "I'm sorry, Tommy, but the car isn't working as it should. We need to take it to the mechanic." Tommy felt really anxious as he looked out the window. He had a feeling that they were going to regret going to the mechanic. They finally arrived at the mechanic and everything seemed to be going well. The mechanic looked under the hood and said, "I'm sorry, there's nothing I can do for you. The damage is too bad." Tommy felt a deep regret as he looked back at his mom. She could barely look at him. She slowly said, "I'm sorry, Tommy. I had a feeling it would end this way." The look of regret in his mom's eyes told him that it was time to go home.

"Look at the forest," said Mommy. "Let's take a walk." Jimmy was excited and said, "Yay!" He put on his regular shoes and grabbed his regular sweater and ran outside to see the forest. On the way, Mommy said, "Jimmy, look closely at the forest. You'll see some really cool things! Can you guess what they are?" Jimmy thought for a moment and said, "No, Mommy. I don't know what's there. What is it?" Mommy smiled. "Well, if you look closely, you can see lots of animals in the forest. Can you spot them?" Jimmy looked around and saw birds and rabbits hopping around the trees. He clapped his hands and said, "Wow! This is so cool! I can see the animals! Thank you, Mommy!" Mommy had foreshadowed their exciting discovery in the forest and they were both rewarded with a beautiful view of nature. A regular walk in the forest had been turned into a special adventure.

Once there was a little boy. He loved to make things. One day, he decided to make a jog. First, he put on his warm coat and his mittens, for the weather outside was icy cold. Then, he stepped outside. He started to jog up and down the sidewalk. He was careful not to slip on the icy surface. Pretty soon, the little boy was feeling very happy and warm. His heart was pounding and he was breathing hard from the jog. Finally, he made it to the end of the street. He was so happy that he had run the whole way! From then on, whenever the weather was cold, the little boy would make a jog and feel warm and happy all over again.

Tommy was anxious. He did not like to go to the barber. The barber had big scissors and a loud machine that buzzed his hair. Tommy wanted to keep his hair long and curly. But his mom said he had to go to the barber today. She said his hair was too messy and dirty. Tommy and his mom walked to the barber shop. Tommy saw other kids sitting in big chairs. They had capes around their necks and wet hair. The barber was cutting their hair with scissors and the machine. Tommy felt scared. He did not want to sit in the big chair. He did not want the barber to touch his hair. His mom talked to the barber. She said Tommy needed a shampoo and a trim. The barber smiled and said okay. He took Tommy to a sink. He put a towel around Tommy's neck and wet his hair. He squeezed some shampoo on Tommy's head. He rubbed it in. It felt funny. Tommy did not like it. He tried to move his head away. The shampoo got in his eyes. It stung. Tommy cried. He wanted to go home. The barber rinsed the shampoo out of Tommy's hair. He said sorry. He said he was almost done. He took Tommy to the big chair. He put a cape around Tommy's neck. He picked up the scissors. Tommy felt more scared. He did not want the scissors near his hair. He shook his head. He said no. He said stop. The barber put down the scissors. He said okay. He said he would use the machine instead. He turned it on. It made a loud buzzing sound. Tommy felt more scared. He did not want the machine near his hair. He screamed. He said no. He said stop. He kicked his legs. He tried to get out of the chair. The barber turned off the machine. He said okay. He said he would not cut Tommy's hair. He said Tommy could go. He took off the cape and the towel. He gave Tommy a lollipop. He said sorry. He said he hoped Tommy would come back another day. Tommy's mom was embarrassed. She said sorry to the barber. She said sorry to the other kids and their moms. She said Tommy was just nervous. She said he would be better next time. She took Tommy's hand and the lollipop. She walked out of the barber shop. Tommy was happy. He had his hair and his lollipop. He did not have to go to the barber again. He licked his lollipop. He smiled.

A dog and its owner were walking in the park when the dog saw a squirrel. The dog wanted to poke the squirrel to make it run away, but the owner said "No," because the dog might scare it too much. The dog was sad and didn't understand why. Then the owner explained why it shouldn't poke the squirrel. He said that it wasn't nice to get in the way of animals in their own homes, even if it was for fun. The dog felt bad for being selfish and decided to leave the squirrel alone. The owner was very happy with the dog for understanding and he gave the dog a big hug. From then on, the dog was always very careful when playing in the park and never tried to poke anything again.

once upon a time there was a very crazy reindeer. He was always running and jumping around the forest. Every day was a new adventure for him. One day the crazy reindeer came across a river. He wanted to cross it, but he did not know how. He tried running, but he just kept slipping into the river. He suddenly saw a little bird and asked, "Can you help me?" The bird said, "I can split the river in two so you can cross, but only if you help me." The crazy reindeer agreed and the bird started flapping its wings. As it did so, the river split in two and the reindeer was able to cross. He thanked the bird and continued on his way. The end.

"Good morning, kitty," said Sally as she awoke from her bed and noticed the small white tabbycat sleeping in her window sill. The yard was full of vibrant colors and Sally could feel the warm sunshine on her face. Suddenly, she spotted something silly jumping around the yard. It was her neighbor, Jack, wearing a crazy suit made of flowers! He was laughing and shouting, his arms and legs bouncing up and down. "Hi Jack!" said Sally. Jack looked up and grinned. "Hi Sally!" he said. "Look what I'm doing. I'm springing!" Sally opened her mouth wide in amazement. She had never seen anything so crazy. With each jump, Jack seemed to soar higher and higher. He flew around the garden, giggling and smiling. Then all of a sudden, he hopped onto the garden wall and sprang into the sky, disappearing into the horizon. Sally waved goodbye and watched him until he was out of sight. Then she went back inside, filled with a wonderful feeling inside.

Tommy was very excited. He was getting a present! Someone was sending it to him. It was going to be a model! It would be perfect! Tommy waited. He was so excited that he could hardly sit still. He wanted to see the model. He wanted to play with it right away! At last the model arrived. It was better than he could have imagined. There were tiny animals and trees and boats. Everything was perfect. Tommy played with the model all day. He made the animals run around and the boats went on the lakes. He was so happy to have a perfect model!

Alice and Jack were best friends. They played together all the time, sharing games and toys. One day they both found the same furry cap and they wanted it for themselves. They started to quarrel about who should keep it. Each wanted to keep it more than the other. Alice said, "I want the cap. I saw it first". But Jack said, "No, I want it." They argued some more. Suddenly, their mama came into the room. She said, "I can fix this problem. I'll give you both a different cap. Then you can both be happy." Alice and Jack smiled. They hugged each other and put on their new caps. Now they were both happy and could play together.

Zoe was a loyal little girl with a big heart. Whenever one of her friends was feeling sad, she was always there to make them feel better. Her favourite activity was looking for crystals in the park. She would count how many crystals she could find and leave a few behind for her friends. One day, Zoe was playing in the park and found something special. It was the most beautiful crystal she had ever seen. She quickly picked it up and brought it to her mum. "What a special crystal! Can I keep it, mum?" asked Zoe. "Yes, because you have been so loyal," answered her mum with a smile. So Zoe took the crystal into her bedroom and placed it next to her bed. Every night she lay there and would count how many facets the crystal had. It was strangely calming and Zoe was so pleased that she had the crystal. Whenever she felt alone or sad, the crystal seemed to make her feel happy. It was the most loyal companion she had ever had.

old Sam excitedly. Sam and his grandpa were going to plan an adventure. Sam grabbed his cane and tapped the ground as he eagerly waited for his grandpa to get ready. Finally, grandpa was ready. "I'm ready, let's go!" he said. Sam and grandpa went outside. The air was bitter and cold, but that didn't stop them. Grandpa knew exactly where they were going. He led Sam down the street and across the park. "Where are we going?" asked Sam. Grandpa smiled. "We are going to get some sweets from the sweet shop." Sam's eyes lit up. He loved sweets! "Let's go!" he said with a happy smile. As soon as they arrived at the sweet shop, Sam and grandpa gathered up the treats and went off to plan the biggest adventure ever!

"Once upon a time there was a little girl named June. June was a very adventurous girl. One day, June went into the garden to play. While she was playing, she happened to receive a very special stick. It was a long stick, with lots of colourful stripes around it. June was so excited about her new stick, she decided to go explore the hills with it. She held the stick tightly as she ran up the hills and looked around. She could see so many places she wanted to visit! However, as soon as she stopped to take a rest at the top of the hill, her stick began to fly in the air! The wind had caught it and it was flying too high for June to reach. June was very sad, but luckily a friendly, blue bird came to help her. The bird flew up to the top of the hill and brought her stick back down to her. June was so relieved and thanked the bird very much. From that day on, June was always sure to receive her adventurous stick with her wherever she went! The end.

Tommy was sick. He had a hot head and a sore throat. He did not want to eat or play. He only wanted to sleep. Mommy was worried. She wanted to check how hot Tommy was. She had a thermometer. It was a stick that could tell how hot or cold something was. She put it in Tommy's mouth and waited. Tommy did not like the thermometer. He spit it out. He said, "No, Mommy, no! I don't want it!" He hid under the blanket. Mommy insisted. She said, "Tommy, you have to let me see the thermometer. It will help me make you feel better. Please, Tommy, please." Tommy shook his head. He said, "No, Mommy, no! You are nosy. You always want to know everything. Leave me alone!" Mommy sighed. She said, "Tommy, I'm not nosy. I'm your mommy. I love you and I care about you. The thermometer is not bad. It will not hurt you. It will only take a minute. Then you can go back to sleep." Tommy looked at Mommy. He saw her sad face. He felt sorry. He said, "Okay, Mommy, okay. I will let you see the thermometer. But only for a minute. And then you have to give me a hug and a kiss." Mommy smiled. She said, "Thank you, Tommy, thank you. You are a good boy. I will give you a hug and a kiss. And I will also give you some juice and some medicine. They will make you feel better too." She put the thermometer in Tommy's mouth again. She waited. She looked at the thermometer. She said, "Tommy, you have a fever. You are very hot. You need to rest and drink a lot of water. I will stay with you and read you a story. Do you want to hear a story?" Tommy nodded. He said, "Yes, Mommy, yes. I want to hear a story. But not a nosy story. A nice story." Mommy laughed. She said, "Okay, Tommy, okay. I will tell you a nice story. A story about a brave boy who fought a dragon. Do you like dragons?" Tommy smiled. He said, "Yes, Mommy, yes. I like dragons. They are cool. But not as cool as you." Mommy hugged him. She said, "I love you, Tommy. You are my sweet boy. Now, let's hear the story."

"Where's my game?" asked Billy, a 3 year old. Billy's mom smiled. "It's over there. Are you ready to play?" Billy ran to the box of games and opened it. Inside was a game just like he wanted. He was so excited and grabbed the game to play. But then, something strange happened. Mom said, "I'm sorry, Billy, but we have to delay the game. We need to clean up first." Billy was very disappointed. He had been so looking forward to playing his game. But he knew Mom was right and agreed to clean up first. He slowly swept and put away the toys. The truck driver got out of the truck. He opened the back of the truck. He saw Sam and True inside the truck. He was angry and shocked. He called the police. The police came and took Sam and True away. They were in big trouble. They had to go to the hospital. They had to go to the court. They had to go to their parents. They were very sorry. They had learned a hard lesson. They had learned not to follow strangers. They had learned to listen to their friends. They had learned to be careful and safe.

She bit the fruit and felt a sharp pain. The fruit was not a fruit. It was a trap. A hunter had put it there to catch zebras. Zara was stuck and scared. She cried for help. The lion heard Zara's cry and jumped out of the grass. He was ready to pounce on her. But then he saw the hunter coming out of the bushes. The hunter had a gun and a net. He wanted to catch the lion too. The lion was scared and ran away. Zara's mom and dad heard Zara's cry and ran to the tree. They saw the hunter and the trap. They kicked the trap and freed Zara. They hugged her and licked her wounds. They told her to never run away again. Zara was sorry and learned her lesson. She stayed with her herd and was happy.

He thought they looked like prunes, so he tried to find some that matched the shape of the clouds. After searching for a while, he found a big yellow prune. He was so pleased when he found one that perfectly matched the shape of the cloud. He shouted for joy as he held it up for everyone to see. Then he quickly ate it and kept looking for more. Soon, he found lots of yellow prunes and showed them to everyone he saw. He was so proud that he had found the perfect match for the cloud. They all laughed and clapped as Tommy pointed to the sky, proudly showing everyone the perfect yellow prune.

"Look Mama, look!" an excited three year old shouted. Mama squatted down to investigate what had gotten the child so jolly. In the little one's hand was a bright jewel. "It's so pretty!" The child exclaimed. Mama smiled and said, "Yes, it is! Where did you find it?" The child's eyes sparkled with happiness as she pointed to the floor and said, "I wiped it up from the ground". Mama looked around in surprise. She couldn't believe her little one had found such a special find. She took the jewel from the child's hand and said, "I think you should keep it." The little one smiled and hugged her mama, so happy with her new treasure. She wiped it and held it close to her heart. The little one skipped away, so jolly with her new jewel. Mama watched as the little one skipped away, safe with her newfound treasure in her hand.

once upon a time there was a little girl. She had a kite. She went outside to fly it. The wind was strong. She was scared, but she held on to the kite. It flew higher and higher until she couldn't see it in the sky. The little girl was very happy. She wanted her mom to see. She shouted to her mom, "Come and see my kite!" Mom came outside. She saw the kite flying so high and smiled. She said, "That kite is really nice. I recommend you fly it more!" The little girl was so happy. She thanked her mom and told her she would fly her kite more. She was no longer scared of the wind.

"Mom, what's that?" asked the 3 year old, as she pointed to a box in the corner of the room. "That's a box," said her mom. "Let's open it, shall we?" The 3 year old nodded and watched as her mom unlocked the box, revealing a delicious sandwich. "That looks so yummy, can I eat it?" asked the 3 year old. "Of course, but why don't you take it outside," suggested her mom, gesturing to the sunny garden. So the 3 year old grabbed the sandwich and ran outside, feeling shy but excited. She ate her sandwich in the sunshine and when she finished, she went back inside with a smile on her face.

Walter was a little boy. He was three years old. He was very happy. Today, Walter was in his bedroom. He had a favorite toy. It was a purple ball. It was very hard. Walter stood up. He held the purple ball. He held it in his hands. Walter loved the purple ball very much! Walter stood very still. He was concentrating. He wanted to see how long he could stand with the purple ball. At last, Walter could stand for a long time with the purple ball. He was so happy! He laughed and danced around with the purple ball. It was a wonderful day!

Tonight, Mary was very glad. She was going to take a bath in the big bathtub! She put on her favourite bath dress and went to the bathroom. She was so excited to get in the bathtub! Mary climbed into the warm bathtub and put all her bath toys in the water, too. She loved splashing around and playing with her toys. After a while, she started to feel sleepy so she lay down and let the water soak her. She felt so cozy in the bathtub! When Mary got out of the bath, she was feeling happy and refreshed. She was so glad she had taken her bath! Mary put on her warm pyjamas and went to bed. She had had a wonderful day.

From then on, the furniture was a lot less grumpy. It still moved around the house in reverse, but it always had a happy dance in its step."

once upon a time, there was a puppy. He was walking around the park, looking at all the different things. Suddenly, he saw a little girl. She had a big smile on her face and was running around, playing games. The puppy was so confused, he just sat and watched her. The little girl saw the puppy and came over to him. She said "Hello puppy! What are you doing here?" The puppy just looked at her, confused. The little girl said "Do you want to play with me?". The puppy still did not know what to do, so he just continued to look confused. The little girl laughed and said "It's okay, puppy. Come here and I'll show you how to play." The puppy was happy to have someone to play with, so he ran over to her. Together, they had so much fun! The puppy was never confused again, and they became good friends and played together almost every day.

"Look at these chewing gum!" Mom said. Little Lou was excited. He smiled and grabbed the chewing gum. He said, "Yum! I'm gonna chew it!" Mom nodded. Suddenly, there was an emergency siren. Mom said, "Oh no, we have to go." Little Lou was sad. He said, "Can I take the chewing gum?" Mom shook her head and laughed. She said, "That's a funny idea. Come, let's go." Little Lou and Mom ran out of the house. Little Lou looked back, and he saw the chewing gum still lying there. He said, "Bye, chewing gum!"

Two friends, Jack and Emma, had been living together since they were babies. Over the years, they became best friends and did almost everything together. One day, Emma said, "Oh wow, we have been great friends for one whole year. Let's celebrate!" Jack was surprised and replied, "Wow, really? We have been living together for one brilliant year! That's amazing!" To celebrate, the two friends decided to make a special trip to their secret spot in the woods. It was there that they could always come and be together and gain energy from one another's friendship. On their way back home, Jack said to Emma, "Can you believe it? One whole brilliant year!" Emma smiled, happy to share such a great friendship. The two friends hugged each other to celebrate the great anniversary they had gained.

"Mike, count the socks," called his mom. Mike was impatient. He wanted to play with his toys. He didn't want to count socks. But then he looked at the colorful socks. He noticed there was one red sock and one green sock. He started counting. "One, two!" he said. "Mom, I'm done!" His mom smiled. "Good job, Mike!" she said. "Let's put them away now." Mike was very happy. He had finished counting the socks quickly and was now free to play.

Anna and Ben are excited to help Mom bake a cake. They put on their aprons and wash their hands. Mom gives them a big bowl and a spoon. She tells them to kneel on the chairs so they can reach the table. "First, we need to measure the flour," Mom says. She shows them how to use a cup and a spoon to scoop and level the flour. Anna and Ben take turns to fill the cup and pour it into the bowl. They count how many cups they need. "One, two, three, four," they say. "Next, we need to measure the sugar," Mom says. She gives them another cup and a spoon. Anna and Ben do the same as before, but with the sugar. They count how many cups they need. "One, two," they say. "Then, we need to measure the butter," Mom says. She gives them a knife and a stick of butter. She shows them how to cut the butter into small pieces. Anna and Ben use the knife carefully to slice the butter. They count how many pieces they need. "One, two, three, four, five, six," they say. "Now, we need to measure the eggs," Mom says. She gives them a bowl and a fork. She shows them how to crack the eggs and beat them with the fork. Anna and Ben each crack an egg and put it in the bowl. They use the fork to mix the eggs. They count how many eggs they need. "One, two," they say. "Good job, Anna and Ben," Mom says. "You are very good at measuring. Now, we need to mix everything together and put it in the pan. Then, we can bake the cake and eat it later. Are you ready?" "Yes, Mom," Anna and Ben say. "We are ready. We love to bake with you. We love cake." They smile and hug Mom. They are very happy and excited.

Yesterday, Mommy and Daddy had a big surprise. Mommy locked the door and told the kids to close their eyes. When they opened them again, their uncle was standing in the room. The kids were so excited! They hugged their uncle and asked lots of questions. But Daddy said they had to be quiet and sit still, or they'd be naughty. So the kids did their best to listen and be good. Uncle then showed them lots of toys and games. They played until it was time to go, and before they left, Uncle gave them all a hug and a kiss. When it was time for bed, Mommy remembered the surprise and remembered to lock the door. Daddy said goodnight and gave the kids a big hug. The kids were so happy yesterday! They had lots of fun and were very good. Tomorrow, the kids can't wait to see what surprise Mommy and Daddy have for them!
